# Teal design system - full documentation

Version: v0.5.2
---

# Getting started

Teal provides typed React modules, semantic design tokens, and tested interaction behavior for Kryv applications.

## Principles

- **Quiet by default** - Surface, type, and spacing create hierarchy. Color is reserved for action and meaning.

- **Keyboard complete** - Every interactive module has visible focus and a complete keyboard path.

- **One supported interface** - Applications import typed modules and compiled styles from @kryv/teal.

- **Recipes before abstractions** - Product patterns remain recipes until repeated behavior proves a stable module seam.

## Installation

### 1. Install the package

React 18 or 19 is required as a peer dependency.

```bash
npm install @kryv/teal
```

```bash
pnpm add @kryv/teal
```

```bash
yarn add @kryv/teal
```

```bash
bun add @kryv/teal
```

### 2. Import the styles

Import the compiled component styles once at your app entry. Teal modules do not require Tailwind in the consuming application.

```js
import '@kryv/teal/styles.css'
```

### 3. Optionally apply document defaults

base.css applies Teal typography, body colors, selection, and scrollbar defaults. Skip it when the application already owns document-level styling.

```js
import '@kryv/teal/base.css'
```

### 4. Optionally configure Tailwind 3

Use the preset only when application markup needs Teal semantic utilities such as bg-teal-surface-container or text-teal-on-surface-variant.

```js
import tealPreset from '@kryv/teal/tailwind-preset'

/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
export default {
  ...tealPreset,
  content: ['./index.html', './src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'],
}
```

### 5. Load the fonts

Teal typesets headlines in Plus Jakarta Sans and body copy in Manrope. Add the Google Fonts links to your document head.

```html
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
<link
  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Manrope:wght@400;500;600;700;800&family=Plus+Jakarta+Sans:wght@500;600;700;800&display=swap"
  rel="stylesheet"
/>
```

### 6. Enable dark mode

Tokens switch themes when the dark class is present on the html element. Persist the choice however your app prefers.

```js
// Teal themes by toggling the "dark" class on <html>.
document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', darkMode)
```

### 7. Build something

```jsx
import { Button, Field, Input } from '@kryv/teal'

export function SignInForm() {
  return (
    <form className="grid gap-4">
      <Field label="Email" required>
        <Input type="email" />
      </Field>
      <Button type="submit">Sign in</Button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

---

# Foundations

Semantic tokens keep visual decisions consistent across themes and products.

## Color

Use semantic roles instead of raw palette values.

- **Primary** - `--teal-color-primary`
- **Success** - `--teal-color-tertiary`
- **Warning** - `--teal-color-warning`
- **Danger** - `--teal-color-error`
- **Surface** - `--teal-color-surface-container`
- **Elevated surface** - `--teal-color-surface-container-high`

## Typography

- **Plus Jakarta Sans** - `--teal-font-headline`
- **Manrope** - `--teal-font-body`

## Shape, elevation, and motion

- Controls use 12 to 16 pixel radii.
- Surfaces use soft teal elevation.
- Motion stays between 150 and 200 milliseconds and respects reduced motion.

## Visual tokens

Override these supported CSS properties at `:root` to tune Teal without rewriting module styles.

- **Control radius** - `--teal-radius-control`
- **Surface radius** - `--teal-radius-surface`
- **Pill radius** - `--teal-radius-pill`
- **Subtle border** - `--teal-border-subtle`
- **Strong border** - `--teal-border-strong`
- **Focus ring** - `--teal-focus-ring`
- **Raised elevation** - `--teal-shadow-raised`
- **Overlay elevation** - `--teal-shadow-overlay`
- **Extra-small icon** - `--teal-icon-xs`
- **Small icon** - `--teal-icon-sm`
- **Medium icon** - `--teal-icon-md`
- **Large icon** - `--teal-icon-lg`
- **Extra-large icon** - `--teal-icon-xl`
- **Fast motion** - `--teal-motion-fast`
- **Standard motion** - `--teal-motion-standard`

---

# Button

Actions with consistent hierarchy, sizing, loading, and accessible icon treatment.

## Usage

```js
import { Button, IconButton } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>
<IconButton label="More options"><MoreHorizontal /></IconButton>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A user needs to take an explicit action.
### Avoid when

The control is only communicating status or navigation.
### Behavior

Loading disables the native button until the action completes.
### Responsive

Let actions wrap in narrow toolbars instead of shrinking their labels.

## Examples

### Variants and sizes

Primary, secondary, ghost, and danger variants with a dedicated IconButton for icon-only actions.

```jsx
import { Button, IconButton } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Search, Share2 } from 'lucide-react'

export function ButtonDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
          <Button disabled>Publish</Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" disabled>
            Duplicate
          </Button>
          <IconButton label="Share" disabled>
            <Share2 />
          </IconButton>
        </div>
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Publishing unlocks once an editor approves the draft.</p>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <>
      <Button size="sm">Small</Button>
      <Button>Primary</Button>
      <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button>
      <Button variant="ghost">Ghost</Button>
      <Button variant="danger">Danger</Button>
      <Button loading>Saving</Button>
      <IconButton label="Search">
        <Search />
      </IconButton>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Disabled actions

Use disabled state when the action cannot be completed yet, and explain why nearby.

```jsx
import { Button, IconButton } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Search, Share2 } from 'lucide-react'

export function ButtonDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-2">
        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
          <Button disabled>Publish</Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" disabled>
            Duplicate
          </Button>
          <IconButton label="Share" disabled>
            <Share2 />
          </IconButton>
        </div>
        <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Publishing unlocks once an editor approves the draft.</p>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <>
      <Button size="sm">Small</Button>
      <Button>Primary</Button>
      <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button>
      <Button variant="ghost">Ghost</Button>
      <Button variant="danger">Danger</Button>
      <Button loading>Saving</Button>
      <IconButton label="Search">
        <Search />
      </IconButton>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Label** - The visible text naming the action; required unless the button is icon-only.
- **Icon** - An optional leading or trailing glyph that supports the label, hidden from assistive technology.
- **Spinner** - Replaces the content while loading and keeps the button disabled until the action settles.
- **IconButton** - The icon-only variant; its label prop becomes the aria-label and the tooltip text.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use one primary button per view so the main action is unambiguous.
- Write verb-led labels that say what happens, like "Save changes".
- Use IconButton with a descriptive label for icon-only actions.

### Don't

- Don't use a button for navigation; use a Link instead.
- Don't rely on the danger color alone; keep the destructive label explicit.
- Don't disable a button without explaining why nearby.

## Interface

### Button

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| null` | `"primary"` | Visual hierarchy of the action. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| null` | `"md"` | Height and horizontal padding. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Merges the component onto its child element instead of rendering the default element (Radix Slot). Cannot be combined with disabled or loading. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the button, prepends a spinner, and sets aria-busy. |

### IconButton

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` | - | Accessible label applied as `aria-label`; also used as the default tooltip text. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Replaces the icon with a spinner and disables the button while true. |
| `variant` | `"danger" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| null` | `"ghost"` | Visual treatment of the icon button. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| null` | `"md"` | Hit-target size; the icon scales with it. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to and from the button. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Activates the button. |

- Icon-only actions use IconButton, which requires a label applied as aria-label and mirrored in the title tooltip.
- Loading buttons set aria-busy and are disabled so they cannot be activated twice.
- A loading IconButton replaces its icon with a spinner while keeping the accessible label.
- The danger variant carries meaning through its label as well as its color.

## Related modules

- [Link](/modules/link)
- [Button Group](/modules/button-group)
- [Toolbar](/modules/toolbar)
- [Split Button](/modules/split-button)

# Button Group

An attached cluster of related actions with hairline seams and shared corner radius.

## Usage

```js
import { ButtonGroup, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button variant="secondary">Day</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Week</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Month</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Two to four tightly related actions belong to one decision.
### Avoid when

The actions are unrelated or need distinct visual priority; space them normally.
### Behavior

Seams collapse to hairlines and only the outer corners keep their radius.
### Responsive

Let the cluster wrap or switch to vertical orientation on narrow screens.

## Examples

### Attached actions

Buttons butt together with shared seams; vertical stacks work too.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, ButtonGroup, Toggle } from '@kryv/teal'

const rangeOptions = [
  { id: 'day', label: 'Day' },
  { id: 'week', label: 'Week' },
  { id: 'month', label: 'Month' },
]

export function ButtonGroupDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [range, setRange] = useState('week')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <ButtonGroup orientation="vertical">
        <Button variant="secondary">Project settings</Button>
        <Button variant="secondary">Members</Button>
        <Button variant="secondary">Danger zone</Button>
      </ButtonGroup>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-2">
      <ButtonGroup aria-label="Date range">
        {rangeOptions.map((option) => (
          <Toggle
            key={option.id}
            pressed={range === option.id}
            onPressedChange={() => setRange(option.id)}
          >
            {option.label}
          </Toggle>
        ))}
      </ButtonGroup>
      <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
        The selected option pops with an accent fill. For single-select toolbars with a sliding
        indicator, see the ToggleGroup segmented variant.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Vertical cluster

Use vertical orientation when the actions stack in a narrow panel.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, ButtonGroup, Toggle } from '@kryv/teal'

const rangeOptions = [
  { id: 'day', label: 'Day' },
  { id: 'week', label: 'Week' },
  { id: 'month', label: 'Month' },
]

export function ButtonGroupDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [range, setRange] = useState('week')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <ButtonGroup orientation="vertical">
        <Button variant="secondary">Project settings</Button>
        <Button variant="secondary">Members</Button>
        <Button variant="secondary">Danger zone</Button>
      </ButtonGroup>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-2">
      <ButtonGroup aria-label="Date range">
        {rangeOptions.map((option) => (
          <Toggle
            key={option.id}
            pressed={range === option.id}
            onPressedChange={() => setRange(option.id)}
          >
            {option.label}
          </Toggle>
        ))}
      </ButtonGroup>
      <p className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
        The selected option pops with an accent fill. For single-select toolbars with a sliding
        indicator, see the ToggleGroup segmented variant.
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Buttons** - Two to four sibling Buttons rendered flush against each other.
- **Seams** - Hairline borders between buttons that replace the usual gap.
- **Shared radius** - Only the first and last buttons keep their outer corner rounding.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use for closely related options of equal weight, like Day / Week / Month.
- Keep labels to one word so the cluster stays compact.
- Switch to the vertical orientation in narrow side panels.

### Don't

- Don't mix variants inside a group; the cluster reads as one control.
- Don't group unrelated actions just to save space.
- Don't exceed four buttons; use a Menu for larger sets.

## Interface

### ButtonGroup

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `enum` | `horizontal` | Stack direction of the attached buttons. |

## Accessibility

- Each button in the group keeps its own focus stop and accessible name; the group itself adds no keyboard behavior.
- Buttons butt together visually but remain separate controls, so screen readers announce each action individually.
- Disabled buttons keep their native semantics and are skipped in the tab order.

## Related modules

- [Button](/modules/button)
- [Toggle Group](/modules/toggle-group)
- [Toolbar](/modules/toolbar)

# Toggle Group

A cluster of Toggle-styled options with roving focus, in mutually exclusive single mode or independent multiple mode; variant="segmented" renders an options array with a sliding selection pill.

## Usage

```js
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<ToggleGroup type="single" defaultValue="left" aria-label="Text alignment">
  <ToggleGroupItem value="left">Left</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="center">Center</ToggleGroupItem>
  <ToggleGroupItem value="right">Right</ToggleGroupItem>
</ToggleGroup>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Two to five related options need quick on/off switching, such as alignment or formatting controls.
### Avoid when

Options need explanatory text or there are many of them; use RadioGroup or Checkbox with variant="card", or Select instead.
### Behavior

Single mode keeps exactly one item checked and reports the new value; multiple mode reports the full array of pressed values. Disabled items leave the focus order and cannot be toggled.
### Responsive

Items wrap to the next line when the group outgrows its container.

## Examples

### Single selection

type="single" behaves like a radio group: one item stays checked at a time.

```jsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from '@kryv/teal'
import { AlignCenter, AlignLeft, AlignRight, Bold, CalendarDays, Italic, KanbanSquare, List, Underline } from 'lucide-react'

export function ToggleGroupDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <ToggleGroup type="multiple" defaultValue={['bold']} aria-label="Text formatting">
          <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold">
            <Bold />
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic">
            <Italic />
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="underline" aria-label="Underline">
            <Underline />
          </ToggleGroupItem>
        </ToggleGroup>
        <ToggleGroup type="single" defaultValue="week" aria-label="Report range">
          <ToggleGroupItem value="day" size="sm">
            Day
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="week" size="sm">
            Week
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="month" size="sm">
            Month
          </ToggleGroupItem>
        </ToggleGroup>
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <ToggleGroup
        type="single"
        variant="segmented"
        aria-label="Project view"
        defaultValue="board"
        options={[
          { value: 'list', label: 'List', icon: <List /> },
          { value: 'board', label: 'Board', icon: <KanbanSquare /> },
          { value: 'calendar', label: 'Calendar', icon: <CalendarDays />, disabled: true },
        ]}
      />
    )
  }

  return (
    <ToggleGroup type="single" defaultValue="left" aria-label="Text alignment">
      <ToggleGroupItem value="left" aria-label="Align left">
        <AlignLeft />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="center" aria-label="Align center">
        <AlignCenter />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="right" aria-label="Align right">
        <AlignRight />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  )
}
```

### Multiple selection

type="multiple" lets any combination of items stay pressed, plus a compact sm size.

```jsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from '@kryv/teal'
import { AlignCenter, AlignLeft, AlignRight, Bold, CalendarDays, Italic, KanbanSquare, List, Underline } from 'lucide-react'

    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <ToggleGroup type="multiple" defaultValue={['bold']} aria-label="Text formatting">
          <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold">
            <Bold />
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic">
            <Italic />
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="underline" aria-label="Underline">
            <Underline />
          </ToggleGroupItem>
        </ToggleGroup>
        <ToggleGroup type="single" defaultValue="week" aria-label="Report range">
          <ToggleGroupItem value="day" size="sm">
            Day
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="week" size="sm">
            Week
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="month" size="sm">
            Month
          </ToggleGroupItem>
        </ToggleGroup>
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <ToggleGroup
        type="single"
        variant="segmented"
        aria-label="Project view"
        defaultValue="board"
        options={[
          { value: 'list', label: 'List', icon: <List /> },
          { value: 'board', label: 'Board', icon: <KanbanSquare /> },
          { value: 'calendar', label: 'Calendar', icon: <CalendarDays />, disabled: true },
        ]}
      />
    )
  }

  return (
    <ToggleGroup type="single" defaultValue="left" aria-label="Text alignment">
      <ToggleGroupItem value="left" aria-label="Align left">
        <AlignLeft />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="center" aria-label="Align center">
        <AlignCenter />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="right" aria-label="Align right">
        <AlignRight />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  )
}
```

### Segmented options

variant="segmented" renders an options array on a pill track; a measured pill slides behind the active option.

```jsx
import { ToggleGroup, ToggleGroupItem } from '@kryv/teal'
import { AlignCenter, AlignLeft, AlignRight, Bold, CalendarDays, Italic, KanbanSquare, List, Underline } from 'lucide-react'

export function ToggleGroupDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <ToggleGroup type="multiple" defaultValue={['bold']} aria-label="Text formatting">
          <ToggleGroupItem value="bold" aria-label="Bold">
            <Bold />
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="italic" aria-label="Italic">
            <Italic />
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="underline" aria-label="Underline">
            <Underline />
          </ToggleGroupItem>
        </ToggleGroup>
        <ToggleGroup type="single" defaultValue="week" aria-label="Report range">
          <ToggleGroupItem value="day" size="sm">
            Day
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="week" size="sm">
            Week
          </ToggleGroupItem>
          <ToggleGroupItem value="month" size="sm">
            Month
          </ToggleGroupItem>
        </ToggleGroup>
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <ToggleGroup
        type="single"
        variant="segmented"
        aria-label="Project view"
        defaultValue="board"
        options={[
          { value: 'list', label: 'List', icon: <List /> },
          { value: 'board', label: 'Board', icon: <KanbanSquare /> },
          { value: 'calendar', label: 'Calendar', icon: <CalendarDays />, disabled: true },
        ]}
      />
    )
  }

  return (
    <ToggleGroup type="single" defaultValue="left" aria-label="Text alignment">
      <ToggleGroupItem value="left" aria-label="Align left">
        <AlignLeft />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="center" aria-label="Align center">
        <AlignCenter />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="right" aria-label="Align right">
        <AlignRight />
      </ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Group** - A roving-focus container that needs an accessible name, usually through aria-label.
- **Item** - A Toggle-styled option; single mode exposes aria-checked, multiple mode aria-pressed.
- **Size variant** - The sm size for compact toolbars.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Name the group with aria-label, since items are often icon-only.
- Use type=single for mutually exclusive modes like text alignment.
- Keep groups to two to five items so every option stays visible.

### Don't

- Don't use it for settings that need explanatory text; use RadioGroup or Checkbox with variant="card".
- Don't use it to submit form choices; it is a control cluster, not a fieldset.

## Interface

### ToggleGroup

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | - | - |
| `variant` | `enum` | `default` | `segmented` renders `options` on a pill track with a sliding indicator (single-select). |
| `options` | `ToggleGroupOption[]` | - | Convenience options rendered by the segmented variant instead of children. |
| `size` | `enum` | `md` | Density of the segmented variant. |

### ToggleGroupItem

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `enum` | `md` | Control size. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | - | - |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the group's current item. |
| `Arrow Left` + `Arrow Right` | Moves focus between items without changing the selection. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Toggles the focused item. |

- Single mode exposes radio semantics (aria-checked); multiple mode exposes toggle buttons (aria-pressed).
- The group needs an accessible name, usually through aria-label.
- With variant="segmented" the sliding selection pill is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

## Related modules

- [Toggle](/modules/toggle)
- [Radio Group](/modules/radio-group)

# Link

Themed inline and standalone links with an external indicator.

## Usage

```js
import { Link } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Link href="/projects">View projects</Link>
<Link href="#" external>Status page</Link>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Navigation happens inline in prose or as a lightweight standalone action.
### Avoid when

The affordance performs an action; use Button instead.
### Behavior

External links open a new tab with rel="noreferrer" and an indicator icon.
### Responsive

Let inline links wrap naturally with their surrounding text.

## Examples

### Inline and external

Inline links underline within prose; external links open a new tab with an icon.

```jsx
import { Link } from '@kryv/teal'

export function LinkDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Link href="#" variant="standalone">
        View all projects
      </Link>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <Link href="#" external>
        System status
      </Link>
    )
  }

  return (
    <p className="max-w-md text-sm">
      Your workspace is shared with the design team. <Link href="#">Manage access</Link> to change who
      can see this project.
    </p>
  )
}
```

### Standalone navigation

Use the standalone variant outside prose, where underline-on-hover signals the affordance.

```jsx
import { Link } from '@kryv/teal'

export function LinkDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Link href="#" variant="standalone">
        View all projects
      </Link>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <Link href="#" external>
        System status
      </Link>
    )
  }

  return (
    <p className="max-w-md text-sm">
      Your workspace is shared with the design team. <Link href="#">Manage access</Link> to change who
      can see this project.
    </p>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Anchor text** - The underlined link text, inline within prose or standalone.
- **External indicator** - The icon appended to links that open a new tab, paired with rel="noreferrer".

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use links for navigation, even when the destination opens in a new tab.
- Use the external prop for off-site links so the new-tab behavior is signposted.
- Write link text that makes sense out of context, not "click here".

### Don't

- Don't use a link to perform an action like saving or deleting; use a Button.
- Don't wrap whole sentences or paragraphs in a link.

## Interface

### Link

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | `false` | Composes the link styles onto a single child element instead of rendering an anchor. |
| `external` | `boolean` | `false` | Opens the link in a new tab with `rel="noreferrer"` and appends an external-link indicator. |
| `variant` | `"inline" \| "standalone" \| null` | - | - |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to and from the link. |
| `Enter` | Follows the link. |

- Renders a native anchor, so screen readers announce it as a link and browser link behaviors work.
- External links open in a new tab with rel="noreferrer"; the indicator icon is decorative, so pair the text with wording that makes the destination clear.

## Related modules

- [Button](/modules/button)
- [Breadcrumb](/modules/breadcrumb)
- [Skip Link](/modules/skip-link)

# Toggle

A pressed-state button for binary preferences in toolbars and filter rows.

## Usage

```js
import { Toggle } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Toggle aria-label="Bold"><Bold /></Toggle>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A preference flips between two states inside a toolbar or filter row.
### Avoid when

The choice needs a label with explanation; use Switch or Checkbox.
### Behavior

aria-pressed reflects the value and the pressed tint follows.
### Responsive

Keep toggle content icon-sized so rows stay compact.

## Examples

### Pressed state

aria-pressed and data-state reflect the current value; tint follows.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Toggle } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Bold, Italic, List, Underline } from 'lucide-react'

export function ToggleDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [formats, setFormats] = useState({ bold: true, italic: false, underline: false })
  const [filters, setFilters] = useState({ starred: false, archived: false })

  const toggleFormat = (key) => setFormats((current) => ({ ...current, [key]: !current[key] }))
  const toggleFilter = (key) => setFilters((current) => ({ ...current, [key]: !current[key] }))

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
        <Toggle size="sm" pressed={filters.starred} onPressedChange={() => toggleFilter('starred')}>
          Starred
        </Toggle>
        <Toggle size="sm" pressed={filters.archived} onPressedChange={() => toggleFilter('archived')}>
          Archived
        </Toggle>
        <Toggle size="sm" disabled>
          Locked
        </Toggle>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
      <Toggle aria-label="Bold" pressed={formats.bold} onPressedChange={() => toggleFormat('bold')}>
        <Bold aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />
      </Toggle>
      <Toggle aria-label="Italic" pressed={formats.italic} onPressedChange={() => toggleFormat('italic')}>
        <Italic aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />
      </Toggle>
      <Toggle aria-label="Underline" pressed={formats.underline} onPressedChange={() => toggleFormat('underline')}>
        <Underline aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />
      </Toggle>
      <Toggle aria-label="Bulleted list">
        <List aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />
        List
      </Toggle>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Filter rows

Use toggles in a toolbar for independent on/off preferences.

```jsx

  const [filters, setFilters] = useState({ starred: false, archived: false })

  const toggleFormat = (key) => setFormats((current) => ({ ...current, [key]: !current[key] }))
  const toggleFilter = (key) => setFilters((current) => ({ ...current, [key]: !current[key] }))

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
        <Toggle size="sm" pressed={filters.starred} onPressedChange={() => toggleFilter('starred')}>
          Starred
        </Toggle>
        <Toggle size="sm" pressed={filters.archived} onPressedChange={() => toggleFilter('archived')}>
          Archived
        </Toggle>
        <Toggle size="sm" disabled>
          Locked
        </Toggle>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
      <Toggle aria-label="Bold" pressed={formats.bold} onPressedChange={() => toggleFormat('bold')}>
        <Bold aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />
      </Toggle>
      <Toggle aria-label="Italic" pressed={formats.italic} onPressedChange={() => toggleFormat('italic')}>
        <Italic aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />
      </Toggle>
      <Toggle aria-label="Underline" pressed={formats.underline} onPressedChange={() => toggleFormat('underline')}>
        <Underline aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />
      </Toggle>
      <Toggle aria-label="Bulleted list">
        <List aria-hidden="true" className="size-4" />
        List
      </Toggle>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Button** - The pressable control carrying aria-pressed for its on/off state.
- **Icon or label** - Compact content, usually icon-sized, named by aria-label when icon-only.
- **Pressed tint** - The data-state styling that visually distinguishes on from off.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use for binary states that apply immediately, like Bold or a filter flag.
- Give icon-only toggles an aria-label naming the option.
- Group related toggles in a Toolbar or ToggleGroup.

### Don't

- Don't use for settings that need explanation; use Switch with a label.
- Don't use a toggle to fire a one-shot action; use a Button.

## Interface

### Toggle

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `enum` | `md` | Control size. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | - | - |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to and from the toggle. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Flips the pressed state. |

- Exposes its state through aria-pressed, announced as a pressed or not-pressed toggle button.
- Icon-only toggles require aria-label to have an accessible name.

- [Toggle Group](/modules/toggle-group)
- [Switch](/modules/switch)
- [Toolbar](/modules/toolbar)

# Toolbar

A horizontal action bar with grouped controls and hairline separators.

## Usage

```js
import { Toolbar, ToolbarGroup, ToolbarSeparator, IconButton } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Toolbar>
  <ToolbarGroup>
    <IconButton label="Undo"><Undo2 /></IconButton>
  </ToolbarGroup>
  <ToolbarSeparator />
  <ToolbarGroup>
    <IconButton label="Bold"><Bold /></IconButton>
  </ToolbarGroup>
</Toolbar>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Several small controls act on one editor or view.
### Avoid when

The actions are unrelated page actions; use a header action area.
### Behavior

role="toolbar" groups controls; separators are decorative hairlines.
### Responsive

Let groups wrap or scroll horizontally on narrow screens.

## Examples

### Editor actions

role="toolbar" with groups keeps related controls navigable.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { IconButton, Toolbar, ToolbarGroup, ToolbarSeparator } from '@kryv/teal'
import { AlignCenter, AlignLeft, AlignRight, Bold, Italic, Link2, List, Redo2, Underline, Undo2 } from 'lucide-react'

const alignments = [
  { key: 'left', label: 'Align left', icon: AlignLeft },
  { key: 'center', label: 'Align center', icon: AlignCenter },
  { key: 'right', label: 'Align right', icon: AlignRight },
]

export function ToolbarDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [alignment, setAlignment] = useState('left')
  const [active, setActive] = useState({ bold: true, italic: false, underline: false })

  const toggleFormat = (key) => setActive((current) => ({ ...current, [key]: !current[key] }))
  const pressedClasses = 'teal-u-bg-primary/10 teal-u-text-primary'

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Toolbar aria-label="Text formatting">
        <ToolbarGroup>
          <IconButton
            size="sm"
            label="Bold"
            aria-pressed={active.bold}
            className={active.bold ? pressedClasses : undefined}
            onClick={() => toggleFormat('bold')}
          >
            <Bold aria-hidden="true" />
          </IconButton>
          <IconButton
            size="sm"
            label="Italic"
            aria-pressed={active.italic}
            className={active.italic ? pressedClasses : undefined}
            onClick={() => toggleFormat('italic')}
          >
            <Italic aria-hidden="true" />
          </IconButton>
          <IconButton
            size="sm"
            label="Underline"
            aria-pressed={active.underline}
            className={active.underline ? pressedClasses : undefined}
            onClick={() => toggleFormat('underline')}
          >
            <Underline aria-hidden="true" />
          </IconButton>
        </ToolbarGroup>
        <ToolbarSeparator />
        <ToolbarGroup>
          <IconButton size="sm" label="Insert link">
            <Link2 aria-hidden="true" />
          </IconButton>
          <IconButton size="sm" label="Bulleted list">
            <List aria-hidden="true" />
          </IconButton>
        </ToolbarGroup>
      </Toolbar>
    )
  }

  return (
    <Toolbar aria-label="Editor actions">
      <ToolbarGroup>
        <IconButton size="sm" label="Undo">
          <Undo2 aria-hidden="true" />
        </IconButton>
        <IconButton size="sm" label="Redo" disabled>
          <Redo2 aria-hidden="true" />
        </IconButton>
      </ToolbarGroup>
      <ToolbarSeparator />
      <ToolbarGroup>
        {alignments.map(({ key, label, icon: Icon }) => (
          <IconButton
            key={key}
            size="sm"
            label={label}
            aria-pressed={alignment === key}
            className={alignment === key ? pressedClasses : undefined}
            onClick={() => setAlignment(key)}
          >
            <Icon aria-hidden="true" />
          </IconButton>
        ))}
      </ToolbarGroup>
    </Toolbar>
  )
}
```

### Formatting groups

Group related controls and separate them with hairlines.

```jsx

          >
            <Bold aria-hidden="true" />
          </IconButton>
          <IconButton
            size="sm"
            label="Italic"
            aria-pressed={active.italic}
            className={active.italic ? pressedClasses : undefined}
            onClick={() => toggleFormat('italic')}
          >
            <Italic aria-hidden="true" />
          </IconButton>
          <IconButton
            size="sm"
            label="Underline"
            aria-pressed={active.underline}
            className={active.underline ? pressedClasses : undefined}
            onClick={() => toggleFormat('underline')}
          >
            <Underline aria-hidden="true" />
          </IconButton>
        </ToolbarGroup>
        <ToolbarSeparator />

          <IconButton size="sm" label="Insert link">
            <Link2 aria-hidden="true" />

          <Redo2 aria-hidden="true" />
        </IconButton>

```

## Anatomy

- **Toolbar** - The role="toolbar" container holding all groups.
- **ToolbarGroup** - A role="group" cluster of related controls within the bar.
- **ToolbarSeparator** - A decorative hairline between groups, hidden from assistive technology.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Group related controls with ToolbarGroup and separate clusters with ToolbarSeparator.
- Label every icon-only control with IconButton's label prop.
- Keep the bar to one row of compact controls that act on one view.

### Don't

- Don't put page-level commit actions here; use an ActionBar.
- Don't use a toolbar as a general layout row.
- Don't nest toolbars inside each other.

## Interface

### Toolbar

_This module forwards native element properties._

### ToolbarGroup

_This module forwards native element properties._

### ToolbarSeparator

_This module forwards native element properties._

## Accessibility

- Renders role="toolbar" so assistive technology announces the grouped controls as one toolbar.
- ToolbarGroup uses role="group" to keep related controls together in the accessibility tree.
- ToolbarSeparator is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
- Keyboard behavior comes from the controls inside; label icon buttons with IconButton's label prop.

- [Button](/modules/button)

# Split Button

A primary action joined to a menu of related alternatives.

## Usage

```js
import { SplitButton } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<SplitButton
  label="Deploy"
  onClick={() => undefined}
  items={[{ id: 'staging', label: 'Deploy to staging', onSelect: () => undefined }]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

One default action has a few close alternatives.
### Avoid when

The actions are unrelated; use separate buttons or a plain Menu.
### Behavior

The main button fires the default; the chevron owns the menu.
### Responsive

Keep the label short so the joined control stays one line.

## Examples

### Default plus alternatives

The main action fires directly; the chevron opens the related menu.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { SplitButton } from '@kryv/teal'

export function SplitButtonDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
        <SplitButton
          label="Save draft"
          variant="secondary"
          onClick={() => setMessage('Draft saved')}
          items={[
            { id: 'save-exit', label: 'Save and exit', onSelect: () => setMessage('Saved and exited') },
            { id: 'discard', label: 'Discard draft', variant: 'danger', separatorBefore: true, onSelect: () => setMessage('Draft discarded') },
          ]}
        />
        {message ? <p className="text-sm text-on-surface-variant">{message}</p> : null}
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <SplitButton
        label="Deploy"
        onClick={() => setMessage('Deploying to production')}
        items={[
          { id: 'staging', label: 'Deploy to staging', onSelect: () => setMessage('Deploying to staging') },
          { id: 'preview', label: 'Create preview deployment', onSelect: () => setMessage('Creating preview deployment') },
          { id: 'schedule', label: 'Schedule deployment', separatorBefore: true, onSelect: () => setMessage('Deployment scheduled') },
        ]}
      />
      {message ? <p className="text-sm text-on-surface-variant">{message}</p> : null}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Secondary and danger variants

The menu can carry a danger item behind the separator.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { SplitButton } from '@kryv/teal'

export function SplitButtonDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
        <SplitButton
          label="Save draft"
          variant="secondary"
          onClick={() => setMessage('Draft saved')}
          items={[
            { id: 'save-exit', label: 'Save and exit', onSelect: () => setMessage('Saved and exited') },
            { id: 'discard', label: 'Discard draft', variant: 'danger', separatorBefore: true, onSelect: () => setMessage('Draft discarded') },
          ]}
        />
        {message ? <p className="text-sm text-on-surface-variant">{message}</p> : null}
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-3">
      <SplitButton
        label="Deploy"
        onClick={() => setMessage('Deploying to production')}
        items={[
          { id: 'staging', label: 'Deploy to staging', onSelect: () => setMessage('Deploying to staging') },
          { id: 'preview', label: 'Create preview deployment', onSelect: () => setMessage('Creating preview deployment') },
          { id: 'schedule', label: 'Schedule deployment', separatorBefore: true, onSelect: () => setMessage('Deployment scheduled') },
        ]}
      />
      {message ? <p className="text-sm text-on-surface-variant">{message}</p> : null}
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Main action** - The button that fires the default action on click.
- **Menu trigger** - The chevron button named by menuLabel ("More actions" by default).
- **Menu** - The list of alternative actions sharing the main action's context.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Make the default the action most people want most of the time.
- Keep alternatives to a handful of close variants of the same action.
- Keep the main label short so the joined control stays on one line.

### Don't

- Don't put unrelated actions in the menu; use separate buttons or a plain Menu.
- Don't hide the only way to do something behind the chevron.

## Interface

### SplitButton

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables both the main action and the menu trigger. |
| `items` (required) | `MenuItem[]` | - | Secondary actions rendered in the attached menu. |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Content of the main action button. |
| `menuLabel` | `string` | `More actions` | Accessible label for the menu trigger button and the menu itself. |
| `onClick` (required) | `() => void` | - | Called when the main action is clicked. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| null` | - | Size of both buttons. |
| `variant` | `enum` | `primary` | Color treatment shared by both buttons. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the main action and then to the menu trigger. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Activates the focused half; the trigger opens the menu. |
| `Escape` | Closes the menu without selecting an item. |

- The main action and the menu trigger are separate focus stops with separate accessible names.
- The chevron trigger is named by menuLabel ("More actions" by default) and the menu shares that label.
- Menu items follow menu keyboard behavior through the underlying Menu component.

## Related modules

- [Button](/modules/button)
- [Menu](/modules/menu)
- [Button Group](/modules/button-group)

# Action Bar

A horizontal bar for contextual page-level actions such as a sticky save/cancel bar at the bottom of an editing surface.

## Usage

```js
import { ActionBar } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<ActionBar sticky label="Edit actions">
  <Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
  <Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>
</ActionBar>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A page or panel has primary and secondary actions that apply to the whole content, like saving an edited record.
### Avoid when

Actions belong to a single field or card; place buttons inline or use a ButtonGroup instead.
### Behavior

Renders a labelled region with actions aligned to the end; sticky pins it to the configured edge of the scrolling container.
### Responsive

The bar stretches full width and lets its actions wrap or shrink; keep the action set small on narrow screens.

## Examples

### Sticky bottom bar

The default bottom-positioned bar stays pinned while the surrounding form scrolls, keeping commit actions reachable.

```jsx
import { ActionBar, Button } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ActionBarDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xl overflow-hidden rounded-2xl border border-solid border-teal-outline-variant/40">
        <ActionBar position="top" label="Document actions">
          <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
            Discard
          </Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
            Save draft
          </Button>
        </ActionBar>
        <div className="p-4 text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
          A top-positioned bar keeps page-level actions visible above the content they affect.
        </div>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xl overflow-hidden rounded-2xl border border-solid border-teal-outline-variant/40">
      <div className="p-4 text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
        The sticky bar below stays pinned to the bottom of the editing surface while the form scrolls.
      </div>
      <ActionBar sticky label="Edit actions">
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
          Cancel
        </Button>
        <Button variant="primary" size="sm">
          Save changes
        </Button>
      </ActionBar>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Top bar

Positioned above the content for toolbars whose actions scope everything below them.

```jsx
import { ActionBar, Button } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ActionBarDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xl overflow-hidden rounded-2xl border border-solid border-teal-outline-variant/40">
        <ActionBar position="top" label="Document actions">
          <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
            Discard
          </Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
            Save draft
          </Button>
        </ActionBar>
        <div className="p-4 text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
          A top-positioned bar keeps page-level actions visible above the content they affect.
        </div>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xl overflow-hidden rounded-2xl border border-solid border-teal-outline-variant/40">
      <div className="p-4 text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
        The sticky bar below stays pinned to the bottom of the editing surface while the form scrolls.
      </div>
      <ActionBar sticky label="Edit actions">
        <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">
          Cancel
        </Button>
        <Button variant="primary" size="sm">
          Save changes
        </Button>
      </ActionBar>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Region** - The labelled landmark (role="region") wrapping the bar, named by the label prop.
- **Actions** - The caller-supplied buttons aligned to the end of the bar.
- **Sticky edge** - The optional sticky positioning that pins the bar to the top or bottom of its scroll container.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Label the region so multiple landmarks stay distinguishable.
- Place the primary commit action last in the bar.
- Keep the bar to two or three actions that apply to the whole surface.

### Don't

- Don't use it for actions scoped to one field or card; place those inline.
- Don't stack more than one action bar on a page.

## Interface

### ActionBar

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `Actions` | Accessible name for the action region. |
| `position` | `enum` | `bottom` | Edge of the content the bar sits on; flips the hairline border and sticky offset. |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `false` | Keeps the bar visible while the surrounding content scrolls. |

## Accessibility

- Exposed as a labelled landmark region so screen-reader users can jump straight to the page actions.
- The label prop names the region; choose one that describes what the actions apply to.

## Related modules

- [Toolbar](/modules/toolbar)
- [Bulk Action Bar](/modules/bulk-action-bar)
- [Page Header](/modules/page-header)

# Bulk Action Bar

A bar that appears when list or table rows are selected, announcing the selection count and offering bulk actions.

## Usage

```js
import { BulkActionBar } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<BulkActionBar count={selected.length} onClear={clearSelection}>
  <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Archive</Button>
  <Button variant="danger" size="sm">Delete</Button>
</BulkActionBar>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A list or table supports multi-select and the same action must apply to every selected row at once.
### Avoid when

Only one row is ever acted on; use row-level buttons or a Menu in context mode instead.
### Behavior

Renders nothing while count is 0; the count is announced politely as it changes, and onClear resets the selection.
### Responsive

Actions flex to fill the bar; on narrow widths keep bulk actions to two or three short labels.

## Examples

### Selection actions

Shows the selected row count alongside destructive and neutral bulk actions with a clear button.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { BulkActionBar, Button } from '@kryv/teal'

export function BulkActionBarDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(3)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xl">
        <BulkActionBar count={count} onClear={() => setCount(0)}>
          <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
            Archive
          </Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
            Assign
          </Button>
        </BulkActionBar>
        {count === 0 ? (
          <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => setCount(3)}>
            Select 3 rows again
          </Button>
        ) : null}
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xl">
      <BulkActionBar count={5} onClear={() => {}}>
        <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
          Download
        </Button>
        <Button variant="danger" size="sm">
          Delete
        </Button>
      </BulkActionBar>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Clearing the selection

The bar unmounts itself when the count drops to zero, so the list returns to its idle state.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { BulkActionBar, Button } from '@kryv/teal'

export function BulkActionBarDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(3)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xl">
        <BulkActionBar count={count} onClear={() => setCount(0)}>
          <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
            Archive
          </Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
            Assign
          </Button>
        </BulkActionBar>
        {count === 0 ? (
          <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" onClick={() => setCount(3)}>
            Select 3 rows again
          </Button>
        ) : null}
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xl">
      <BulkActionBar count={5} onClear={() => {}}>
        <Button variant="secondary" size="sm">
          Download
        </Button>
        <Button variant="danger" size="sm">
          Delete
        </Button>
      </BulkActionBar>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Count** - The selection total, announced politely through a live region as it changes.
- **Actions** - The bulk operations applied to every selected row at once.
- **Clear** - The control that resets the selection; the bar unmounts itself at zero.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Offer only actions that are safe to apply to many rows at once.
- Pair destructive bulk actions with a confirmation step.
- Keep labels to two or three short words on narrow screens.

### Don't

- Don't render the bar with an empty selection; it handles that itself.
- Don't put row-specific navigation or links in the bar.

## Interface

### BulkActionBar

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` (required) | `number` | - | Number of selected rows; the bar renders nothing while this is 0. |
| `label` | `string` | `Bulk actions` | Accessible name for the bulk action region. |
| `onClear` | `() => void` | - | Called when the user clears the selection. |

## Accessibility

- The selection count sits in an aria-live polite region so screen readers announce each change.
- Exposed as a labelled landmark region named by the label prop.

- [Action Bar](/modules/action-bar)
- [Table](/modules/table)
- [Checkbox](/modules/checkbox)

# Floating Action Button

A fixed-position primary action button for the single most important creation task on a screen.

## Usage

```js
import { FloatingActionButton } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<FloatingActionButton
  label="Create item"
  tooltip="Add a new item"
  position="bottom-right"
  onClick={createItem}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

One creation action dominates the screen, such as composing a message or adding a record to a long list.
### Avoid when

Several actions compete or the action is destructive; use an ActionBar or regular Button instead.
### Behavior

Stays fixed to the chosen viewport corner while content scrolls; label always names the button for assistive tech.
### Responsive

Keeps a constant offset from the viewport edges at all widths; prefer the extended pill only when space allows.

## Examples

### Round FAB with tooltip

Icon-only button fixed to a viewport corner; the tooltip supplies the visible name on hover.

```jsx
import { FilePlus, FolderPlus, Pencil, Upload } from 'lucide-react'
import { FloatingActionButton } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FloatingActionButtonDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <FloatingActionButton
        label="Compose message"
        extendedLabel="Compose"
        icon={<Pencil aria-hidden />}
        position="bottom-left"
      />
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <FloatingActionButton
        label="Create actions"
        position="bottom-right"
        actions={[
          { label: 'New file', icon: <FilePlus aria-hidden /> },
          { label: 'New folder', icon: <FolderPlus aria-hidden /> },
          { label: 'Upload', icon: <Upload aria-hidden /> },
        ]}
      />
    )
  }

  return <FloatingActionButton label="Create item" tooltip="Add a new item" position="bottom-right" />
}
```

### Extended FAB

An extendedLabel turns the round button into a pill with text for extra clarity.

```jsx
import { FilePlus, FolderPlus, Pencil, Upload } from 'lucide-react'
import { FloatingActionButton } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FloatingActionButtonDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <FloatingActionButton
        label="Compose message"
        extendedLabel="Compose"
        icon={<Pencil aria-hidden />}
        position="bottom-left"
      />
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <FloatingActionButton
        label="Create actions"
        position="bottom-right"
        actions={[
          { label: 'New file', icon: <FilePlus aria-hidden /> },
          { label: 'New folder', icon: <FolderPlus aria-hidden /> },
          { label: 'Upload', icon: <Upload aria-hidden /> },
        ]}
      />
    )
  }

  return <FloatingActionButton label="Create item" tooltip="Add a new item" position="bottom-right" />
}
```

### Actions fan-out

The actions prop expands the FAB into a fan of related actions with menu keyboard support.

```jsx
import { FilePlus, FolderPlus, Pencil, Upload } from 'lucide-react'
import { FloatingActionButton } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FloatingActionButtonDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <FloatingActionButton
        label="Compose message"
        extendedLabel="Compose"
        icon={<Pencil aria-hidden />}
        position="bottom-left"
      />
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <FloatingActionButton
        label="Create actions"
        position="bottom-right"
        actions={[
          { label: 'New file', icon: <FilePlus aria-hidden /> },
          { label: 'New folder', icon: <FolderPlus aria-hidden /> },
          { label: 'Upload', icon: <Upload aria-hidden /> },
        ]}
      />
    )
  }

  return <FloatingActionButton label="Create item" tooltip="Add a new item" position="bottom-right" />
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Button** - The round, fixed-position button named by the required label prop.
- **Icon** - The centered glyph, a plus by default, hidden from assistive technology.
- **Tooltip** - The optional hover and focus hint defaulting to the label.
- **Extended label** - The optional text that turns the round button into a labelled pill.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Reserve it for the single most important creation action on a screen.
- Always provide label so the icon-only button has an accessible name.
- Use extendedLabel where space allows for extra clarity.

### Don't

- Don't use it for destructive or secondary actions.
- Don't show more than one floating action button per screen.
- Don't let it cover primary content; pick the corner that stays clear.

## Interface

### FloatingActionButton

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `FloatingActionButtonAction[]` | - | Related actions the button fans out into; turns the FAB into a menu trigger. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial open state of the fan-out when uncontrolled. |
| `direction` | `enum` | `up` | Direction the actions fan out toward. |
| `extendedLabel` | `string` | - | Text rendered next to the icon; turns the round FAB into an extended pill. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon rendered inside the button. Defaults to a plus icon. |
| `label` (required) | `string` | - | Accessible name for the button; also the default tooltip text. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Called when the actions fan-out opens or closes. |
| `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state of the fan-out. |
| `openIcon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon shown on the open trigger when actions are present. Defaults to an X icon. |
| `position` | `enum` | `bottom-right` | Viewport corner the button is fixed to. |
| `tooltip` | `string` | - | Tooltip text shown on hover and focus; pass the label or a longer hint. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to and from the button. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Activates the button. |

- Icon-only by default, so the required label prop provides the accessible name via aria-label.
- The optional tooltip also exposes the name to sighted keyboard users on focus.

## Related modules

- [Action Bar](/modules/action-bar)
- [Button](/modules/button)
- [Menu](/modules/menu)

# Share Button

A button that opens a small popover with a copy-link action and, where supported, the native share sheet.

## Usage

```js
import { ShareButton } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<ShareButton
  url="https://example.com/report/42"
  title="Q3 report"
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Users need to pass a deep link to a record, report, or page to someone else.
### Avoid when

The goal is duplicating content inside the app; use a dedicated duplicate action instead.
### Behavior

Copies the given URL (or the current page URL) with visible and announced feedback, and degrades gracefully when clipboard or share APIs are missing.
### Responsive

The trigger is a standard button and the popover clamps to the viewport width, so it works at any size.

## Examples

### Copy link

The popover copies the URL to the clipboard and confirms with a swapped label and live-region announcement.

```jsx
import { ShareButton } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ShareButtonDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <ShareButton
          url="https://teal.kryv.dev/modules/share-button"
          title="ShareButton — Teal"
          variant="ghost"
          size="sm"
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <ShareButton url="https://teal.kryv.dev" title="Teal design system" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Native share fallback

Where navigator.share exists a Share via action appears; elsewhere the popover quietly offers copy only.

```jsx
import { ShareButton } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ShareButtonDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <ShareButton
          url="https://teal.kryv.dev/modules/share-button"
          title="ShareButton — Teal"
          variant="ghost"
          size="sm"
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <ShareButton url="https://teal.kryv.dev" title="Teal design system" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Trigger** - The button that opens the share popover.
- **Popover** - The small panel holding the copy-link action and, where supported, the native share action.
- **Confirmation** - The swapped label plus a visually hidden live region announcing that the link was copied.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Pass a canonical URL for the record rather than relying on the current page URL.
- Keep the title short; it is forwarded to the native share sheet.
- Let the native share action appear automatically where navigator.share exists.

### Don't

- Don't use it to duplicate content inside the app; add a dedicated duplicate action.
- Don't build custom copy feedback; the announced confirmation is built in.

## Interface

### ShareButton

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `copiedLabel` | `string` | `Link copied` | Feedback label shown briefly after the link is copied. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `label` | `string` | `Share` | Accessible name and visible text of the trigger button. |
| `variant` | `enum` | `secondary` | Visual style forwarded to the trigger button. |
| `size` | `enum` | - | Size forwarded to the trigger button. |
| `text` | `string` | - | Text shared through the native share sheet. |
| `title` | `string` | - | Title shared through the native share sheet. |
| `url` | `string` | - | URL copied or shared. Defaults to the current page URL. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Opens the share popover from the trigger. |
| `Escape` | Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger. |

- Copy feedback is announced through a polite live region, not just the swapped icon.
- The popover is labelled by the trigger text and closes on Escape via the underlying Popover.

## Related modules

- [Popover](/modules/popover)
- [Button](/modules/button)
- [Toast](/modules/toast)

# Field

A deep form seam that connects labels, descriptions, errors, and required state.

## Usage

```js
import { Field, Input } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Field label="Display name" description="Shown to other workspace members" required>
  <Input defaultValue="Avery Chen" />
</Field>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A control needs a visible label, help text, or validation message.
### Avoid when

The control already owns an equivalent form-label composition.
### Behavior

Field provides the id and ARIA relationships consumed by its child control.
### Responsive

Keep labels readable and let long error messages wrap.

## Examples

### Label, description, and error

Field wires the label, help text, and error message to the control inside it automatically.

```jsx
import { Checkbox, Field, Input, Switch, TextArea } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FieldDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5">
        <Field
          label="Work email"
          description="Used for sign-in and workspace invitations"
          required
          error="Enter a valid work email address"
        >
          <Input type="email" defaultValue="avery@example" autoComplete="email" />
        </Field>
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5">
        <Field label="Marketing emails" description="Unsubscribe any time from the email footer">
          <Checkbox defaultChecked />
        </Field>
        <Field label="Beta features" description="Applies immediately to this workspace">
          <Switch />
        </Field>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5">
      <Field label="Display name" description="Shown to other workspace members" required>
        <Input defaultValue="Avery Chen" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Notes" error="Keep notes under 240 characters">
        <TextArea defaultValue="Notify the incident team before changing this account." />
      </Field>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Choice controls

Checkbox and Switch render the Field label instead of their own when nested inside one.

```jsx
import { Checkbox, Field, Input, Switch, TextArea } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FieldDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5">
        <Field
          label="Work email"
          description="Used for sign-in and workspace invitations"
          required
          error="Enter a valid work email address"
        >
          <Input type="email" defaultValue="avery@example" autoComplete="email" />
        </Field>
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5">
        <Field label="Marketing emails" description="Unsubscribe any time from the email footer">
          <Checkbox defaultChecked />
        </Field>
        <Field label="Beta features" description="Applies immediately to this workspace">
          <Switch />
        </Field>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5">
      <Field label="Display name" description="Shown to other workspace members" required>
        <Input defaultValue="Avery Chen" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Notes" error="Keep notes under 240 characters">
        <TextArea defaultValue="Notify the incident team before changing this account." />
      </Field>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Account profile

Pair a required profile value with a clear validation message.

```jsx
import { Checkbox, Field, Input, Switch, TextArea } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FieldDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5">
        <Field
          label="Work email"
          description="Used for sign-in and workspace invitations"
          required
          error="Enter a valid work email address"
        >
          <Input type="email" defaultValue="avery@example" autoComplete="email" />
        </Field>
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5">
        <Field label="Marketing emails" description="Unsubscribe any time from the email footer">
          <Checkbox defaultChecked />
        </Field>
        <Field label="Beta features" description="Applies immediately to this workspace">
          <Switch />
        </Field>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5">
      <Field label="Display name" description="Shown to other workspace members" required>
        <Input defaultValue="Avery Chen" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Notes" error="Keep notes under 240 characters">
        <TextArea defaultValue="Notify the incident team before changing this account." />
      </Field>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Label** - Visible label wired to the control with htmlFor; carries the required marker when required is set.
- **Control** - The single child that receives the generated id, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid wiring.
- **Description** - Optional help text linked to the control through aria-describedby.
- **Error** - Validation message that marks the control aria-invalid and renders in error color.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Wrap every free-standing control in a Field so labels and errors stay wired automatically.
- Write errors that say how to fix the value, not just that it is invalid.
- Keep descriptions to one sentence; move longer explanations to an Alert with appearance="callout" or a help page.

### Don't

- Don't nest more than one control in a Field; use Fieldset for groups.
- Don't mark a field required visually without the required prop, or the attribute and marker drift apart.
- Don't clear the error while the value is still invalid; re-validate on change.

## Interface

### Field

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | The form control this field labels and describes. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Help text rendered below the control and linked to it for assistive technology. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | - | Error message; marks the control as invalid and links the message to it. |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Visible label associated with the control. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the control as required and renders a required indicator. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` | - | Marks the control invalid without requiring a visible error message. |

### Label

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Merges the component onto its child element instead of rendering the default element (Radix Slot). |

## Accessibility

- The label is wired to the control with htmlFor, so clicking the label focuses the control.
- Description and error text are linked to Input and TextArea children through aria-describedby automatically.
- Setting error marks the control aria-invalid and renders the message in error color.
- The required indicator is decorative; the underlying control keeps the native required attribute.
- Custom controls can join the same wiring through the exported useFieldControl hook and mergeDescriptionIds helper.

## Related modules

- [Input](/modules/input)
- [Fieldset](/modules/fieldset)
- [Form](/modules/form)
- [Form Error Summary](/modules/form-error-summary)

# Input

A native single-line text control with Teal sizing, invalid states, and a forwarded ref; clearable adds a clear action, loading swaps it for a spinner, and type="password" adds a reveal toggle.

## Usage

```js
import { Input } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Input placeholder="Project name" />
<Input clearable label="Search projects" />
<Input type="password" label="Password" />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Users enter or search for a single line of text.
### Avoid when

A constrained set of choices, a long-form editor, or multi-line text (use TextArea) is clearer.
### Behavior

Native input behavior is preserved, including browser validation and refs. clearable shows a clear action once the field has a value and loading swaps it for a spinner in the same slot; type="password" adds a visibility toggle that reports state through aria-pressed.
### Responsive

Use full width on small screens and constrain width at larger sizes.

## Examples

### States

Default, invalid, and disabled inputs share the same sizing and focus treatment.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Input } from '@kryv/teal'

export function InputDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('')

  if (exampleIndex === 4) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-xs gap-4">
        <Input
          type="password"
          label="Password"
          description="Use at least 12 characters"
          autoComplete="new-password"
        />
        <Input type="password" label="Current password" autoComplete="current-password" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 3) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-4">
        <Input
          clearable
          label="Search projects"
          description="Results update as you type"
          placeholder="Type a project name"
          value={query}
          onValueChange={setQuery}
        />
        <Input clearable label="Loading results" defaultValue="Design review" loading />
        <Input clearable label="Archived projects" placeholder="Unavailable" disabled />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-4">
        <Input clearable size="sm" label="Filter files" placeholder="Type to filter" />
        <Input
          label="Workspace slug"
          defaultValue="not a slug"
          aria-invalid="true"
          description="Use lowercase letters, numbers, and dashes only."
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-4">
        <Input aria-label="Email address" type="email" placeholder="name@company.com" autoComplete="email" />
        <Input aria-label="Mobile number" type="tel" inputMode="tel" placeholder="+1 555 010 2299" autoComplete="tel" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-4">
      <Input aria-label="Search projects" placeholder="Search projects" />
      <Input aria-label="Email address" defaultValue="not-an-email" aria-invalid="true" />
      <Input aria-label="Disabled input" placeholder="Disabled input" disabled />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Semantic types

type, inputMode, and autoComplete steer the on-screen keyboard and autofill.


### Search and inline validation

Use a compact search control alongside an input that reports its invalid state.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Input } from '@kryv/teal'

export function InputDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('')

  if (exampleIndex === 4) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-xs gap-4">
        <Input
          type="password"
          label="Password"
          description="Use at least 12 characters"
          autoComplete="new-password"
        />
        <Input type="password" label="Current password" autoComplete="current-password" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 3) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-4">
        <Input
          clearable
          label="Search projects"
          description="Results update as you type"
          placeholder="Type a project name"
          value={query}
          onValueChange={setQuery}
        />
        <Input clearable label="Loading results" defaultValue="Design review" loading />
        <Input clearable label="Archived projects" placeholder="Unavailable" disabled />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-4">
        <Input clearable size="sm" label="Filter files" placeholder="Type to filter" />
        <Input
          label="Workspace slug"
          defaultValue="not a slug"
          aria-invalid="true"
          description="Use lowercase letters, numbers, and dashes only."
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-4">
        <Input aria-label="Email address" type="email" placeholder="name@company.com" autoComplete="email" />
        <Input aria-label="Mobile number" type="tel" inputMode="tel" placeholder="+1 555 010 2299" autoComplete="tel" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-4">
      <Input aria-label="Search projects" placeholder="Search projects" />
      <Input aria-label="Email address" defaultValue="not-an-email" aria-invalid="true" />
      <Input aria-label="Disabled input" placeholder="Disabled input" disabled />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Clearable and loading

clearable shows a clear action once the field has a value; loading swaps it for a spinner in the same slot, and disabled fields hide both.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Input } from '@kryv/teal'
```
