# Editable

Click-to-edit text that commits on Enter or blur and cancels with Escape.

## Usage

```js
import { Editable } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Editable label="Project name" defaultValue="Orion" onSubmit={(value) => undefined} />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A displayed value is renamed or corrected in place.
### Avoid when

The value is edited alongside others in a form; use Field and Input.
### Behavior

Enter and blur commit, Escape cancels, and the draft is preselected.
### Responsive

The preview truncates within its container width.

## Examples

### Inline rename

Preview stays a button; editing autofocuses and selects the draft.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Editable } from '@kryv/teal'

export function EditableDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [name, setName] = useState('Project Orion')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Editable label="Short description" placeholder="Add a description" />
        <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Empty values stay discoverable through the placeholder.</span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Editable label="Project name" value={name} onSubmit={setName} />
      <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Click the text to rename; Enter commits, Escape cancels.</span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Empty value

A placeholder keeps an empty value discoverable and inviting.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Editable } from '@kryv/teal'

export function EditableDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [name, setName] = useState('Project Orion')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <Editable label="Short description" placeholder="Add a description" />
        <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Empty values stay discoverable through the placeholder.</span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <Editable label="Project name" value={name} onSubmit={setName} />
      <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Click the text to rename; Enter commits, Escape cancels.</span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Preview** - The button that shows the current value and starts editing on activation.
- **Edit input** - The autofocused field with the current draft preselected.
- **Edit affordance** - The labeled edit button with a pencil icon marking the value as changeable.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use Editable for single values renamed in place, like project titles.
- Commit on Enter and blur so keyboard and pointer flows both save.
- Show a placeholder so empty values stay discoverable.

### Don't

- Don't use it inside multi-field forms; use Field and Input.
- Don't validate on cancel; Escape always restores the committed value.
- Don't hide the edit affordance; the pencil communicates interactivity.

## Interface

### Editable

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | - | Initial text when uncontrolled. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Prevents switching to edit mode. |
| `label` | `string` | `text` | Accessible name describing the edited text. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the draft text on every keystroke while editing. |
| `onSubmit` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the final text when a draft is committed (Enter or blur). |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `Empty` | Text shown in preview mode when the value is empty. |
| `value` | `string` | - | Controlled text shown in preview mode. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Starts editing from the preview or edit button. |
| `Enter` | Commits the draft while editing. |
| `Escape` | Cancels editing and restores the committed value. |
| `Tab` | Commits the draft on blur and moves focus on. |

- The preview is a real button showing the value or placeholder, so the entry point is keyboard reachable.
- The edit input autofocuses with the current value preselected and is named by the label.
- A separate IconButton labeled Edit plus the label offers an explicit affordance; the pencil icon is decorative.

- [Input](/modules/input)
- [Field](/modules/field)
- [Form](/modules/form)

# Currency Input

A numeric amount field with a leading currency symbol that formats the value with Intl.NumberFormat on blur.

## Usage

```js
import { CurrencyInput } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<CurrencyInput
  label="Invoice total"
  currency="USD"
  locale="en-US"
  defaultValue={1234.5}
  onChange={(amount) => console.log(amount)}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

The user enters a monetary amount in a known currency, such as prices, budgets, or invoice totals.
### Avoid when

The value is a plain number without a currency; use NumberInput instead. For multi-currency entry, pair a Select with NumberInput.
### Behavior

Emits the parsed number on every edit (undefined when emptied) and formats the display with Intl.NumberFormat on blur, clamping to min/max.
### Responsive

The field stretches to fill its container; the leading symbol addon stays a fixed width.

## Examples

### Currency and locale

The symbol and fraction digits follow the currency code, while grouping and separators follow the locale.

```jsx
import { CurrencyInput } from '@kryv/teal'

export function CurrencyInputDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
        <CurrencyInput
          label="Monthly budget"
          description="Clamped between $0 and $5,000 when the field loses focus."
          min={0}
          max={5000}
          defaultValue={1250}
        />
        <CurrencyInput label="Custom amount" placeholder="0.00" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
      <CurrencyInput label="Invoice total" defaultValue={1234.5} />
      <CurrencyInput label="Revenue" currency="EUR" locale="de-DE" defaultValue={98765.4} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Clamped budget

min and max clamp the committed amount on blur, and a description explains the limits.

```jsx
import { CurrencyInput } from '@kryv/teal'

export function CurrencyInputDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
        <CurrencyInput
          label="Monthly budget"
          description="Clamped between $0 and $5,000 when the field loses focus."
          min={0}
          max={5000}
          defaultValue={1250}
        />
        <CurrencyInput label="Custom amount" placeholder="0.00" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
      <CurrencyInput label="Invoice total" defaultValue={1234.5} />
      <CurrencyInput label="Revenue" currency="EUR" locale="de-DE" defaultValue={98765.4} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Label** - The visible label associated with the amount field.
- **Currency symbol** - A fixed-width leading addon derived from the currency code; decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
- **Amount input** - A decimal text field that emits the parsed number and reformats with Intl.NumberFormat on blur.
- **Help or error text** - Optional description, for example the min and max limits, linked with aria-describedby.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Set the currency and locale from the user's account, not the server's location.
- Clamp with min and max when a budget or limit exists, and say so in the description.
- Store the emitted number, not the formatted display string.

### Don't

- Don't use it for values without a currency; use NumberInput.
- Don't use one field for multi-currency entry; pair a currency Select with the amount.

## Interface

### CurrencyInput

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | - | Extra description ids, merged with the component's own description. |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` | - | Marks the input invalid for form validation and screen readers. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | - | Accessible name when there is no visible label. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `currency` | `string` | `USD` | ISO 4217 currency code used for the leading symbol and fraction digits. |
| `defaultValue` | `number` | - | Initial amount when uncontrolled. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Supporting text rendered below the input. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Prevents interaction with the input. |
| `id` | `string` | - | Explicit id; otherwise Field or an internal id is used. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Visible label rendered above the input. Required outside a Field; inside a Field the Field's label is used. |
| `locale` | `string` | `en-US` | BCP 47 locale used for grouping and decimal separators. |
| `max` | `number` | - | Largest allowed amount; the field clamps to it on blur. |
| `min` | `number` | - | Smallest allowed amount; the field clamps to it on blur. |
| `onChange` | `(value: number) => void` | - | Called with the parsed amount, or undefined when the field is emptied. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | - | Text shown when the field is empty. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | Marks the input as required. |
| `value` | `number` | - | Controlled amount. |

## Accessibility

- The visible label is associated with the input; use aria-label when there is no visible label.
- The currency symbol is decorative (aria-hidden) because the formatted value communicates the unit.
- inputMode="decimal" summons a numeric keypad on touch devices.

- [Number Input](/modules/number-input)
- [Masked Input](/modules/masked-input)
- [Input Group](/modules/input-group)

# Fieldset

A semantic fieldset/legend group for related fields, with optional help text linked to the whole group.

## Usage

```js
import { Fieldset, Field, Input } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Fieldset legend="Shipping address">
  <Field label="Street" required>
    <Input />
  </Field>
</Fieldset>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Several controls together answer one question, such as an address block or a set of related checkboxes.
### Avoid when

A single labeled control is enough; use Field on its own instead.
### Behavior

The legend names the group for assistive technology; the disabled attribute disables every control inside, as native fieldsets do.
### Responsive

Children lay out in a single-column grid; add your own grid classes inside for multi-column rows.

## Examples

### Grouping fields

Related Fields sit under one legend so the group is announced as a unit.

```jsx
import { Checkbox, Field, Fieldset, Input } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FieldsetDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Fieldset
        className="w-full max-w-md"
        legend="Notification channels"
        description="Choose how the workspace reaches you"
      >
        <Checkbox label="Email digest" description="A weekly summary of activity" defaultChecked />
        <Checkbox label="Mentions" description="Only when someone tags you" />
      </Fieldset>
    )
  }

  return (
    <Fieldset className="w-full max-w-md" legend="Shipping address">
      <Field label="Street" required>
        <Input placeholder="500 Market Street" />
      </Field>
      <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
        <Field label="City">
          <Input placeholder="San Francisco" />
        </Field>
        <Field label="Postal code">
          <Input placeholder="94105" />
        </Field>
      </div>
    </Fieldset>
  )
}
```

### Group description

Help text below the legend is linked to the fieldset with aria-describedby.

```jsx
import { Checkbox, Field, Fieldset, Input } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FieldsetDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Fieldset
        className="w-full max-w-md"
        legend="Notification channels"
        description="Choose how the workspace reaches you"
      >
        <Checkbox label="Email digest" description="A weekly summary of activity" defaultChecked />
        <Checkbox label="Mentions" description="Only when someone tags you" />
      </Fieldset>
    )
  }

  return (
    <Fieldset className="w-full max-w-md" legend="Shipping address">
      <Field label="Street" required>
        <Input placeholder="500 Market Street" />
      </Field>
      <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
        <Field label="City">
          <Input placeholder="San Francisco" />
        </Field>
        <Field label="Postal code">
          <Input placeholder="94105" />
        </Field>
      </div>
    </Fieldset>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Fieldset** - The native grouping element; setting disabled on it disables every control inside.
- **Legend** - Names the group so screen readers announce it when focus enters any field.
- **Description** - Optional help text for the whole group, linked with aria-describedby.
- **Children** - The related Fields or controls, laid out in a single-column grid by default.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Group controls that together answer one question, like an address block.
- Keep the legend short; it is repeated before every field inside.
- Nest Field components inside so labels and errors still work per control.

### Don't

- Don't wrap a single control in a Fieldset; Field alone is enough.
- Don't use Fieldset as a visual card for unrelated content; use Card.

## Interface

### Fieldset

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legend` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Caption rendered as the fieldset legend; names the group for assistive technology. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Help text rendered below the legend and linked to the group for assistive technology. |

## Accessibility

- Renders a real fieldset/legend pair, so screen readers announce the legend when entering the group.
- The description is exposed through aria-describedby on the fieldset.

## Related modules

- [Field](/modules/field)
- [Form](/modules/form)
- [Card](/modules/card)

# Form

A lightweight form wrapper that collects field values on submit and shares an error map through context, with no form library.

## Usage

```js
import { Form, Field, Input, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Form
  errors={{ email: 'Use your work email' }}
  onSubmit={(values) => console.log(values)}
>
  <Field label="Work email" required>
    <Input name="email" type="email" />
  </Field>
  <Button type="submit" variant="primary">Save</Button>
</Form>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A plain HTML form needs value collection and a shared validation error map without adopting a form library.
### Avoid when

Complex per-field state, async validation, or dependent fields are required; a dedicated form library fits better.
### Behavior

Submitting collects values with FormData (repeated names become arrays) and calls onSubmit after preventing navigation; the errors map is read through useFormFieldError.
### Responsive

Layout is fully caller-controlled; stack fields single-column on narrow screens.

## Examples

### Submitting values

onSubmit receives every named field value collected with FormData; the default page navigation is prevented.

```jsx
import { Button, Field, Form, Input } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FormDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Form
        className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5"
        errors={{ email: 'Use your work email to continue' }}
        onSubmit={() => undefined}
      >
        <Field label="Work email" error="Use your work email to continue" required>
          <Input name="email" type="email" placeholder="avery@kryvlabs.com" />
        </Field>
        <div>
          <Button type="submit" variant="primary">
            Request invite
          </Button>
        </div>
      </Form>
    )
  }

  return (
    <Form
      className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5"
      onSubmit={(values) => console.log('submitted', values)}
    >
      <Field label="Display name" description="Shown to other workspace members" required>
        <Input name="displayName" defaultValue="Avery Chen" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Job title">
        <Input name="jobTitle" placeholder="Product designer" />
      </Field>
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <Button type="submit" variant="primary">
          Save profile
        </Button>
        <Button type="reset" variant="ghost">
          Reset
        </Button>
      </div>
    </Form>
  )
}
```

### Server error map

The errors prop is exposed through context so descendants can render per-field messages without prop drilling.

```jsx
import { Button, Field, Form, Input } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FormDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Form
        className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5"
        errors={{ email: 'Use your work email to continue' }}
        onSubmit={() => undefined}
      >
        <Field label="Work email" error="Use your work email to continue" required>
          <Input name="email" type="email" placeholder="avery@kryvlabs.com" />
        </Field>
        <div>
          <Button type="submit" variant="primary">
            Request invite
          </Button>
        </div>
      </Form>
    )
  }

  return (
    <Form
      className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-5"
      onSubmit={(values) => console.log('submitted', values)}
    >
      <Field label="Display name" description="Shown to other workspace members" required>
        <Input name="displayName" defaultValue="Avery Chen" />
      </Field>
      <Field label="Job title">
        <Input name="jobTitle" placeholder="Product designer" />
      </Field>
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <Button type="submit" variant="primary">
          Save profile
        </Button>
        <Button type="reset" variant="ghost">
          Reset
        </Button>
      </div>
    </Form>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Form element** - A semantic form that prevents the default navigation and collects named values with FormData on submit.
- **Error context** - The errors map shared with descendants, read through useFormFieldError without prop drilling.
- **Fields and controls** - Named inputs whose values arrive in the onSubmit payload; repeated names become arrays.
- **Actions** - Submit and reset buttons supplied by the caller.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Give every collected control a name attribute; unnamed controls are skipped.
- Render server errors next to their fields, and add a FormErrorSummary for long forms.
- Put the submit Button inside the Form so Enter submission works.

### Don't

- Don't reach for it when you need async per-field validation or dependent fields; adopt a form library.
- Don't duplicate the errors map into local state; pass it straight to the errors prop.

## Interface

### Form

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `errors` | `Record<string, ReactNode>` | - | Validation messages keyed by field name, exposed to descendants through context. |
| `onSubmit` | `(values: Record<string, FormDataEntryValue \| FormDataEntryValue[]>, event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => void` | - | Called with the collected field values on submit; the default page navigation is prevented. |

## Accessibility

- Renders a semantic form element; give it an accessible name when the page has several forms.
- Error messages flow through context so fields can link them with aria-describedby and mark controls aria-invalid.

## Related modules

- [Field](/modules/field)
- [Fieldset](/modules/fieldset)
- [Form Error Summary](/modules/form-error-summary)

# Form Error Summary

A top-of-form alert that lists validation errors as anchor links which focus the offending field.

## Usage

```js
import { FormErrorSummary } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<FormErrorSummary
  errors={[
    { fieldId: "email", label: "Email", message: "Enter a valid email address." },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Long or complex forms submit server- or client-side validation failures that users must locate quickly.
### Avoid when

A single visible field fails inline; the Field error message alone is enough and a summary would repeat it.
### Behavior

Activating an error link prevents navigation and focuses the element with the matching id, adding tabindex=-1 first when it is not naturally focusable. Renders nothing when the errors list is empty.
### Responsive

The summary stacks its icon, heading, and link list at any width within the form container.

## Examples

### Multiple field errors

Each error becomes a link whose target is the field id, so activating it moves focus straight to the control.

```jsx
import { Field, FormErrorSummary, Input } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FormErrorSummaryDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-md space-y-4">
        <FormErrorSummary
          title="Fix this error to continue"
          errors={[{ fieldId: 'demo-card-number', label: 'Card number', message: 'Enter the 16-digit number on the card.' }]}
        />
        <Field id="demo-card-number" label="Card number" error="Enter the 16-digit number on the card." required>
          <Input placeholder="1234 5678 9012 3456" />
        </Field>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-md space-y-4">
      <FormErrorSummary
        errors={[
          { fieldId: 'demo-email', label: 'Email', message: 'Enter a valid email address.' },
          { fieldId: 'demo-password', label: 'Password', message: 'Use at least 12 characters.' },
        ]}
      />
      <Field id="demo-email" label="Email" error="Enter a valid email address." required>
        <Input type="email" defaultValue="avery@example" />
      </Field>
      <Field id="demo-password" label="Password" error="Use at least 12 characters." required>
        <Input type="password" defaultValue="short" />
      </Field>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Single error with custom title

The heading can be tailored to the error count or form context while the linking behavior stays the same.

```jsx
import { Field, FormErrorSummary, Input } from '@kryv/teal'

export function FormErrorSummaryDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-md space-y-4">
        <FormErrorSummary
          title="Fix this error to continue"
          errors={[{ fieldId: 'demo-card-number', label: 'Card number', message: 'Enter the 16-digit number on the card.' }]}
        />
        <Field id="demo-card-number" label="Card number" error="Enter the 16-digit number on the card." required>
          <Input placeholder="1234 5678 9012 3456" />
        </Field>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-md space-y-4">
      <FormErrorSummary
        errors={[
          { fieldId: 'demo-email', label: 'Email', message: 'Enter a valid email address.' },
          { fieldId: 'demo-password', label: 'Password', message: 'Use at least 12 characters.' },
        ]}
      />
      <Field id="demo-email" label="Email" error="Enter a valid email address." required>
        <Input type="email" defaultValue="avery@example" />
      </Field>
      <Field id="demo-password" label="Password" error="Use at least 12 characters." required>
        <Input type="password" defaultValue="short" />
      </Field>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Alert container** - A role=alert region, so new validation failures are announced as soon as it renders.
- **Heading** - A customizable title summarizing the failure count or context.
- **Error list** - Anchor links, one per error, whose targets are the offending field ids.
- **Icon** - A decorative alert icon; the message text carries the meaning.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Place it at the top of the form and move focus there after a failed submit.
- Keep each link's message identical to the error shown at its field.
- Pass real field ids so activating a link focuses the control.

### Don't

- Don't render it for a single inline error; the field message is enough.
- Don't link to fields that are hidden or disabled on the current step.

## Interface

### FormErrorSummary

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `errors` (required) | `FormErrorItem[]` | - | Field errors listed as focus links; the summary renders nothing when empty. |
| `onErrorClick` | `(error: FormErrorItem) => void` | - | Called after an error link is activated, with its item. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | `There is a problem` | Heading text of the summary. |

## Accessibility

- The summary uses role="alert" so new validation failures are announced as soon as it renders.
- Each entry is a real anchor linking to the field id, so the destination is exposed to assistive technology even before activation.

## Related modules

- [Form](/modules/form)
- [Field](/modules/field)
- [Alert](/modules/alert)

# Masked Input

A text field that enforces a simple digit mask, inserting separators automatically as the user types.

## Usage

```js
import { MaskedInput } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<MaskedInput
  label="Date"
  mask="##/##/####"
  onChange={(value) => console.log(value)}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

The value has a fixed digit count with familiar separators, such as dates, card expiries, or US phone numbers.
### Avoid when

The format varies by region or allows letters; use a plain Input with a description, or PhoneInput for international numbers.
### Behavior

Only digits are accepted, literals are inserted automatically, the caret stays after the last filled slot, and onChange receives the masked string.
### Responsive

The field stretches to fill its container; fixed-width masks pair well with tabular numerals.

## Examples

### Date and expiry masks

'#' marks a digit slot and every other character is a literal; the mask itself is the placeholder.

```jsx
import { MaskedInput } from '@kryv/teal'

export function MaskedInputDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
        <MaskedInput
          label="Phone (US)"
          mask="(###) ###-####"
          description="Only digits are accepted; separators appear automatically."
        />
        <MaskedInput label="Zip + 4" mask="#####-####" defaultValue="941073101" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
      <MaskedInput label="Date" mask="##/##/####" />
      <MaskedInput label="Card expiry" mask="##/##" defaultValue="0428" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Phone and ZIP masks

Longer regional formats work the same way, and a description can document the expected shape.

```jsx
import { MaskedInput } from '@kryv/teal'

export function MaskedInputDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
        <MaskedInput
          label="Phone (US)"
          mask="(###) ###-####"
          description="Only digits are accepted; separators appear automatically."
        />
        <MaskedInput label="Zip + 4" mask="#####-####" defaultValue="941073101" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
      <MaskedInput label="Date" mask="##/##/####" />
      <MaskedInput label="Card expiry" mask="##/##" defaultValue="0428" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Label** - The visible label associated with the field.
- **Masked input** - A text field that accepts digits for # slots, inserts literal separators automatically, and keeps the caret after the last filled slot.
- **Mask placeholder** - The mask itself renders as the placeholder, so the expected shape is visible before typing.
- **Help or error text** - Optional description documenting the expected format, linked with aria-describedby.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use it for fixed digit-count formats like dates, card expiries, or US phone numbers.
- Add a description when the format is ambiguous across regions, such as day-first dates.
- Validate the completed value on submit; the mask only enforces shape.

### Don't

- Don't use it for formats with letters or variable length; the mask only handles digits.
- Don't use it for international phone numbers; use PhoneInput instead.

## Interface

### MaskedInput

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | - | Extra description ids, merged with the component's own description. |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` | - | Marks the input invalid for form validation and screen readers. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | - | Accessible name when there is no visible label. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | - | Initial value when uncontrolled; digits are extracted and re-masked. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Supporting text rendered below the input. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Prevents interaction with the input. |
| `id` | `string` | - | Explicit id; otherwise Field or an internal id is used. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Visible label rendered above the input. Required outside a Field; inside a Field the Field's label is used. |
| `mask` (required) | `string` | - | Mask pattern; `#` marks a digit slot, every other character is a literal (use non-digit literals). |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the masked string whenever the digits change. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | - | Text shown when the field is empty; defaults to the mask itself. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | Marks the input as required. |
| `value` | `string` | - | Controlled value; digits are extracted and re-masked. |

## Accessibility

- The mask doubles as the placeholder so the expected format is visible before typing.
- The visible label is associated with the input; use aria-label when there is no visible label.
- Non-digit key presses are ignored rather than announced; pair with a description for the expected format.

## Related modules

- [Input](/modules/input)
- [Phone Input](/modules/phone-input)
- [PIN Input](/modules/pin-input)

# Mention Input

A textarea with @-mention autocomplete that inserts chosen people as plain text tokens.

## Usage

```js
import { MentionInput } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<MentionInput
  label="Comment"
  placeholder="Type @ to mention a teammate…"
  options={[{ value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Lovelace' }]}
  onMentionSelect={(option) => undefined}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Free-form text needs lightweight references to people or records, such as comments, handoff notes, or review feedback.
### Avoid when

Mentions must stay structured or deletable as chips — that needs a tokenized editor; for plain multi-line text without mentions use TextArea.
### Behavior

Choosing an option inserts `@Label ` at the caret as plain text; the popup only opens for an @ that starts a new token and closes after insertion.
### Responsive

The textarea fills its container and the popup anchors below it with a fixed, scrollable width.

## Examples

### Mention autocomplete

Typing @ opens the popup; the query filters options and Enter inserts the highlighted person.

```jsx
import { MentionInput } from '@kryv/teal'

const people = [
  { value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Lovelace' },
  { value: 'alan', label: 'Alan Turing' },
  { value: 'grace', label: 'Grace Hopper' },
  { value: 'katherine', label: 'Katherine Johnson' },
]

export function MentionInputDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-md">
        <MentionInput
          label="Handoff notes"
          defaultValue={'Follow up with @Grace Hopper about the rollout.'}
          options={people}
          rows={4}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-md">
      <MentionInput
        label="Comment"
        placeholder="Type @ to mention a teammate…"
        options={people}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Prefilled conversation

Existing mentions are plain text, so drafts round-trip through any storage without a rich text format.

```jsx
import { MentionInput } from '@kryv/teal'

const people = [
  { value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Lovelace' },
  { value: 'alan', label: 'Alan Turing' },
  { value: 'grace', label: 'Grace Hopper' },
  { value: 'katherine', label: 'Katherine Johnson' },
]

export function MentionInputDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-md">
        <MentionInput
          label="Handoff notes"
          defaultValue={'Follow up with @Grace Hopper about the rollout.'}
          options={people}
          rows={4}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-md">
      <MentionInput
        label="Comment"
        placeholder="Type @ to mention a teammate…"
        options={people}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Label** - The visible label associated with the textarea.
- **Textarea** - A plain multi-line field that keeps focus while the popup is open, with aria-autocomplete list.
- **Mention popup** - A listbox of options filtered by the query after an @ that starts a new token.
- **Inserted mention** - Plain @Label text at the caret, so drafts round-trip through any storage.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Feed options from the people or records directory of the current context.
- Use onMentionSelect to record the chosen id alongside the plain text.
- Keep option labels as display names people recognize.

### Don't

- Don't use it when mentions must stay structured or deletable as chips; that needs a tokenized editor.
- Don't dump hundreds of options in the popup; filter server-side for large directories.

## Interface

### MentionInput

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | - | Initial text when uncontrolled. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Visible label rendered above the textarea. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the full text whenever it changes. |
| `onMentionSelect` | `(option: MentionOption) => void` | - | Called with the option after its mention token is inserted. |
| `options` (required) | `MentionOption[]` | - | People or records offered by the @ -mention autocomplete popup. |
| `value` | `string` | - | Controlled text. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Arrow Down` + `Arrow Up` | Moves the highlight through the mention options. |
| `Enter` + `Tab` | Inserts the highlighted mention. |
| `Escape` | Dismisses the popup without changing the text. |

- The textarea keeps focus while the popup is open and points to the highlighted option with aria-activedescendant.
- aria-expanded and aria-controls mirror the popup state; options render in a listbox named "Mentions".

## Related modules

- [Input](/modules/input)
- [Combobox](/modules/combobox)

# Password Strength Meter

A progressbar-style meter that visualizes password strength from a caller-supplied or built-in score.

## Usage

```js
import { PasswordStrengthMeter } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<PasswordStrengthMeter
  password={password}
  score={(value) => zxcvbn(value).score}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A sign-up or password-change flow should give live feedback on password quality next to a password Input.
### Avoid when

You only need to state requirements; a description list under a password Input is simpler and less noisy.
### Behavior

Scores are clamped to 0–4 and mapped to Very weak through Very strong; the score prop replaces the default heuristic entirely.
### Responsive

The meter stretches to fill its container; the label and strength text stay on one row with space between.

## Examples

### Default heuristic

The built-in scorer rewards length and character variety, mapping passwords onto five labeled bands.

```jsx
import { PasswordStrengthMeter } from '@kryv/teal'

export function PasswordStrengthMeterDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
        <PasswordStrengthMeter
          label="Passphrase strength"
          password="correct horse battery staple"
          score={(value) => Math.min(4, Math.floor(value.length / 8))}
        />
        <PasswordStrengthMeter password="Abcdefgh1!23" showLabel={false} />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
      <PasswordStrengthMeter password="abc" />
      <PasswordStrengthMeter password="Abcdefg1" />
      <PasswordStrengthMeter password="Abcdefgh1!23" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Custom scorer

Bring your own scoring function (for example zxcvbn) or hide the visible text while keeping the accessible value.

```jsx
import { PasswordStrengthMeter } from '@kryv/teal'

export function PasswordStrengthMeterDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
        <PasswordStrengthMeter
          label="Passphrase strength"
          password="correct horse battery staple"
          score={(value) => Math.min(4, Math.floor(value.length / 8))}
        />
        <PasswordStrengthMeter password="Abcdefgh1!23" showLabel={false} />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
      <PasswordStrengthMeter password="abc" />
      <PasswordStrengthMeter password="Abcdefg1" />
      <PasswordStrengthMeter password="Abcdefgh1!23" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Label row** - The meter label and the current strength band text, spaced apart on one row.
- **Meter track** - A progressbar with aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax 4, and the band name as aria-valuetext.
- **Fill** - The colored portion reflecting the clamped 0–4 score; never the only signal, since the band is also text.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Place it directly under the password Input it scores and pass the live password value.
- Supply a real estimator such as zxcvbn through the score prop for sign-up flows.
- Keep the visible band text on; hide it only when space is truly constrained.

### Don't

- Don't use the meter as the only statement of password requirements; list the rules too.
- Don't block submission on the meter alone; enforce policy server-side.

## Interface

### PasswordStrengthMeter

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `Password strength` | Accessible name for the meter. |
| `password` (required) | `string` | - | Password to score. |
| `score` | `(password: string) => number` | - | Custom scoring function returning 0 (very weak) to 4 (very strong). |
| `showLabel` | `boolean` | `true` | Hides the visible strength text; assistive technology still hears it via aria-valuetext. |

## Accessibility

- Exposes role="progressbar" with aria-valuemin 0, aria-valuemax 4, and the band name as aria-valuetext.
- The strength is never conveyed by color alone; the band label is visible text and an accessible value.

## Related modules

- [Input](/modules/input)
- [Meter](/modules/meter)
- [Form](/modules/form)

# Phone Input

A country calling-code dropdown paired with a national number field that emits an E.164-ish string.

## Usage

```js
import { PhoneInput } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<PhoneInput
  label="Phone number"
  defaultValue="+14155552671"
  onChange={(value) => console.log(value)}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

You collect phone numbers that must be stored in a normalized international form, such as contact or billing profiles.
### Avoid when

The number is always domestic; a MaskedInput with a national format is less UI. For free-form contact info use a plain Input.
### Behavior

Emits +<dial><digits> on every edit and undefined when the number is emptied; non-digit characters are stripped from the national number.
### Responsive

The country dropdown keeps its natural width while the number field flexes to fill the remaining space.

## Examples

### Basic entry

A curated calling-code list keeps the dropdown short while covering the most common regions.

```jsx
import { PhoneInput } from '@kryv/teal'

export function PhoneInputDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
        <PhoneInput
          label="Support line"
          description="Stored as an E.164-ish string like +442071234567."
          defaultValue="+442071234567"
        />
        <PhoneInput label="Mobile" placeholder="555 123 4567" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
      <PhoneInput label="Phone number" />
      <PhoneInput label="Emergency contact" defaultValue="+14155552671" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Prefilled international number

An existing E.164-ish value is parsed back into the right country and national number.

```jsx
import { PhoneInput } from '@kryv/teal'

export function PhoneInputDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
        <PhoneInput
          label="Support line"
          description="Stored as an E.164-ish string like +442071234567."
          defaultValue="+442071234567"
        />
        <PhoneInput label="Mobile" placeholder="555 123 4567" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-md gap-6">
      <PhoneInput label="Phone number" />
      <PhoneInput label="Emergency contact" defaultValue="+14155552671" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Country dropdown** - A select of curated calling codes with its own accessible name, preceding the number field in tab order.
- **Number field** - A type=tel input that strips non-digits and emits +dial plus national number on every edit.
- **Label** - The visible label, associated with the number field.
- **Help or error text** - Optional description or validation message linked with aria-describedby.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Store the emitted E.164-ish string so numbers stay normalized across regions.
- Prefill existing values; the component parses them back into country and number.
- Validate the final number on submit; the field only normalizes shape.

### Don't

- Don't use it for domestic-only entry; a MaskedInput with the national format is less UI.
- Don't split the value yourself; read the combined string from onChange.

## Interface

### PhoneInput

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | - | Extra description ids, merged with the component's own description. |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` | - | Marks the input invalid for form validation and screen readers. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | - | Initial E.164-ish value when uncontrolled. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Supporting text rendered below the input. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Prevents interaction with both controls. |
| `id` | `string` | - | Explicit id for the number input; otherwise Field or an internal id is used. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Visible label rendered above the input. Required outside a Field; inside a Field the Field's label is used. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the E.164-ish string, or undefined when the number is emptied. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | - | Text shown when the number field is empty. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | Marks the input as required. |
| `value` | `string` | - | Controlled E.164-ish value, e.g. "+14155552671". |

## Accessibility

- The country dropdown has its own accessible name, "Country calling code".
- The visible label points at the number field; the dropdown precedes it in the tab order.
- type="tel" summons a telephone keypad on touch devices.

- [Input](/modules/input)
- [Select](/modules/select)

# Rich Text Editor

A lightweight markdown editor whose toolbar formats the textarea selection, with an optional live preview pane.

## Usage

```js
import { RichTextEditor } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<RichTextEditor
  label="Release notes"
  preview
  defaultValue="## Highlights

- Faster sync for **large workspaces**"
  onChange={(value) => undefined}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Users write formatted long-form text that should stay portable markdown, such as release notes, docs, or issue descriptions.
### Avoid when

Users expect WYSIWYG editing of rich content — that requires a contentEditable framework; for short plain answers use TextArea.
### Behavior

Editing stays in a plain textarea; toolbar actions toggle markdown markers around the selection or at the start of the selected lines and keep the selection usable afterwards.
### Responsive

The toolbar wraps within the editor width; the preview pane stacks below the textarea on narrow screens and sits beside it from md up.

## Examples

### Markdown toolbar

Bold, italic, heading, list, and link actions wrap the current selection with markdown syntax and restore the selection.

```jsx
import { RichTextEditor } from '@kryv/teal'

export function RichTextEditorDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-2xl">
        <RichTextEditor
          label="Release notes"
          preview
          defaultValue={'## Highlights\n\n- Faster sync for **large workspaces**\n- Read the [migration guide](https://example.com)'}
          rows={6}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-lg">
      <RichTextEditor
        label="Update summary"
        placeholder="Write markdown…"
        defaultValue="The toolbar formats the *current selection*."
        rows={6}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Live preview

The preview pane renders headings, lists, links, and inline marks next to the textarea as you type.

```jsx
import { RichTextEditor } from '@kryv/teal'

export function RichTextEditorDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-2xl">
        <RichTextEditor
          label="Release notes"
          preview
          defaultValue={'## Highlights\n\n- Faster sync for **large workspaces**\n- Read the [migration guide](https://example.com)'}
          rows={6}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-lg">
      <RichTextEditor
        label="Update summary"
        placeholder="Write markdown…"
        defaultValue="The toolbar formats the *current selection*."
        rows={6}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Toolbar** - A labelled toolbar of format actions that wrap the current selection with markdown syntax.
- **Textarea** - The plain-text editing surface; the markdown source is the value.
- **Preview pane** - An optional labelled region rendering headings, lists, links, and inline marks as you type.
- **Label** - The visible label associated with the textarea.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Turn on the preview for long-form writing like release notes or docs.
- Store the markdown output as-is so it stays portable.
- Keep the default toolbar; it covers the marks the preview renders.

### Don't

- Don't promise WYSIWYG behavior; editing stays in plain markdown.
- Don't use it for short plain answers; a TextArea is lighter.

## Interface

### RichTextEditor

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` | `string` | - | Accessible name for the text area when there is no visible label. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | - | Initial markdown when uncontrolled. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Visible label rendered above the editor. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the full markdown whenever it changes. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | - | Placeholder text of the text area. |
| `preview` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders a live preview pane next to the text area. |
| `rows` | `number` | `8` | Visible height of the text area in rows. |
| `value` | `string` | - | Controlled markdown. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves between the toolbar buttons and the textarea. |

- Toolbar actions are grouped in a labelled toolbar and each button has an accessible name.
- The preview is a labelled region so screen reader users can skip or inspect the rendered markdown.

# Transfer List

A dual listbox that moves options between an available list and a chosen list with buttons or the keyboard.

## Usage

```js
import { TransferList } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<TransferList
  sourceLabel="Available"
  targetLabel="Selected"
  options={[
    { value: 'design', label: 'Design' },
    { value: 'engineering', label: 'Engineering' },
  ]}
  onValueChange={(values) => undefined}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

The user builds a set from a larger pool and benefits from seeing both states side by side, such as permissions or team skills.
### Avoid when

Only a handful of options exist — checkboxes or a Combobox with multiple are lighter; ordering within the chosen set is not supported.
### Behavior

value always reflects the target list; moves preserve the original option order, and moved items stay selected so they can be sent back immediately.
### Responsive

Both lists flex to share the available width; on narrow screens give the group a min width or stack it in a scrollable container.

## Examples

### Uncontrolled transfer

Click options to select them, then move them with the arrow buttons or Enter.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { TransferList } from '@kryv/teal'

const skills = [
  { value: 'design', label: 'Design' },
  { value: 'engineering', label: 'Engineering' },
  { value: 'marketing', label: 'Marketing' },
  { value: 'operations', label: 'Operations' },
  { value: 'research', label: 'Research' },
]

export function TransferListDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [chosen, setChosen] = useState(['engineering'])

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-lg">
        <TransferList
          aria-label="Team skill picker"
          sourceLabel="Available skills"
          targetLabel="Covered by the team"
          value={chosen}
          onValueChange={setChosen}
          options={skills}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-lg">
      <TransferList options={skills} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Controlled with custom labels

A controlled value seeds the target list and renames both listboxes for the domain.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { TransferList } from '@kryv/teal'

const skills = [
  { value: 'design', label: 'Design' },
  { value: 'engineering', label: 'Engineering' },
  { value: 'marketing', label: 'Marketing' },
  { value: 'operations', label: 'Operations' },
  { value: 'research', label: 'Research' },
]

export function TransferListDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [chosen, setChosen] = useState(['engineering'])

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-lg">
        <TransferList
          aria-label="Team skill picker"
          sourceLabel="Available skills"
          targetLabel="Covered by the team"
          value={chosen}
          onValueChange={setChosen}
          options={skills}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-lg">
      <TransferList options={skills} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Source listbox** - The available options, a multiselectable listbox named by sourceLabel.
- **Target listbox** - The chosen options, whose values are the component's value.
- **Move buttons** - Arrow buttons labelled from the list names; Enter moves the selection too.
- **Option rows** - Clickable, keyboard-selectable rows; moved items stay selected for an immediate send-back.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Name both lists for the domain, such as Available roles and Granted roles.
- Use it when seeing both states side by side helps, like permissions or skills.
- Keep option values stable so moved items keep their original order.

### Don't

- Don't use it for a handful of options; checkboxes or a Combobox with multiple are lighter.
- Don't expect reordering within the target list; order follows the source.

## Interface

### TransferList

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `Transfer list` | Accessible name for the whole transfer group. |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` | - | Initial target values when uncontrolled. |
| `onValueChange` | `(values: string[]) => void` | - | Called with the full list of target values whenever items move. |
| `options` (required) | `TransferListOption[]` | - | All options; those listed in `value` render in the target list. |
| `sourceLabel` | `string` | `Available` | Accessible name of the source list. |
| `targetLabel` | `string` | `Selected` | Accessible name of the target list. |
| `value` | `string[]` | - | Controlled target values. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Arrow Down` + `Arrow Up` | Moves focus within the listbox. |
| `Home` + `End` | Moves focus to the first or last option. |
| `Space` | Toggles selection of the focused option. |
| `Enter` | Moves the selected options (or just the focused one) to the other list. |

- Both lists are listboxes with aria-multiselectable="true" and their own accessible names.
- The move buttons are labelled from the list names and disable while nothing is selected on their side.

## Related modules

- [Combobox](/modules/combobox)
- [Checkbox](/modules/checkbox)
- [List](/modules/list)

# Date Picker

A date field with a keyboard-navigable popover: day, month, year, or datetime modes, plus two-click range selection.

## Usage

```js
import { DatePicker } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<DatePicker label="Start date" onValueChange={(date) => undefined} />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Users pick a calendar date, month, year, timestamp, or date range.
### Avoid when

The value is free-form text; use Input.
### Behavior

mode switches the popover between day, month, year, and datetime panels; selection="range" turns two clicks into {from, to} with presets and a connected band.
### Responsive

The popover collision-handles; the field keeps its layout width.

## Examples

### Calendar selection

Arrows move between days, Enter selects, min and max bound the range.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { DatePicker } from '@kryv/teal'

export function DatePickerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [dueDate, setDueDate] = useState(/** @type {Date | undefined} */ (undefined))
  const [sprintStart, setSprintStart] = useState(new Date())
  const [month, setMonth] = useState(new Date())
  const [year, setYear] = useState(new Date())
  const [startsAt, setStartsAt] = useState(new Date())
  const [range, setRange] = useState(/** @type {{ from: Date | null, to: Date | null } | undefined} */ (undefined))

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    const quarterStart = new Date()
    quarterStart.setDate(quarterStart.getDate() - 14)
    const quarterEnd = new Date()
    quarterEnd.setDate(quarterEnd.getDate() + 60)
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
        <DatePicker
          label="Sprint start"
          description="Limited to the current planning window"
          value={sprintStart}
          onValueChange={(value) => {
            if (value instanceof Date) setSprintStart(value)
          }}
          minDate={quarterStart}
          maxDate={quarterEnd}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
        <DatePicker
          label="Billing month"
          mode="month"
          description="Commits the first of the chosen month"
          value={month}
          onValueChange={(value) => {
            if (value instanceof Date) setMonth(value)
          }}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 3) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
        <DatePicker
          label="Graduation year"
          mode="year"
          description="Commits January 1 of the chosen year"
          value={year}
          onValueChange={(value) => {
            if (value instanceof Date) setYear(value)
          }}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 4) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
        <DatePicker
          label="Starts at"
          mode="datetime"
          description="Day and time in one popover"
          value={startsAt}
          onValueChange={(value) => {
            if (value instanceof Date) setStartsAt(value)
          }}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 5) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
        <DatePicker
          label="Report period"
          selection="range"
          description="Two clicks pick the start and end; presets fill common windows"
          value={range}
          onValueChange={(value) => {
            if (value && !(value instanceof Date)) setRange(value)
          }}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
      <DatePicker
        label="Due date"
        description="Used for the project milestone"
        value={dueDate}
        onValueChange={(value) => {
          if (value === undefined) setDueDate(undefined)
          else if (value instanceof Date) setDueDate(value)
        }}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Range selection

selection="range" turns two clicks into {from, to}, with presets and a connected band between the endpoints.

## Anatomy

- **Field** - The button-like input showing the formatted date.
- **Calendar popover** - The month grid with full keyboard navigation.
- **Month navigation** - Previous and next buttons around an announced month label.
- **Day cells** - Grid buttons bounded by the min and max dates.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Set minDate and maxDate when only a planning window is valid.
- Explain what the date drives, like a milestone, in the description.
- Keep the caller-owned value as a Date, not a string.

### Don't

- Don't stack two pickers for a range; set selection="range".
- Don't expect free-typed input; the calendar is the parser.
- Don't disable dates silently; state the valid window in the description.

## Interface

### DatePicker

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | - | - |
| `aria-label` | `string` | - | Accessible name when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` | - | Marks the input invalid for form validation and screen readers. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `defaultValue` | `Date \| DateRange` | - | Initial selection when uncontrolled. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Supporting text rendered below the input. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Prevents interaction with the input. |
| `hourCycle` | `enum` | `24` | 12 shows a 1–12 hour field with an AM/PM toggle; 24 shows a 0–23 hour field. Only for mode="datetime". |
| `id` | `string` | - | Explicit id; otherwise Field or an internal id is used. |
| `isDateDisabled` | `(date: Date) => boolean` | - | Disables specific days in the calendar grid. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Visible label rendered above the input. Required outside a Field; inside a Field the Field's label is used. |
| `maxDate` | `Date` | - | Latest selectable date (inclusive). |
| `minDate` | `Date` | - | Earliest selectable date (inclusive). |
| `mode` | `enum` | `day` | Picker granularity: 'day' (default), 'month', 'year', or 'datetime' (day grid plus time fields). |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: Date \| DateRange) => void` | - | Called with the selected date, or the range after every selection step. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `Pick a date` | Text shown when nothing is selected. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | Marks the input as required. |
| `selection` | `enum` | `single` | 'single' (default) picks one date; 'range' picks {from, to} (only meaningful with mode="day"). |
| `value` | `Date \| DateRange` | - | Controlled selection. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Arrow Down` | Opens the popover from the field. |
| `Arrow Left` + `Arrow Right` | Moves the focused day by one day; in month or year mode, moves by one month or year. |
| `Arrow Up` + `Arrow Down` | Moves the focused day by one week; in month or year mode, moves by one row. |
| `Home` + `End` | Jumps to the first or last month of the year, or year of the decade page. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Selects the focused day, month, or year; in range mode, picks the start then the end. |

- Day, month, and year buttons use a roving tab index, so each panel is a single Tab stop.
- The month label, visible year, and decade range are announced with aria-live as the view changes.
- Dates outside minDate and maxDate are disabled and cannot be selected.
- Range start and end days expose their state through aria-pressed, and today keeps aria-current date.
- In datetime mode the time fields reuse the TimePicker group with labeled Hour and Minutes inputs, and Done closes the popover.

## Related modules

- [Calendar](/modules/calendar)
- [Time Picker](/modules/time-picker)

# Time Picker

A segmented hour and minute field with 12- and 24-hour cycles.

## Usage

```js
import { TimePicker } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<TimePicker label="Start time" defaultValue="09:30" onChange={(value) => undefined} />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

The user enters a time of day.
### Avoid when

A date or a date range is needed; use DatePicker.
### Behavior

Hour and minute fields clamp while typing; the 12-hour cycle adds a period toggle.
### Responsive

The segmented group stays inline and fits compact forms.

## Examples

### Segmented time

Fields clamp as you type; the 12-hour cycle adds an AM/PM toggle.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { TimePicker } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TimePickerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('09:30')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <TimePicker label="Reminder time" defaultValue="18:45" hourCycle={12} />
        <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">The 12-hour cycle adds an AM/PM toggle.</span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <TimePicker label="Start time" value={value} onChange={setValue} />
      <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Current value: {value}</span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### 12-hour clock

hourCycle={12} swaps the hour range and adds an AM/PM toggle.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { TimePicker } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TimePickerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState('09:30')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid gap-2">
        <TimePicker label="Reminder time" defaultValue="18:45" hourCycle={12} />
        <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">The 12-hour cycle adds an AM/PM toggle.</span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid gap-2">
      <TimePicker label="Start time" value={value} onChange={setValue} />
      <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Current value: {value}</span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Group** - The labeled container with group semantics around the segments.
- **Hour field** - The clamped hour segment labeled Hour.
- **Minute field** - The clamped minute segment labeled Minutes.
- **Period toggle** - The AM/PM switch shown with the 12-hour cycle.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Match hourCycle to the audience's locale.
- Bind a string value like 09:30 and let the segments clamp while typing.
- Pair with DatePicker; its datetime mode covers full timestamps.

### Don't

- Don't use it for durations; use NumberInput with a unit.
- Don't use it for time zones; pair with TimezoneSelect.
- Don't prefill the current time unless now is a sensible default.

## Interface

### TimePicker

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | - | Initial time in "HH:mm" (24h) when uncontrolled. Defaults to "00:00". |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Prevents interaction with every field. |
| `hourCycle` | `enum` | `24` | 12 shows a 1–12 hour field with an AM/PM toggle; 24 shows a 0–23 hour field. |
| `label` | `string` | `Time` | Accessible name for the time field group. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the 24-hour "HH:mm" value after every valid edit. |
| `value` | `string` | - | Controlled time in "HH:mm" (24h). |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus through the hour, minute, and period controls. |
| `Typing` | Edits a segment; values clamp as you type. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Toggles AM or PM on the period buttons. |

- The segments sit in a group named by the field label; the hour and minute inputs are labeled Hour and Minutes.
- The AM/PM toggle reports its state through aria-pressed.
- The 24-hour cycle omits the period control entirely.

## Related modules

- [Date Picker](/modules/date-picker)
- [Timezone Select](/modules/timezone-select)
- [Number Input](/modules/number-input)

# Color Picker

A swatch trigger with preset colors and a validated hex field.

## Usage

```js
import { ColorPicker } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<ColorPicker label="Brand color" defaultValue="#006a6c" onChange={(value) => undefined} />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

The user picks a color from presets or a hex value.
### Avoid when

A full design-token editor is required.
### Behavior

Presets commit immediately; hex input validates and normalizes on Enter or blur.
### Responsive

The trigger fits toolbars; the panel caps at the preset grid width.

## Examples

### Presets and hex

Presets commit immediately; the hex field normalizes #rgb and #rrggbb on Enter or blur.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, ColorPicker } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ColorPickerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [color, setColor] = useState('#006a6c')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <ColorPicker label="Brand color" value={color} onChange={setColor} />
        <span
          className="inline-flex size-10 items-center justify-center rounded-lg border border-teal-outline-variant text-xs font-semibold"
          style={{ backgroundColor: color, color: '#ffffff' }}
        >
          {color}
        </span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <ColorPicker label="Theme color" value={color} onChange={setColor} />
        <Button size="sm" style={{ backgroundColor: color, borderColor: color }}>
          Themed action
        </Button>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return <ColorPicker label="Accent color" defaultValue="#065a60" onChange={() => undefined} />
}
```

### Live preview

A controlled value mirrored on a swatch so the picked color previews in context.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'

          className="inline-flex size-10 items-center justify-center rounded-lg border border-teal-outline-variant text-xs font-semibold"
          style={{ backgroundColor: color, color: '#ffffff' }}
        >
          {color}
        </span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <ColorPicker label="Theme color" value={color} onChange={setColor} />
        <Button size="sm" style={{ backgroundColor: color, borderColor: color }}>
          Themed action
        </Button>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return <ColorPicker label="Accent color" defaultValue="#065a60" onChange={() => undefined} />
}
```

### Controlled color

Pair value with onChange when the color drives other UI.


## Anatomy

- **Trigger** - The swatch button that shows the current color and opens the panel.
- **Preset grid** - Named swatches that commit immediately on activation.
- **Hex field** - The validated input that normalizes #rgb and #rrggbb on Enter or blur.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Name presets so each choice is announced by more than its color.
- Curate presets to the palette users should actually pick from.
- Accept typed hex when brand precision matters.

### Don't

- Don't use it as a theme editor; it is a single-value picker.
- Don't rely on the swatch alone; keep the value text visible for verification.
- Don't reject shorthand hex; normalize it instead of erroring.

## Interface

### ColorPicker

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `Choose color` | Accessible name for the trigger button. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | `#006a6c` | Initial hex color when uncontrolled. Defaults to the teal primary. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Prevents opening the picker. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the normalized "#rrggbb" value after every selection. |
| `value` | `string` | - | Controlled hex color value. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Opens the panel from the swatch trigger, or commits the focused preset. |
| `Tab` | Moves focus through the preset swatches and the hex field. |
| `Enter` | Normalizes and commits the typed hex value. |

- Every preset swatch has its name applied as an aria-label and reports selection through aria-pressed.
- The preset grid is a labeled group and the swatch preview is decorative.
- Invalid hex input marks the field aria-invalid and does not commit.

# Timezone Select

A searchable select over a curated set of IANA timezones with UTC offset labels.

## Usage

```js
import { TimezoneSelect } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<TimezoneSelect
  label="Workspace time zone"
  value={zone}
  onValueChange={setZone}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

People schedule or display times across regions and need a recognizable zone with its offset visible.
### Avoid when

The full IANA database is required; this curated list covers common zones, so build on Combobox with custom options instead.
### Behavior

Filtering matches the city label, selection reports the IANA zone id, and the input shows the city with its UTC offset.
### Responsive

The input fills its container and the option list overlays below it at the same width.

## Examples

### Searchable timezone list

Typing a city name filters roughly thirty common IANA zones, each labeled with its current UTC offset.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { TimezoneSelect } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TimezoneSelectDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [zone, setZone] = useState('America/New_York')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xs space-y-2">
        <TimezoneSelect
          label="Workspace time zone"
          description="Used for scheduling across the team"
          value={zone}
          onValueChange={setZone}
        />
        <p className="text-sm text-on-surface-variant">Selected: {zone}</p>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
      <TimezoneSelect
        label="Event time zone"
        description="Type a city name to filter the list"
        defaultValue="Europe/London"
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Controlled selection

The value is the IANA zone id, so it can be stored directly and shown back to the user.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { TimezoneSelect } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TimezoneSelectDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [zone, setZone] = useState('America/New_York')

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xs space-y-2">
        <TimezoneSelect
          label="Workspace time zone"
          description="Used for scheduling across the team"
          value={zone}
          onValueChange={setZone}
        />
        <p className="text-sm text-on-surface-variant">Selected: {zone}</p>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
      <TimezoneSelect
        label="Event time zone"
        description="Type a city name to filter the list"
        defaultValue="Europe/London"
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Combobox input** - The filterable field, built on Combobox, that shows the chosen city with its UTC offset.
- **Option list** - Roughly thirty curated IANA zones, each labeled with its current offset.
- **Selected value** - The IANA zone id, such as Europe/Berlin, emitted for direct storage.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Store the IANA id, not the offset; offsets change with daylight saving.
- Default to the detected zone so most users never open the list.
- Keep offsets visible to disambiguate cities that share a name.

### Don't

- Don't use it when the full IANA database is required; build on Combobox with custom options.
- Don't sort or label zones by fixed offsets; labels follow the current offset.

## Interface

### TimezoneSelect

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-describedby` | `string` | - | - |
| `aria-label` | `string` | - | Accessible name when there is no visible label. |
| `aria-invalid` | `boolean \| "true" \| "false"` | - | Marks the input invalid for form validation and screen readers. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | - | Initial IANA zone id when uncontrolled. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Supporting text rendered below the input. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | - | Prevents interaction with the input. |
| `emptyMessage` | `ReactNode` | `No matching time zones` | Message shown when no timezone matches the typed text. |
| `id` | `string` | - | Explicit id; otherwise Field or an internal id is used. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Visible label rendered above the input. Required outside a Field; inside a Field the Field's label is used. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the IANA zone id of the selected timezone. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | `Select a time zone` | Text shown when no timezone is selected. |
| `required` | `boolean` | - | Marks the input as required. |
| `value` | `string` | - | Controlled IANA zone id, e.g. "America/New_York". |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Arrow Down` | Opens the list or moves the highlight to the next option. |
| `Arrow Up` | Moves the highlight to the previous option. |
| `Enter` | Selects the highlighted option. |
| `Escape` | Closes the list and restores the selected label. |

- The input is an aria-expanded combobox with aria-activedescendant pointing at the highlighted option.
- Each option's accessible name includes the city and its UTC offset.

## Related modules

- [Combobox](/modules/combobox)
- [Select](/modules/select)
- [Date Picker](/modules/date-picker)

# Tree Select

A single-select control whose popover shows an expandable, typeahead-enabled tree of options; display="columns" walks the hierarchy one column per level.

## Usage

```js
import { TreeSelect } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<TreeSelect
  label="Office"
  options={[
    { value: 'emea', label: 'EMEA', children: [{ value: 'berlin', label: 'Berlin' }] },
    { value: 'singapore', label: 'Singapore' },
  ]}
  onValueChange={(value) => undefined}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Users pick one value from a hierarchy where intermediate grouping helps orientation, such as regions, folders, or org units.
### Avoid when

The option set is flat or small — use Select; if the user needs to drill through many levels, display="columns" scans faster.
### Behavior

Branch nodes only expand or collapse; leaf nodes commit a single value, close the popover, and render their label in the trigger.
### Responsive

The popover matches the trigger width and the tree scrolls vertically; deep levels indent rather than widen the control.

## Examples

### Basic tree select

Branches expand and collapse; only leaf nodes commit the selection.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { TreeSelect } from '@kryv/teal'

const locations = [
  {
    value: 'emea',
    label: 'EMEA',
    children: [
      { value: 'berlin', label: 'Berlin' },
      { value: 'lisbon', label: 'Lisbon' },
    ],
  },
  {
    value: 'americas',
    label: 'Americas',
    children: [
      { value: 'nyc', label: 'New York' },
      { value: 'sao-paulo', label: 'São Paulo' },
      { value: 'remote', label: 'Remote hub', disabled: true },
    ],
  },
  { value: 'singapore', label: 'Singapore' },
]

const teams = [
  {
    value: 'engineering',
    label: 'Engineering',
    children: [
      { value: 'frontend', label: 'Frontend' },
      { value: 'backend', label: 'Backend' },
      { value: 'platform', label: 'Platform' },
    ],
  },
  {
    value: 'design',
    label: 'Design',
    children: [
      { value: 'product', label: 'Product Design' },
      { value: 'research', label: 'Research' },
    ],
  },
  { value: 'operations', label: 'Operations' },
]

export function TreeSelectDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [office, setOffice] = useState('lisbon')
  const [path, setPath] = useState(['engineering', 'backend'])

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
        <TreeSelect
          label="Office"
          description="Regional offices only; hubs are not assignable"
          defaultExpandedValues={['americas']}
          value={office}
          onValueChange={(value) => {
            if (typeof value === 'string') setOffice(value)
          }}
          options={locations}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
        <TreeSelect
          label="Owning team"
          display="columns"
          description="The full path from department to team"
          value={path}
          onValueChange={(value) => {
            if (Array.isArray(value)) setPath(value)
          }}
          options={teams}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
      <TreeSelect label="Office" placeholder="Pick an office…" options={locations} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Controlled with pre-expanded branches

A controlled value is revealed and highlighted on open; disabled nodes stay visible but cannot be chosen.

### Columns display

display="columns" renders one labelled column per level; choosing a leaf commits the full path of values.
