```jsx
function artwork(label, from, to) {
  const svg = `<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='960' height='600'><defs><linearGradient id='g' x1='0' y1='0' x2='1' y2='1'><stop offset='0' stop-color='${from}'/><stop offset='1' stop-color='${to}'/></linearGradient></defs><rect width='960' height='600' fill='url(#g)'/><text x='480' y='310' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='44' fill='rgba(255,255,255,0.9)' text-anchor='middle'>${label}</text></svg>`
  return `data:image/svg+xml,${encodeURIComponent(svg)}`
}

const images = [
  { src: artwork('Aurora study', '#0f766e', '#22d3ee'), alt: 'Aurora study artwork', caption: 'Aurora study — gradient draft' },
  { src: artwork('Canyon dusk', '#9a3412', '#f59e0b'), alt: 'Canyon dusk artwork' },
  { src: artwork('Tide pools', '#1d4ed8', '#67e8f9'), alt: 'Tide pools artwork', caption: 'Tide pools, exported at 960×600' },
]

export function LightboxDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [index, setIndex] = useState(0)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-3">
        {images.map((image, i) => (
          <button
            key={image.alt}
            type="button"
            aria-label={`Open ${image.alt}`}
            onClick={() => {
              setIndex(i)
              setOpen(true)
            }}
            className="overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-teal-outline-variant/50"
          >
            <img src={image.src} alt="" className="h-16 w-24 object-cover" />
          </button>
        ))}
        <Lightbox open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} images={images} index={index} onIndexChange={setIndex} label="Artwork gallery" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>View gallery</Button>
      <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Arrow keys move between images, Escape closes.</span>
      <Lightbox open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} images={images} label="Artwork gallery" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Overlay** - The full-screen dialog surface that dims the page and traps focus while open.
- **Image stage** - The current image, scaled to fit the viewport, with its alt and optional caption.
- **Prev/next controls** - Chevron buttons that mirror the arrow keys and wrap around the ends.
- **Counter** - The live "n of m" indicator tracking the current position.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Give every image meaningful alt text and a short caption where it adds context.
- Open at the clicked thumbnail's index via the controlled index prop.
- Let the overlay own paging; arrow keys and buttons stay in sync.

### Don't

- Don't use a lightbox for a single image that needs zoom inspection; use ImageViewer.
- Don't write long prose captions; keep them to a short label.
- Don't hide the close path; Escape and the backdrop always close it.

## Interface

### Lightbox

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `Close` | Accessible label for the close button. |
| `defaultIndex` | `number` | `0` | Initial image index when uncontrolled. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | - | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `images` (required) | `LightboxImage[]` | - | Images shown in gallery order. |
| `index` | `number` | - | Controlled index of the visible image. |
| `label` | `string` | `Image gallery` | Accessible name of the gallery dialog. |
| `onIndexChange` | `(index: number) => void` | - | Called when the visible image changes. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Called when the lightbox opens or closes. |
| `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Arrow Right` | Shows the next image, wrapping past the last. |
| `Arrow Left` | Shows the previous image, wrapping before the first. |
| `Home` | Jumps to the first image. |
| `End` | Jumps to the last image. |
| `Escape` | Closes the lightbox. |

- Rendered as a labelled dialog that traps focus while open.
- The position counter ('3 of 8') is announced via a polite live region.
- Images always require alt text supplied by the caller.

- [Image Viewer](/modules/image-viewer)
- [Dialog](/modules/dialog)

# Notification Center

Popover panel that lists recent notifications with read states and a mark-all-read action.

## Usage

```js
import { NotificationCenter } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<NotificationCenter
  trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Notifications</Button>}
  items={notifications}
  onMarkAllRead={markAllRead}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A product aggregates events from several sources behind a single bell-style entry point, such as deploys, comments, and billing alerts.
### Avoid when

A single transient update; use Toast or Alert instead of an inbox.
### Behavior

Rows reuse NotificationItem; the panel never mutates the items — read state changes are reported through onMarkAllRead for the caller to apply.
### Responsive

The panel caps at 24rem and narrows to the viewport on small screens, with the list scrolling internally.

## Examples

### Inbox with unread items

Unread rows stay emphasized and the mark-all-read action appears only while unread items remain.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, NotificationCenter } from '@kryv/teal'

/** @type {import('@kryv/teal').NotificationCenterItem[]} */
const initialItems = [
  { id: '1', title: 'Deploy finished', appLabel: 'Orion', timestamp: '2 min ago', href: '#', severity: 'success' },
  { id: '2', title: 'Quota almost reached', appLabel: 'Billing', timestamp: '1 hour ago', href: '#', severity: 'warning' },
  { id: '3', title: 'New comment on PR 17', appLabel: 'Forge', timestamp: 'Yesterday', href: '#', read: true },
]

export function NotificationCenterDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [items, setItems] = useState(initialItems)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <NotificationCenter
          trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Notifications</Button>}
          items={[]}
          onMarkAllRead={() => {}}
        />
        <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">An empty center shows the catch-up message.</span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <NotificationCenter
        trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Notifications</Button>}
        items={items}
        onMarkAllRead={() => setItems((current) => current.map((item) => ({ ...item, read: true })))}
      />
      <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Unread rows stay emphasized until marked read.</span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Empty center

With no notifications the panel shows a catch-up message instead of a list.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, NotificationCenter } from '@kryv/teal'

/** @type {import('@kryv/teal').NotificationCenterItem[]} */
const initialItems = [
  { id: '1', title: 'Deploy finished', appLabel: 'Orion', timestamp: '2 min ago', href: '#', severity: 'success' },
  { id: '2', title: 'Quota almost reached', appLabel: 'Billing', timestamp: '1 hour ago', href: '#', severity: 'warning' },
  { id: '3', title: 'New comment on PR 17', appLabel: 'Forge', timestamp: 'Yesterday', href: '#', read: true },
]

export function NotificationCenterDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [items, setItems] = useState(initialItems)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <NotificationCenter
          trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Notifications</Button>}
          items={[]}
          onMarkAllRead={() => {}}
        />
        <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">An empty center shows the catch-up message.</span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <NotificationCenter
        trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Notifications</Button>}
        items={items}
        onMarkAllRead={() => setItems((current) => current.map((item) => ({ ...item, read: true })))}
      />
      <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Unread rows stay emphasized until marked read.</span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Trigger** - The caller-supplied button, often a bell icon, that opens the panel.
- **Panel** - The popover surface listing notifications, capped in width with internal scrolling.
- **Notification rows** - NotificationItem rows with read state emphasis for unread items.
- **Mark-all-read** - An action shown only while unread items remain; the caller applies the change via onMarkAllRead.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Keep items sanitized pointers to source events, with severity and app labels.
- Apply onMarkAllRead in caller state so read changes persist.
- Show the empty state message instead of an empty list when nothing remains.

### Don't

- Don't mutate the source events from the panel; it reports intent only.
- Don't use it for transient feedback; use Toast.
- Don't let the list grow unbounded; trim to recent notifications.

## Interface

### NotificationCenter

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `enum` | `end` | Horizontal alignment of the panel relative to the trigger. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | - | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `emptyMessage` | `ReactNode` | `You're all caught up` | Content shown when there are no notifications. |
| `items` (required) | `NotificationCenterItem[]` | - | Notifications listed newest first. |
| `label` | `string` | `Notifications` | Accessible name of the popover panel. |
| `markAllReadLabel` | `string` | `Mark all as read` | Accessible label of the mark-all-read action. |
| `onMarkAllRead` | `() => void` | - | Renders the mark-all-read action and calls this when pressed. Never mutates the items. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Called when the panel opens or closes. |
| `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state. |
| `side` | `enum` | `bottom` | Side of the trigger the panel opens on. |
| `trigger` (required) | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` | - | Element that toggles the panel; receives trigger props automatically. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Escape` | Closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger. |

- The panel is a labelled popover and the notifications form a labelled list.
- Unread rows append an 'unread' marker to the link's accessible name.

## Related modules

- [Notification Item](/modules/notification-item)
- [Popover](/modules/popover)
- [Toast](/modules/toast)

# Prompt Dialog

A modal dialog with a single labeled input that returns the entered value on confirm.

## Usage

```js
import { PromptDialog } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<PromptDialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title="Rename report"
  label="Report name"
  defaultValue="Q3 revenue"
  onSubmit={(value) => rename(value)}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Quick single-value captures like renaming, creating folders, or tagging, where a full form would be overkill.
### Avoid when

Multiple fields or validation-heavy input; compose a Dialog with Field components instead.
### Behavior

Confirm (or Enter) calls onSubmit with the entered value and closes; cancel and Escape close without submitting.
### Responsive

A compact centered dialog capped to the viewport width with comfortable margins on small screens.

## Examples

### Rename flow

The input is prefilled with the current value and focused on open.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, PromptDialog } from '@kryv/teal'

export function PromptDialogDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [value, setValue] = useState('')
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>{exampleIndex ? 'Create folder' : 'Rename report'}</Button>
      {value ? <p className="mt-3 text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Submitted: {value}</p> : null}
      <PromptDialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title={exampleIndex ? 'Create folder' : 'Rename report'}
        description={
          exampleIndex ? 'The folder is created inside the current workspace.' : 'The new name appears everywhere the report is shared.'
        }
        label={exampleIndex ? 'Folder name' : 'Report name'}
        defaultValue={exampleIndex ? '' : 'Q3 revenue'}
        placeholder={exampleIndex ? 'e.g. Board materials' : undefined}
        confirmLabel={exampleIndex ? 'Create' : 'Rename'}
        onSubmit={(next) => setValue(next)}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

### Create flow

An empty input with a placeholder collects a brand-new name.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, PromptDialog } from '@kryv/teal'

export function PromptDialogDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [value, setValue] = useState('')
  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>{exampleIndex ? 'Create folder' : 'Rename report'}</Button>
      {value ? <p className="mt-3 text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">Submitted: {value}</p> : null}
      <PromptDialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        title={exampleIndex ? 'Create folder' : 'Rename report'}
        description={
          exampleIndex ? 'The folder is created inside the current workspace.' : 'The new name appears everywhere the report is shared.'
        }
        label={exampleIndex ? 'Folder name' : 'Report name'}
        defaultValue={exampleIndex ? '' : 'Q3 revenue'}
        placeholder={exampleIndex ? 'e.g. Board materials' : undefined}
        confirmLabel={exampleIndex ? 'Create' : 'Rename'}
        onSubmit={(next) => setValue(next)}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Title** - The verb-led heading that names the dialog, like "Rename report".
- **Input** - The single labeled text field, focused on open and optionally prefilled with defaultValue.
- **Confirm and cancel** - The action pair; confirm or Enter submits the value, cancel and Escape discard it.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Prefill defaultValue when editing an existing name so users adjust rather than retype.
- Use a verb-led title and a visible input label, not placeholder-only naming.
- Validate the submitted value in onSubmit and give feedback on empty or invalid input.

### Don't

- Don't use it for multi-field or validation-heavy forms; compose Dialog with Field instead.
- Don't submit on behalf of the user; Enter is the only implicit submit.
- Don't reuse one prompt for unrelated actions; keep one intent per dialog.

## Interface

### PromptDialog

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cancelLabel` | `string` | `Cancel` | Text of the cancel button. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `confirmLabel` | `string` | `Confirm` | Text of the confirm button. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | - | Initial open state when uncontrolled. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | - | Initial input value; restored each time the dialog opens. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Supporting text rendered under the title. |
| `label` (required) | `string` | - | Label of the input. |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` | - | Called when the cancel button is pressed. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | - | Called when the dialog opens or closes. |
| `onSubmit` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the entered value when the dialog is confirmed. |
| `open` | `boolean` | - | Controlled open state. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | - | Placeholder of the input. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Title rendered at the top; also the accessible name of the dialog. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` | Submits the entered value and closes the dialog. |
| `Escape` | Closes the dialog without submitting. |
| `Tab` | Moves focus between the input and the footer buttons. |

- Renders with role="dialog" named by its title; the input is associated with a visible label.
- The input receives focus automatically when the dialog opens.

## Related modules

- [Dialog](/modules/dialog)
- [Alert Dialog](/modules/alert-dialog)
- [Field](/modules/field)

# Toast

Imperative, announced feedback with semantic variants, optional actions, and dismissal.

## Usage

```js
import { Toaster, toast } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
// Mount once near the app root
<Toaster />

// Call toast() from anywhere
toast({ title: 'Changes saved', variant: 'success' })
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A completed or failed action needs brief asynchronous feedback.
### Avoid when

The message is required to continue or must be read in context.
### Behavior

Toaster announces messages and supports timed or manual dismissal.
### Responsive

Position toasts away from mobile browser controls and safe areas.

## Examples

### Saving feedback

Call toast() from anywhere once a Toaster is mounted near the app root.

```jsx
import { Button, toast } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ToastDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Button
        onClick={() =>
          toast({
            title: 'Report failed to save',
            description: 'Check your connection, then try saving again.',
            variant: 'danger',
          })
        }
      >
        Show failure toast
      </Button>
    )
  }
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <Button
        onClick={() =>
          toast({
            title: 'Report archived',
            description: 'The report moved to the archive.',
            variant: 'success',
            action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => {} },
          })
        }
      >
        Show undo toast
      </Button>
    )
  }
  return (
    <Button
      onClick={() =>
        toast({ title: 'Changes saved', description: 'Your settings are up to date.', variant: 'success' })
      }
    >
      Show toast
    </Button>
  )
}
```

### Failure feedback

Use a danger variant for a failed action and keep the recovery path in context.

```jsx
import { Button, toast } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ToastDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Button
        onClick={() =>
          toast({
            title: 'Report failed to save',
            description: 'Check your connection, then try saving again.',
            variant: 'danger',
          })
        }
      >
        Show failure toast
      </Button>
    )
  }
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <Button
        onClick={() =>
          toast({
            title: 'Report archived',
            description: 'The report moved to the archive.',
            variant: 'success',
            action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => {} },
          })
        }
      >
        Show undo toast
      </Button>
    )
  }
  return (
    <Button
      onClick={() =>
        toast({ title: 'Changes saved', description: 'Your settings are up to date.', variant: 'success' })
      }
    >
      Show toast
    </Button>
  )
}
```

### Undo feedback

Offer a short action when users may want to reverse a completed operation.

```jsx
import { Button, toast } from '@kryv/teal'

export function ToastDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Button
        onClick={() =>
          toast({
            title: 'Report failed to save',
            description: 'Check your connection, then try saving again.',
            variant: 'danger',
          })
        }
      >
        Show failure toast
      </Button>
    )
  }
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <Button
        onClick={() =>
          toast({
            title: 'Report archived',
            description: 'The report moved to the archive.',
            variant: 'success',
            action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: () => {} },
          })
        }
      >
        Show undo toast
      </Button>
    )
  }
  return (
    <Button
      onClick={() =>
        toast({ title: 'Changes saved', description: 'Your settings are up to date.', variant: 'success' })
      }
    >
      Show toast
    </Button>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Toaster viewport** - Fixed container mounted once near the app root; stacks incoming toasts and owns their live region.
- **Toast** - The announced surface carrying the message; auto-dismisses after its duration unless made persistent.
- **Variant icon** - Decorative severity glyph matched to the neutral, info, success, warning, or danger variant.
- **Title and description** - The message text; the title is required and the description carries detail.
- **Action and close** - An optional action button plus a labeled dismiss control.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Mount exactly one Toaster near the app root so every toast() call shares it.
- Match the variant to the outcome, such as success for a completed save.
- Pass duration: Infinity for messages the user must not miss, and pair them with an action.

### Don't

- Don't toast information the user must act on later; use Alert so it stays in context.
- Don't fire several toasts for one operation; collapse retries into a single final message.
- Don't put long copy in a toast; keep the title to a phrase and move detail into the description.

## Interface

### Toaster

_This module forwards native element properties._

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `F8` | Moves focus to the toast viewport so toasts can be reviewed and dismissed. |
| `Escape` | Dismisses the focused toast. |
| `Swipe right` | Dismisses a toast on touch devices. |

- Toasts are announced through a live region as they appear.
- Actions render as real buttons with accessible labels.
- Pass duration: Infinity for critical messages that must be dismissed manually.

## Related modules

- [Alert](/modules/alert)
- [Announcer](/modules/announcer)

# Empty State

An explanatory empty result with an optional action and SVG icon.

## Usage

```js
import { EmptyState, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<EmptyState
  title="No reports"
  description="Create a report to begin tracking results."
  action={<Button>Create report</Button>}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A product surface has no results or has not been configured.
### Avoid when

Content is merely loading or filtered temporarily.
### Behavior

Explain what happened and give one clear next action when useful.
### Responsive

Keep the message readable and center the action beneath it.

## Examples

### First-run

Pair a short explanation with a single primary action.

```jsx
import { Button, EmptyState } from '@kryv/teal'

export function EmptyStateDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <EmptyState
        title="No matching reports"
        description="No reports match the current filters. Adjust or clear them to see more results."
        action={<Button variant="secondary">Clear filters</Button>}
        className="w-full max-w-lg"
      />
    )
  }
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-10">
        <EmptyState
          status="404"
          title="Route not found"
          description="The link may be outdated or the page removed."
          action={<Button variant="secondary">Back to dashboard</Button>}
        />
        <EmptyState
          status="403"
          title="Access restricted"
          description="You need the security role to open this area."
          action={<Button variant="secondary">Request access</Button>}
        />
        <EmptyState
          status="500"
          title="Something went wrong"
          description="The server hit an unexpected error while loading the report."
          action={<Button variant="secondary">Retry request</Button>}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <EmptyState
      title="No reports"
      description="Create a report to begin tracking results."
      action={<Button>Create report</Button>}
      className="w-full max-w-lg"
    />
  )
}
```

### Filtered empty result

Explain that filters produced no results and offer a way to adjust them.

```jsx
import { Button, EmptyState } from '@kryv/teal'

export function EmptyStateDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <EmptyState
        title="No matching reports"
        description="No reports match the current filters. Adjust or clear them to see more results."
        action={<Button variant="secondary">Clear filters</Button>}
        className="w-full max-w-lg"

    )
  }

    return (

        <EmptyState
          status="404"

          description="The link may be outdated or the page removed."
          action={<Button variant="secondary">Back to dashboard</Button>}
        />
        <EmptyState
          status="403"
          title="Access restricted"
          description="You need the security role to open this area."
          action={<Button variant="secondary">Request access</Button>}
        />
        <EmptyState
          status="500"
          title="Something went wrong"
          description="The server hit an unexpected error while loading the report."
          action={<Button variant="secondary">Retry request</Button>}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <EmptyState
      title="No reports"
      description="Create a report to begin tracking results."
      action={<Button>Create report</Button>}
      className="w-full max-w-lg"
    />
  )
}
```

### Status outcomes

Pass status to show a standard icon and tint for success, error, warning, info, or HTTP outcomes like 404.

```jsx
import { Button, EmptyState } from '@kryv/teal'

export function EmptyStateDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <EmptyState
        title="No matching reports"
        description="No reports match the current filters. Adjust or clear them to see more results."
        action={<Button variant="secondary">Clear filters</Button>}
        className="w-full max-w-lg"
      />
    )
  }
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-10">
        <EmptyState
          status="404"
          title="Route not found"
          description="The link may be outdated or the page removed."
          action={<Button variant="secondary">Back to dashboard</Button>}
        />
        <EmptyState
          status="403"
          title="Access restricted"
          description="You need the security role to open this area."
          action={<Button variant="secondary">Request access</Button>}
        />
        <EmptyState
          status="500"
          title="Something went wrong"
          description="The server hit an unexpected error while loading the report."
          action={<Button variant="secondary">Retry request</Button>}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <EmptyState
      title="No reports"
      description="Create a report to begin tracking results."
      action={<Button>Create report</Button>}
      className="w-full max-w-lg"
    />
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Icon well** - Rounded container holding a decorative SVG icon; hidden from assistive technology.
- **Title** - Heading naming the empty condition; renders h3 by default and adjusts with titleAs.
- **Description** - Short explanation of why the surface is empty and what happens next.
- **Action** - Caller-supplied next step, usually a single primary Button.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Lead with what happened, then offer one clear next action.
- Distinguish a first-run empty surface from a filtered no-results state in the copy.

### Don't

- Don't use an empty state while content is still loading; use Skeleton or LoadingState.
- Don't stack several competing actions under one empty state.

## Interface

### EmptyState

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | - | Call to action rendered below the description. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | - | Supporting text that explains the empty state. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon rendered above the title. Overrides the status's standard icon. |
| `status` | `enum` | - | Outcome status; picks the default icon and its tint. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Short heading for the empty state. |
| `titleAs` | `enum` | `"h3"` | Heading element used for the title; defaults to 'h3'. Adjust to fit the page outline. |

## Accessibility

- The title renders as an h3 by default; adjust titleAs so the empty state fits the page outline.
- The action is a real button or link; keep to a single primary action.
- The status icon is always aria-hidden, including custom icon overrides; the title and description carry the meaning.

- [Loading](/modules/loading)
- [Alert](/modules/alert)

# Loading

Named progress and loading treatments for local, skeleton, and full-surface states.

## Usage

```js
import { Spinner, Progress, Skeleton, LoadingState } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Spinner label="Saving" />
<Progress label="Import progress" value={64} />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-40" />
<LoadingState label="Loading reports" />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Users need feedback while content or work is in progress.
### Avoid when

The operation is instant or no meaningful progress exists.
### Behavior

Use Spinner for local work, Skeleton for layout, and Progress for measurable work.
### Responsive

Prefer local indicators so small screens retain useful content.

## Examples

### Loading treatments

Spinner and Progress for active work, Skeleton for layout placeholders, LoadingState for regions.

```jsx
import { LoadingState, Progress, Skeleton, Spinner } from '@kryv/teal'

export function LoadingDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-4">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <Skeleton className="h-10 w-10 rounded-full" />
          <div className="grid flex-1 gap-2">
            <Skeleton className="h-3 w-2/5" />
            <Skeleton className="h-3 w-3/5" />
          </div>
        </div>
        <Skeleton className="h-24 w-full" />
        <Skeleton className="h-3 w-4/5" />
        <Skeleton className="h-3 w-3/5" />
      </div>
    )
  }
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <Progress shape="circle" value={64} label="Import progress" />
        <Progress shape="circle" size={72} strokeWidth={7} value={82} label="Storage used" />
        <Progress shape="circle" size={72} strokeWidth={7} label="Syncing files" />
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-5">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-5">
        <Spinner label="Loading example" />
        <Progress label="Import progress" value={64} />
      </div>
      <Skeleton className="h-20 w-full" />
      <LoadingState label="Loading reports" className="min-h-32" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Skeleton composition

Skeleton blocks mirror the shape of the incoming content.

```jsx
import { LoadingState, Progress, Skeleton, Spinner } from '@kryv/teal'

    )
  }

    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <Progress shape="circle" value={64} label="Import progress" />
        <Progress shape="circle" size={72} strokeWidth={7} value={82} label="Storage used" />

```

### Radial progress

shape="circle" gives Progress a compact radial treatment; omit value for a spinning indeterminate arc.

```jsx

```

### Skeleton region

Reserve the eventual layout with Skeleton when content shape is known.

```jsx
import { LoadingState, Progress, Skeleton, Spinner } from '@kryv/teal'

export function LoadingDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-4">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
          <Skeleton className="h-10 w-10 rounded-full" />
          <div className="grid flex-1 gap-2">
            <Skeleton className="h-3 w-2/5" />
            <Skeleton className="h-3 w-3/5" />
          </div>
        </div>
        <Skeleton className="h-24 w-full" />
        <Skeleton className="h-3 w-4/5" />
        <Skeleton className="h-3 w-3/5" />
      </div>
    )
  }
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <Progress shape="circle" value={64} label="Import progress" />
        <Progress shape="circle" size={72} strokeWidth={7} value={82} label="Storage used" />
        <Progress shape="circle" size={72} strokeWidth={7} label="Syncing files" />
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-5">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-5">
        <Spinner label="Loading example" />
        <Progress label="Import progress" value={64} />
      </div>
      <Skeleton className="h-20 w-full" />
      <LoadingState label="Loading reports" className="min-h-32" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Spinner** - role="status" glyph with an accessible label for local, short waits.
- **Progress** - Determinate bar that exposes aria-valuenow for measurable work.
- **Skeleton** - aria-hidden placeholder block that reserves the shape of incoming content.
- **LoadingState** - Centered role="status" treatment that stands in for a whole region or panel.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Match the treatment to the wait: Skeleton when the layout is known, Progress when it is measurable.
- Give Spinner and LoadingState a label that names the work, such as "Saving".

### Don't

- Don't show a spinner for operations that usually resolve instantly; it reads as flicker.
- Don't layer Skeleton and Spinner over the same region at once.

## Interface

### LoadingState

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `Loading` | Accessible label announced by screen readers while the region is loading. |

### Spinner

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `Loading` | Accessible label announced by screen readers. |
| `size` | `enum` | `48` | Diameter of the spinner. |

### Skeleton

_This module forwards native element properties._

### Progress

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `string` | `Loading` | Accessible label describing what the progress bar measures. |
| `shape` | `enum` | `bar` | Visual treatment: a linear bar, or a radial circle that spins when `value` is omitted. |
| `size` | `number` | `48` | Diameter of the circle in pixels. Only applies when `shape="circle"`. |
| `strokeWidth` | `number` | `5` | Width of the track and fill strokes in pixels. Only applies when `shape="circle"`. |
| `asChild` | `boolean` | - | Merges the component onto its child element instead of rendering the default element (Radix Slot). |
| `value` | `number \| null` | `0` | Current progress, clamped between 0 and max. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | Maximum value used to compute the filled percentage. |

## Accessibility

- Spinner and LoadingState render role="status" with an accessible label, announced once to screen readers.
- Progress exposes aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax through the Radix progress primitive; shape="circle" renders the same progressbar semantics as a radial arc, with the centered percentage aria-hidden because the progressbar value already carries it.
- Skeleton is aria-hidden because it duplicates content that is about to load.
- All motion respects prefers-reduced-motion.

- [Loading Bar](/modules/loading-bar)
- [Blocking Overlay](/modules/blocking-overlay)
- [Meter](/modules/meter)

# Alert

An inline feedback surface with semantic variants, an optional title, and dismissal; appearance renders it as a raised surface, a page-level banner strip, or a presentational callout.

## Usage

```js
import { Alert, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Alert variant="warning" title="Payment method expiring">
  The workspace card ends in 04/25. Update billing details to avoid interruption.
</Alert>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Feedback must stay visible in context until it is read or dismissed.
### Avoid when

A brief confirmation is enough; use a toast for transient feedback.
### Behavior

Danger renders role="alert" for immediate announcement; other variants render role="status". appearance="callout" renders no live region and stays in the reading flow.
### Responsive

Let the body text wrap and keep the title to a short phrase.

## Examples

### Variants

Semantic variants pair a standard icon with a matching surface treatment.

```jsx
import { Alert, Button } from '@kryv/teal'

export function AlertDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Alert
        variant="warning"
        title="Payment method expiring"
        onDismiss={() => undefined}
        className="w-full max-w-lg"
      >
        The workspace card ends in 04/25. Update billing details to avoid interruption.
      </Alert>
    )
  }
  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-2xl gap-3">
        <Alert appearance="banner" variant="info" title="Scheduled maintenance">
          The workspace will be read-only on Sunday from 02:00 to 03:00 UTC.
        </Alert>
        <Alert
          appearance="banner"
          variant="warning"
          title="Trial ends in 7 days"
          action={<Button size="sm">Upgrade plan</Button>}
          onDismiss={() => undefined}
        >
          Upgrade to keep unlimited projects and priority support for the whole workspace.
        </Alert>
      </div>
    )
  }
  if (exampleIndex === 3) {
    return (
      <div className="flex w-full max-w-xl flex-col gap-4">
        <Alert appearance="callout" title="Heads up">
          New pricing starts next month. Your current plan is locked in until the end of the billing cycle.
        </Alert>
        <Alert appearance="callout" accent={false} variant="warning" title="Trial ending soon">
          Your trial ends in 5 days. Add a payment method to keep your workspace active.
        </Alert>
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-3">
      <Alert variant="success" title="Report published">
        The quarterly security report is now available to all workspace members.
      </Alert>
      <Alert variant="danger" title="Sign-in blocked">
        We stopped a sign-in attempt from an unrecognized device.
      </Alert>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Dismissible

Pass onDismiss to render a close button for feedback the user can clear.


### Banner appearance

appearance="banner" renders a full-width page-level strip with an optional trailing action.


### Callout appearance

appearance="callout" stays in the reading flow with a left accent bar; pass accent={false} to hide it.

```jsx
import { Alert, Button } from '@kryv/teal'

      </Alert>
    </div>

```

## Anatomy

- **Variant icon** - Decorative severity glyph, hidden from assistive technology; not rendered for the banner appearance.
- **Title** - Optional bold lead-in naming the condition.
- **Body** - The explanatory message; wraps within the surface.
- **Action** - Caller-supplied trailing control, such as a Button.
- **Dismiss** - Optional labeled IconButton rendered when onDismiss is passed.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Keep the alert mounted until the condition resolves or the user dismisses it.
- Use the danger variant for failures that need immediate attention; it announces assertively.
- Use appearance="banner" for workspace-wide conditions and appearance="callout" for quiet guidance that should not announce itself.

### Don't

- Don't use Alert for brief confirmations; use Toast instead.
- Don't rely on the icon or color alone; the text must carry the meaning.

## Interface

### Alert

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | - | Caller-supplied trailing control rendered before the dismiss button. |
| `accent` | `boolean` | - | Shows the variant-colored left accent bar; defaults to true for the callout appearance. |
| `icon` | `ReactNode` | - | Icon override; defaults to the variant's standard icon. Always hidden from assistive technology. Not rendered for the banner appearance. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | - | Renders a dismiss button and calls this when it is pressed. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` | - | Bold leading text of the alert. |
| `variant` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| null` | `"info"` | Semantic treatment of the alert. |
| `appearance` | `"surface" \| "banner" \| "callout"` | `"surface"` | Surface style: raised card, full-width banner strip, or quiet callout. |

## Accessibility

- Danger renders role="alert" so the message is announced immediately; other variants render role="status".
- appearance="banner" keeps the same role semantics; appearance="callout" renders no live region, so screen readers meet it in reading order rather than as an announcement.
- The variant icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; meaning is carried by the text.
- The dismiss control is a labeled button in the normal tab order.

- [Toast](/modules/toast)
- [Step-Up Notice](/modules/step-up-notice)

# Notification Item

A sanitized ecosystem inbox row with severity, source application, read state, deep link, and delivery-state controls.

## Usage

```js
import { NotificationItem } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<NotificationItem
  severity="warning"
  appLabel="Yang Operations"
  timestamp="2 hours ago"
  title="photos-api restarted unexpectedly"
  href="#"
  onMute={() => undefined}
  onArchive={() => undefined}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

An inbox lists sanitized pointers to application events.
### Avoid when

The feedback is local to the current task; use Alert or Toast instead.
### Behavior

Mute and archive touch delivery state only; the deep link never mutates the source.
### Responsive

Text wraps and controls stay reachable at mobile widths.

## Examples

### Unread with controls

Unread items are emphasized and announced; mute and archive only touch delivery state, never the source event.

```jsx
import { NotificationItem } from '@kryv/teal'

export function NotificationItemDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <NotificationItem
      severity="success"
      appLabel="Photos"
      timestamp="just now"
      title="Import finished"
      href="#"
      read
    />
  ) : (
    <NotificationItem
      severity="warning"
      appLabel="Yang Operations"
      timestamp="2 hours ago"
      title="photos-api restarted unexpectedly"
      href="#"
      onMute={() => undefined}
      onArchive={() => undefined}
    />
  )
}
```

### Read

Read items drop the emphasis and the unread announcement.

```jsx
import { NotificationItem } from '@kryv/teal'

export function NotificationItemDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <NotificationItem
      severity="success"
      appLabel="Photos"
      timestamp="just now"
      title="Import finished"
      href="#"
      read
    />
  ) : (
    <NotificationItem
      severity="warning"
      appLabel="Yang Operations"
      timestamp="2 hours ago"
      title="photos-api restarted unexpectedly"
      href="#"
      onMute={() => undefined}
      onArchive={() => undefined}
    />
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Severity dot** - Small colored marker matched to the severity variant.
- **Severity icon** - Decorative status icon beside the content; hidden from assistive technology.
- **Title link** - Deep link to the source application event; unread items are bold and append a screen-reader-only unread marker.
- **Metadata** - Source application label and caller-supplied timestamp.
- **Mute and archive** - Optional IconButtons that change delivery state only, never the source event.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Pass sanitized title and appLabel from the ecosystem payload; the row renders what it is given.
- Wire mute and archive to delivery-state endpoints only.

### Don't

- Don't mutate the source event from onMute or onArchive.
- Don't use NotificationItem for feedback local to the current task; use Alert or Toast.

## Interface

### NotificationItem

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appLabel` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Label of the source application, supplied sanitized by the caller. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `href` (required) | `string` | - | URL of the source application deep link. |
| `onArchive` | `() => void` | - | Renders an archive control and calls this when pressed. Never mutates the source event. |
| `onMute` | `() => void` | - | Renders a mute control and calls this when pressed. Never mutates the source event. |
| `read` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the item as read; unread items are emphasized and announce an unread marker. |
| `severity` | `enum` | `info` | Severity drives the indicator and icon. |
| `timestamp` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Human-readable timestamp supplied by the caller. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Notification title, supplied sanitized by the caller. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the title link and to the mute and archive buttons. |
| `Enter` | Follows the title link to the source application. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Activates the mute or archive button. |

- Unread items are bold and append a screen-reader-only ", unread" marker to the title link.
- The severity dot and icon are aria-hidden; severity must also be clear from the title or surrounding context.
- Mute and archive are IconButtons with explicit accessible labels.

## Related modules

- [Notification Center](/modules/notification-center)
- [Health Indicator](/modules/health-indicator)
- [Toast](/modules/toast)

# Health Indicator

An explicit ecosystem health status that reports unknown and stale evidence instead of implying health.

## Usage

```js
import { HealthIndicator } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<HealthIndicator status="healthy" label="Photos" />
<HealthIndicator status="unknown" label="Trict" />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A surface reports one application or ecosystem health status.
### Avoid when

The status is decorative; omit it instead of implying health.
### Behavior

Unknown, stale, and checking are explicit states; health is never inferred from missing evidence.
### Responsive

The badge and label wrap naturally in compact headers.

## Examples

### Reported statuses

Healthy, degraded, and down come straight from source evidence.

```jsx
import { HealthIndicator } from '@kryv/teal'

export function HealthIndicatorDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <HealthIndicator status="stale" label="Photos" />
      <HealthIndicator status="unknown" label="Trict" />
      <HealthIndicator status="loading" label="Yang Operations" />
    </div>
  ) : (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <HealthIndicator status="healthy" label="Photos" />
      <HealthIndicator status="degraded" label="Yang Operations" />
      <HealthIndicator status="down" label="Trict" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Missing evidence

Stale, unknown, and checking states stay visible; health is never inferred.

```jsx
import { HealthIndicator } from '@kryv/teal'

export function HealthIndicatorDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <HealthIndicator status="stale" label="Photos" />
      <HealthIndicator status="unknown" label="Trict" />
      <HealthIndicator status="loading" label="Yang Operations" />
    </div>
  ) : (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-4">
      <HealthIndicator status="healthy" label="Photos" />
      <HealthIndicator status="degraded" label="Yang Operations" />
      <HealthIndicator status="down" label="Trict" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Status badge** - Badge whose text and variant come straight from the reported status.
- **Label** - Optional application name rendered beside the badge.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Report missing evidence as unknown rather than implying healthy.
- Keep the status mapping on the evidence side; the indicator never infers.

### Don't

- Don't hide stale or unknown states to keep a dashboard green.
- Don't show a healthy badge without fresh evidence behind it.

## Interface

### HealthIndicator

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Application name rendered beside the status. |
| `status` (required) | `enum` | - | Current health evidence. Missing evidence must be reported as 'unknown', never inferred as healthy. |

## Accessibility

- The status renders as Badge text, so the state never depends on color alone.
- Stale, unknown, and checking are explicit states with their own wording; health is never implied by a missing value.

## Related modules

- [Status Dot](/modules/status-dot)
- [Badge](/modules/badge)
- [Notification Item](/modules/notification-item)

# Step-Up Notice

An inline warning that explains a required fresh verification and hosts the caller’s verification action.

## Usage

```js
import { StepUpNotice, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<StepUpNotice
  title="Confirm it's you"
  action={<Button size="sm">Verify with passkey</Button>}
>
  Approving a repair requires fresh verification.
</StepUpNotice>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A sensitive action requires fresh strong authentication first.
### Avoid when

A plain warning suffices; use Alert instead.
### Behavior

The verification action is caller-supplied; the notice never starts or auto-submits verification.
### Responsive

The action wraps beneath the explanation on narrow screens.

## Examples

### Verification required

The action is caller-supplied; the notice never starts verification on its own.

```jsx
import { Button, StepUpNotice } from '@kryv/teal'

export function StepUpNoticeDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <StepUpNotice title="Session expiring" onDismiss={() => undefined}>
      Verify again to keep this session active.
    </StepUpNotice>
  ) : (
    <StepUpNotice
      title="Confirm it's you"
      action={<Button size="sm">Verify with passkey</Button>}
    >
      Approving a repair requires fresh verification before Yang continues.
    </StepUpNotice>
  )
}
```

### Dismissible

Pass onDismiss when the notice is informational rather than blocking.

```jsx
import { Button, StepUpNotice } from '@kryv/teal'

export function StepUpNoticeDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return exampleIndex ? (
    <StepUpNotice title="Session expiring" onDismiss={() => undefined}>
      Verify again to keep this session active.
    </StepUpNotice>
  ) : (
    <StepUpNotice
      title="Confirm it's you"
      action={<Button size="sm">Verify with passkey</Button>}
    >
      Approving a repair requires fresh verification before Yang continues.
    </StepUpNotice>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Warning surface** - Built on Alert with the warning variant and its status semantics.
- **Title** - Bold lead-in naming the verification requirement.
- **Explanation** - Children text describing why fresh verification is required.
- **Action** - Caller-supplied verification control, such as a passkey Button; the notice never starts verification itself.
- **Dismiss** - Optional dismiss control rendered when onDismiss is passed.

## Do and don't

### Do

- State which action needs verification and why in the body copy.
- Render the caller's verification control as the action so the flow stays product-owned.

### Don't

- Don't use StepUpNotice for plain warnings; use Alert.
- Don't make the notice dismissible when verification is mandatory to proceed.

## Interface

### StepUpNotice

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `ReactNode` | - | Caller-supplied verification control, such as a passkey button. The notice never starts verification itself. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Explanation of why fresh verification is required. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | - | Renders a dismiss control and calls this when pressed. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Bold leading text of the notice. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the caller-supplied verification action and the dismiss control. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Activates the verification action or dismiss control. |

- Built on Alert with the warning variant, so it renders role="status" and is announced politely.
- Supply a labeled control as the action, such as a Button; it keeps its own accessible name.

## Related modules

- [Alert](/modules/alert)
- [Dialog](/modules/dialog)
- [Button](/modules/button)

# Timeline

A vertical activity feed with tone dots, connectors, and timestamps.

## Usage

```js
import { Timeline } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Timeline
  items={[
    { id: '1', title: 'Deploy finished', timestamp: '2 min ago', tone: 'success' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Events form a chronological feed.
### Avoid when

Items are peers without time order; use a plain list.
### Behavior

Tone dots carry semantics; connectors skip the last item.
### Responsive

Content wraps while the rail stays fixed width.

## Examples

### Activity feed

Tone dots mark event semantics; connectors link the sequence.

```jsx
import { Timeline } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TimelineDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-sm">
        <Timeline
          items={[
            { id: 'queued', title: 'Deploy queued', description: 'Release 2.4.0 · web-app', timestamp: '09:41', tone: 'neutral' },
            { id: 'building', title: 'Build completed', description: '412 modules in 3m 12s', timestamp: '09:46', tone: 'primary' },
            { id: 'live', title: 'Release is live', description: 'Health checks passing', timestamp: '09:52', tone: 'success' },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-sm">
      <Timeline
        items={[
          { id: 'commit', title: 'Jonas pushed 3 commits', description: 'feat: billing usage export', timestamp: '08:15', tone: 'neutral' },
          { id: 'review', title: 'Review approved', description: 'Priya approved #482', timestamp: '08:47', tone: 'primary' },
          { id: 'deploy', title: 'Deployed to production', description: 'Release 2.4.0 is live', timestamp: '09:52', tone: 'success' },
          { id: 'alert', title: 'Error budget warning', description: 'checkout-api above 2% errors', timestamp: '10:03', tone: 'warning' },
          { id: 'rollback', title: 'Rollback triggered', description: 'Reverted to 2.3.9', timestamp: '10:11', tone: 'danger' },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Event tones

Use success and warning tones to mark outcomes in a feed.

```jsx
import { Timeline } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TimelineDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-sm">
        <Timeline
          items={[
            { id: 'queued', title: 'Deploy queued', description: 'Release 2.4.0 · web-app', timestamp: '09:41', tone: 'neutral' },
            { id: 'building', title: 'Build completed', description: '412 modules in 3m 12s', timestamp: '09:46', tone: 'primary' },
            { id: 'live', title: 'Release is live', description: 'Health checks passing', timestamp: '09:52', tone: 'success' },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-sm">
      <Timeline
        items={[
          { id: 'commit', title: 'Jonas pushed 3 commits', description: 'feat: billing usage export', timestamp: '08:15', tone: 'neutral' },
          { id: 'review', title: 'Review approved', description: 'Priya approved #482', timestamp: '08:47', tone: 'primary' },
          { id: 'deploy', title: 'Deployed to production', description: 'Release 2.4.0 is live', timestamp: '09:52', tone: 'success' },
          { id: 'alert', title: 'Error budget warning', description: 'checkout-api above 2% errors', timestamp: '10:03', tone: 'warning' },
          { id: 'rollback', title: 'Rollback triggered', description: 'Reverted to 2.3.9', timestamp: '10:11', tone: 'danger' },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Rail** - Fixed-width left column holding the dots and connectors; hidden from assistive technology.
- **Tone dot** - Colored marker per item: neutral, primary, success, warning, or danger.
- **Connector** - Hairline linking an item to the next; skipped after the last item.
- **Content** - Title, optional description, and timestamp stacked per entry inside an ordered list.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Order items chronologically and give each a stable id.
- Use tone dots to mark outcomes, such as success for a finished deploy.

### Don't

- Don't use Timeline for unordered peer items; use a plain List.
- Don't rely on the dot color alone; the title must state the outcome.

## Interface

### Timeline

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `TimelineItem[]` | - | Entries to render, in display order. |

## Accessibility

- Items render as an ordered list, so screen readers announce position and count.
- Dots and connectors are aria-hidden; the tone meaning must also appear in the item title or description.

## Related modules

- [Activity Feed](/modules/activity-feed)
- [List](/modules/list)
- [Status Dot](/modules/status-dot)

# Meter

A scalar gauge for a known range with optimum-zone coloring.

## Usage

```js
import { Meter } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Meter label="Storage used" value={72} low={60} high={85} optimum={20} />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A quantity within a known range needs a glanceable gauge.
### Avoid when

Progress toward completing a task is shown; use Progress.
### Behavior

role="meter" carries min, max, and now; zones color the fill from low, high, and optimum.
### Responsive

The track fills its container, so constrain width in the layout.

## Examples

### Zones

low, high, and optimum map the value onto neutral, success, warning, and danger fills.

```jsx
import { Meter } from '@kryv/teal'

export function MeterDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-5">
        <Meter label="Storage used" value={68} max={120} formatValue={(v) => `${Math.round(v)} GB of 120 GB`} />
        <Meter label="Bandwidth" value={0.82} max={1} formatValue={(v) => `${Math.round(v * 100)}%`} />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-5">
      <Meter label="Storage used" value={42} low={60} high={85} optimum={20} />
      <Meter label="Memory pressure" value={72} low={60} high={85} optimum={20} />
      <Meter label="CPU load" value={93} low={60} high={85} optimum={20} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Custom formatting

formatValue renders units such as GB in the readout and the accessible value text.

```jsx
import { Meter } from '@kryv/teal'

export function MeterDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-5">
        <Meter label="Storage used" value={68} max={120} formatValue={(v) => `${Math.round(v)} GB of 120 GB`} />
        <Meter label="Bandwidth" value={0.82} max={1} formatValue={(v) => `${Math.round(v * 100)}%`} />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-sm gap-5">
      <Meter label="Storage used" value={42} low={60} high={85} optimum={20} />
      <Meter label="Memory pressure" value={72} low={60} high={85} optimum={20} />
      <Meter label="CPU load" value={93} low={60} high={85} optimum={20} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Label and readout** - Heading text and formatted value on one row; the label names the meter through aria-labelledby.
- **Track** - Rounded container bar that holds the fill.
- **Zone fill** - Colored fill whose tone maps the value against low, high, and optimum into neutral, success, warning, or danger.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Set low, high, and optimum together so the zone colors mean something.
- Use formatValue for units such as GB; it also feeds the accessible value text.

### Don't

- Don't use Meter for task completion; use Progress.
- Don't pass only one or two thresholds; without all three the fill stays neutral.

## Interface

### Meter

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `formatValue` | `(value: number) => string` | `(v) => String(Math.round(v))` | Formats the visible value text. Defaults to the rounded raw value. |
| `high` | `number` | - | Upper boundary of the middle range; used with `low` and `optimum` to color the fill. |
| `label` (required) | `string` | - | Accessible name describing what the meter measures. |
| `low` | `number` | - | Lower boundary of the middle range; used with `high` and `optimum` to color the fill. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | Largest value the meter can show. |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | Smallest value the meter can show. |
| `optimum` | `number` | - | The value considered ideal; determines whether low or high readings are good. |
| `value` (required) | `number` | - | Current value; clamped between `min` and `max`. |

## Accessibility

- role="meter" exposes aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, and an aria-valuetext built from formatValue.
- Zone color is supplementary; the label and numeric readout carry the value.
- The fill width transition is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Related modules

- [Loading](/modules/loading)
- [Stat](/modules/stat)

# Rating

A star rating input with radio semantics, arrow keys, and a read-only display mode.

## Usage

```js
import { Rating } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Rating label="Rate this report" defaultValue={3} onChange={(value) => undefined} />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Users score something on a small fixed scale.
### Avoid when

The input is numeric but not a rating; use Slider or NumberInput.
### Behavior

Stars form a radiogroup with roving tab index and arrow-key selection.
### Responsive

Pick a size per context; the inline group never wraps.

## Examples

### Interactive rating

Stars behave as a radiogroup with roving tab index; arrows move and select.

```jsx
import { Rating } from '@kryv/teal'

export function RatingDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <Rating readOnly value={4} aria-label="Rated 4 out of 5" />
        <Rating readOnly value={3} size="sm" aria-label="Rated 3 out of 5" />
        <Rating readOnly value={5} size="lg" aria-label="Rated 5 out of 5" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <Rating label="Rate this report" defaultValue={3} />
      <Rating label="Rate the onboarding" defaultValue={4} size="lg" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Read-only display

readOnly renders static stars with an img role for review summaries.

```jsx
import { Rating } from '@kryv/teal'

export function RatingDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <Rating readOnly value={4} aria-label="Rated 4 out of 5" />
        <Rating readOnly value={3} size="sm" aria-label="Rated 3 out of 5" />
        <Rating readOnly value={5} size="lg" aria-label="Rated 5 out of 5" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <Rating label="Rate this report" defaultValue={3} />
      <Rating label="Rate the onboarding" defaultValue={4} size="lg" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Group** - role="radiogroup" container named by the label prop; owns the arrow-key handling.
- **Star buttons** - One role="radio" button per star with aria-checked; only the checked star stays in the tab order.
- **Read-only display** - Static stars rendered as role="img" with an "x out of y stars" label when readOnly is set.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Name the group with label, such as "Rate this report".
- Use readOnly for review summaries so scores display without entering the tab order.

### Don't

- Don't use Rating for arbitrary numeric input; use Slider or NumberInput.
- Don't change max away from five without a reason; users expect a familiar scale.

## Interface

### Rating

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultValue` | `number` | `0` | Initial rating when uncontrolled. |
| `label` | `string` | `Rating` | Accessible name for the rating group. |
| `max` | `number` | `5` | Number of stars shown. |
| `onChange` | `(value: number) => void` | - | Called with the new rating when a star is chosen. |
| `readOnly` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders static stars without any interaction. |
| `size` | `enum` | `md` | Star size. |
| `value` | `number` | - | Controlled rating between 0 and `max`. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the checked star, or the first star when nothing is rated. |
| `Arrow Left` + `Arrow Down` | Moves to and selects the previous star. |
| `Arrow Right` + `Arrow Up` | Moves to and selects the next star. |

- Stars form a radiogroup named by the label prop; each star is a role="radio" button with aria-checked.
- Roving tab index keeps one tab stop for the whole group.
- readOnly renders role="img" with an "x out of y stars" label and leaves the tab order entirely.

## Related modules

- [Slider](/modules/slider)
- [Radio Group](/modules/radio-group)
- [Number Input](/modules/number-input)

# Announcer

A visually hidden live region that re-announces a message whenever it changes.

## Usage

```js
import { Announcer, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Announcer message={statusMessage} politeness="polite" />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

State changes off-screen must reach screen-reader users.
### Avoid when

The change is already visible and focused; announcement would duplicate it.
### Behavior

The region clears and rewrites so identical messages re-announce.
### Responsive

The region is visually hidden and has no layout impact.

## Examples

### Status updates

The region clears and rewrites so a repeated message is announced again.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Announcer, Button } from '@kryv/teal'

export function AnnouncerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState(0)
  const [failed, setFailed] = useState(0)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setFailed((count) => count + 1)}>
          Simulate failure
        </Button>
        <Announcer message={failed > 0 ? 'Saving failed. Try again.' : ''} politeness="assertive" />
        <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
          {failed > 0 ? `Announced ${failed} time(s) — assertively.` : 'Failures announce with politeness="assertive".'}
        </span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <Button onClick={() => setSaved((count) => count + 1)}>Save changes</Button>
      <Announcer message={saved > 0 ? 'Changes saved' : ''} />
      <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
        {saved > 0 ? `Announced "Changes saved" ${saved} time(s).` : 'Saving announces through a hidden live region.'}
      </span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Assertive updates

Use politeness="assertive" only for urgent changes that should interrupt.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Announcer, Button } from '@kryv/teal'

export function AnnouncerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState(0)
  const [failed, setFailed] = useState(0)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
        <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setFailed((count) => count + 1)}>
          Simulate failure
        </Button>
        <Announcer message={failed > 0 ? 'Saving failed. Try again.' : ''} politeness="assertive" />
        <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
          {failed > 0 ? `Announced ${failed} time(s) — assertively.` : 'Failures announce with politeness="assertive".'}
        </span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <Button onClick={() => setSaved((count) => count + 1)}>Save changes</Button>
      <Announcer message={saved > 0 ? 'Changes saved' : ''} />
      <span className="text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant">
        {saved > 0 ? `Announced "Changes saved" ${saved} time(s).` : 'Saving announces through a hidden live region.'}
      </span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Live region** - Visually hidden role="status" element with aria-live set from politeness and aria-atomic.
- **Clear-and-rewrite** - The message is emptied and then re-written so a repeated message is announced again.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Keep one Announcer per message channel and update its message prop as state changes.
- Use assertive only for urgent changes that must interrupt the user.

### Don't

- Don't announce changes that are already visible and focused; that duplicates the information.
- Don't mount a new Announcer per message; reuse a single region.

## Interface

### Announcer

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` (required) | `string` | - | Text announced to screen readers; re-announced whenever it changes. |
| `politeness` | `enum` | `polite` | Urgency of the live region. |

## Accessibility

- Renders a visually hidden role="status" region with aria-live set from politeness and aria-atomic="true".
- The region clears and rewrites the message so an identical message is announced again.
- Reserve politeness="assertive" for urgent changes; polite is the default.

## Related modules

- [Toast](/modules/toast)
- [Alert](/modules/alert)
- [Save Status](/modules/save-status)

# Blocking Overlay

A full-surface overlay with a spinner that blocks interaction with the wrapped content during async work.

## Usage

```js
import { BlockingOverlay } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<BlockingOverlay
  visible={isSaving}
  label="Saving changes"
>
  <SettingsForm />
</BlockingOverlay>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

An in-flight operation must not be interrupted by further edits, such as a form save or a bulk action.
### Avoid when

The content can remain interactive or a small inline spinner is enough; use Spinner or LoadingState instead.
### Behavior

While visible it covers the wrapped content, sets aria-busy, moves focus into the overlay, and traps Tab until hidden.
### Responsive

Fills its positioned container at any size; keep the container relative and full-width on small screens.

## Examples

### Always-on overlay

The overlay covering placeholder content while visible.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { BlockingOverlay } from '@kryv/teal'

export function BlockingOverlayDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex w-full max-w-md flex-col items-start gap-3">
        <button
          type="button"
          className="rounded-lg border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-semibold"
          onClick={() => {
            setBusy(true)
            setTimeout(() => setBusy(false), 2000)
          }}
        >
          Simulate save
        </button>
        <BlockingOverlay visible={busy} label="Saving changes" className="w-full rounded-xl border">
          <div className="grid gap-2 p-6 text-sm">
            <p>Form content that cannot be edited while the save is in flight.</p>
            <div className="h-4 w-2/3 rounded bg-black/10" />
            <div className="h-4 w-1/2 rounded bg-black/10" />
          </div>
        </BlockingOverlay>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <BlockingOverlay visible label="Loading report" className="w-full max-w-md rounded-xl border">
      <div className="grid gap-2 p-6">
        <div className="h-4 w-2/3 rounded bg-black/10" />
        <div className="h-4 w-1/2 rounded bg-black/10" />
        <div className="h-4 w-1/3 rounded bg-black/10" />
      </div>
    </BlockingOverlay>
  )
}
```

### Triggered by work

A simulated save that shows and hides the overlay around real async work.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { BlockingOverlay } from '@kryv/teal'

export function BlockingOverlayDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex w-full max-w-md flex-col items-start gap-3">
        <button
          type="button"
          className="rounded-lg border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-semibold"
          onClick={() => {
            setBusy(true)
            setTimeout(() => setBusy(false), 2000)
          }}
        >
          Simulate save
        </button>
        <BlockingOverlay visible={busy} label="Saving changes" className="w-full rounded-xl border">
          <div className="grid gap-2 p-6 text-sm">
            <p>Form content that cannot be edited while the save is in flight.</p>
            <div className="h-4 w-2/3 rounded bg-black/10" />
            <div className="h-4 w-1/2 rounded bg-black/10" />
          </div>
        </BlockingOverlay>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <BlockingOverlay visible label="Loading report" className="w-full max-w-md rounded-xl border">
      <div className="grid gap-2 p-6">
        <div className="h-4 w-2/3 rounded bg-black/10" />
        <div className="h-4 w-1/2 rounded bg-black/10" />
        <div className="h-4 w-1/3 rounded bg-black/10" />
      </div>
    </BlockingOverlay>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Wrapper** - Relative container around the protected content; sets aria-busy while the overlay is visible.
- **Scrim** - Full-surface layer that blocks pointer interaction and traps Tab while shown.
- **Status** - Centered spinner in a role="status" region labeled by the label prop.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use it when concurrent edits would corrupt state, such as during a bulk save.
- Keep the label specific to the work in progress, such as "Saving changes".

### Don't

- Don't block the whole page for one control's work; use a Button loading state instead.
- Don't leave the overlay visible without a failure or timeout path.

## Interface

### BlockingOverlay

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visible` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows the overlay and blocks interaction with the wrapped content while true. |
| `label` | `string` | `Loading` | Accessible label announced while the overlay is visible; also rendered under the spinner. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Cycles focus within the overlay; the blocked content is unreachable. |
| `Shift + Tab` | Cycles focus within the overlay in reverse. |

- The wrapper exposes aria-busy while the overlay is visible.
- The overlay is a role="status" region labeled by the label prop, and focus is restored to the previously focused element when it hides.

## Related modules

- [Loading](/modules/loading)
- [Error Boundary](/modules/error-boundary)
- [Dialog](/modules/dialog)
