# Error Boundary

A class-based error boundary that isolates render failures behind a fallback UI with reset support.

## Usage

```js
import { ErrorBoundary } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<ErrorBoundary
  fallback={(error, reset) => <Fallback error={error} onRetry={reset} />}
  onError={(error, info) => log(error)}
  resetKeys={[pageId]}
>
  <Report />
</ErrorBoundary>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A subtree can fail independently — dashboards, widgets, or third-party embeds — and the rest of the page must survive.
### Avoid when

Handling expected async errors; catch those in data-loading code and show EmptyState or Alert instead.
### Behavior

Catches render errors below it, calls onError, swaps in the fallback, and re-renders children on reset() or when any resetKey changes.
### Responsive

Layout-agnostic; the fallback owns its own sizing.

## Examples

### Recoverable fallback

A render-prop fallback that shows the error and offers a retry via the reset callback.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { ErrorBoundary } from '@kryv/teal'

function MaybeBroken({ broken }) {
  if (broken) throw new Error('The report could not be rendered.')
  return <p className="text-sm">Report content rendered normally.</p>
}

export function ErrorBoundaryDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [broken, setBroken] = useState(true)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <ErrorBoundary fallback={<div className="rounded-xl border p-4 text-sm">This section failed to load.</div>}>
        <MaybeBroken broken />
      </ErrorBoundary>
    )
  }

  return (
    <ErrorBoundary
      onError={(error) => console.error('Caught by boundary:', error.message)}
      fallback={(error, reset) => (
        <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-2 rounded-xl border p-4 text-sm">
          <p>{error.message}</p>
          <button
            type="button"
            className="rounded-lg border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-semibold"
            onClick={() => {
              setBroken(false)
              reset()
            }}
          >
            Retry
          </button>
        </div>
      )}
    >
      <MaybeBroken broken={broken} />
    </ErrorBoundary>
  )
}
```

### Static fallback

A plain React node shown whenever the protected subtree throws.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { ErrorBoundary } from '@kryv/teal'

function MaybeBroken({ broken }) {
  if (broken) throw new Error('The report could not be rendered.')
  return <p className="text-sm">Report content rendered normally.</p>
}

export function ErrorBoundaryDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [broken, setBroken] = useState(true)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <ErrorBoundary fallback={<div className="rounded-xl border p-4 text-sm">This section failed to load.</div>}>
        <MaybeBroken broken />
      </ErrorBoundary>
    )
  }

  return (
    <ErrorBoundary
      onError={(error) => console.error('Caught by boundary:', error.message)}
      fallback={(error, reset) => (
        <div className="flex flex-col items-start gap-2 rounded-xl border p-4 text-sm">
          <p>{error.message}</p>
          <button
            type="button"
            className="rounded-lg border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-semibold"
            onClick={() => {
              setBroken(false)
              reset()
            }}
          >
            Retry
          </button>
        </div>
      )}
    >
      <MaybeBroken broken={broken} />
    </ErrorBoundary>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Boundary** - Class component that catches render errors from its subtree and reports them through onError.
- **Fallback** - Node or render prop receiving (error, reset) that is shown while the subtree is failed.
- **Reset** - Re-renders the children when reset() is called or any resetKey changes.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Place boundaries around independently failing subtrees such as widgets or third-party embeds.
- Give the fallback a recovery path through the reset callback.

### Don't

- Don't catch expected async errors here; handle those in data-loading code with EmptyState or Alert.
- Don't wrap the entire app in one boundary; a single failure then blanks the whole page.

## Interface

### ErrorBoundary

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Content protected by the boundary. |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode \| ((error: Error, reset: () => void) => ReactNode)` | - | Rendered instead of children when an error is caught. As a function it receives the error and a reset callback. |
| `onError` | `(error: Error, info: ErrorInfo) => void` | - | Called with the error and component stack when an error is caught. |
| `resetKeys` | `unknown[]` | - | Resets the boundary whenever any of these values change. |

## Accessibility

- Give the fallback an accessible error message, for example role="alert", so the failure is announced.
- Provide a keyboard-reachable recovery action such as a retry button.

## Related modules

- [Empty State](/modules/empty-state)
- [Alert](/modules/alert)
- [Blocking Overlay](/modules/blocking-overlay)

# Loading Bar

A thin top-of-page progress bar with determinate and indeterminate modes.

## Usage

```js
import { LoadingBar } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<LoadingBar
  value={65}
  label="Loading assets"
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Navigations or page-level loads need ambient progress feedback without replacing the page content.
### Avoid when

The wait is tied to one region or component; use LoadingState or Spinner there instead.
### Behavior

Omits aria-valuenow in indeterminate mode; clamps determinate values to 0–max and animates width changes.
### Responsive

Spans the full viewport width at any size; height stays a thin 2px strip.

## Examples

### Determinate

A known percentage pinned to the top of the page, for example while assets stream in.

```jsx
import { LoadingBar } from '@kryv/teal'

export function LoadingBarDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
        <LoadingBar label="Loading page" />
        <p className="text-black/60">Indeterminate mode — shown while the route loads.</p>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
      <LoadingBar value={65} label="Loading assets" />
      <p className="text-black/60">Determinate mode at 65% — pinned to the top of the page.</p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Indeterminate

A pulsing bar for route transitions where progress cannot be measured.

```jsx
import { LoadingBar } from '@kryv/teal'

export function LoadingBarDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
        <LoadingBar label="Loading page" />
        <p className="text-black/60">Indeterminate mode — shown while the route loads.</p>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
      <LoadingBar value={65} label="Loading assets" />
      <p className="text-black/60">Determinate mode at 65% — pinned to the top of the page.</p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Track** - Thin 2px strip pinned to the top of the page.
- **Fill** - Primary bar whose width animates to the value; pulses across the track when indeterminate.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use it for route transitions and page-level loads where the content stays on screen.
- Switch to determinate mode as soon as a measurable percentage exists.

### Don't

- Don't use it for region-local waits; use LoadingState or Spinner there.
- Don't fake smooth increments; jump to the real value when it is known.

## Interface

### LoadingBar

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | - | Current value between 0 and `max`. Omit for indeterminate mode. |
| `max` | `number` | `100` | Maximum value. |
| `label` | `string` | `Loading` | Accessible label announced by screen readers. |

## Accessibility

- Rendered as role="progressbar" with an aria-label; determinate mode adds aria-valuemin/max/now.
- Indeterminate motion is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Related modules

- [Loading](/modules/loading)
- [Blocking Overlay](/modules/blocking-overlay)

# Network Status

An inline indicator of the browser's online/offline state with a render prop for custom display.

## Usage

```js
import { NetworkStatus } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<NetworkStatus
  onlineLabel="Connected"
  offlineLabel="No connection"
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

The UI depends on connectivity and users benefit from a persistent inline indicator, for example next to sync controls.
### Avoid when

You only need to interrupt the user when connectivity drops; use OfflineBanner instead.
### Behavior

Initializes from navigator.onLine and updates live on the window online/offline events.
### Responsive

Compact inline element; the render prop allows any responsive treatment.

## Examples

### Default indicator

An icon and label that track online/offline browser events.

```jsx
import { NetworkStatus } from '@kryv/teal'

export function NetworkStatusDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <NetworkStatus>
        {(online) => (
          <span className={`text-sm font-semibold ${online ? 'text-emerald-600' : 'text-red-600'}`}>
            {online ? 'Connected — all systems go' : 'Connection lost'}
          </span>
        )}
      </NetworkStatus>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <NetworkStatus />
      <NetworkStatus onlineLabel="Connected" offlineLabel="No connection" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Custom render prop

Fully custom output driven by the current online boolean.

```jsx
import { NetworkStatus } from '@kryv/teal'

export function NetworkStatusDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <NetworkStatus>
        {(online) => (
          <span className={`text-sm font-semibold ${online ? 'text-emerald-600' : 'text-red-600'}`}>
            {online ? 'Connected — all systems go' : 'Connection lost'}
          </span>
        )}
      </NetworkStatus>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <NetworkStatus />
      <NetworkStatus onlineLabel="Connected" offlineLabel="No connection" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Icon** - Decorative connectivity glyph that flips with the online state.
- **Label** - Online and offline text supplied through onlineLabel and offlineLabel.
- **Render prop** - Optional custom output receiving the current online boolean.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Place it near sync or save controls where connectivity changes the outcome.
- Expose the state as text in custom renders, never as color alone.

### Don't

- Don't use it as the only offline signal when unsaved work is at risk; use OfflineBanner.
- Don't poll navigator.onLine yourself; the component already listens to online and offline events.

## Interface

### NetworkStatus

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` | `(online: boolean) => ReactNode` | - | Render prop receiving the current online state for fully custom output. |
| `onlineLabel` | `string` | `Online` | Text shown while the browser is online. |
| `offlineLabel` | `string` | `Offline` | Text shown while the browser is offline. |

## Accessibility

- The icon is aria-hidden; the state is conveyed by the visible text label.
- Render-prop consumers should expose the state as text, not color alone.

## Related modules

- [Offline Banner](/modules/offline-banner)
- [Save Status](/modules/save-status)
- [Status Dot](/modules/status-dot)

# Offline Banner

A dismissible banner that appears at the top of the page when the browser loses connectivity.

## Usage

```js
import { OfflineBanner } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<OfflineBanner
  message="You are offline. Changes may not be saved."
  onDismiss={() => logDismiss()}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Losing connectivity has real consequences — unsaved edits, stalled sync — and the user must be told immediately.
### Avoid when

A subtle always-on indicator is enough; use NetworkStatus instead.
### Behavior

Shows on the offline event, hides on the online event, stays hidden once dismissed until the next offline transition.
### Responsive

Spans the full viewport width and wraps its message at narrow widths.

## Examples

### Default banner

Appears automatically on the offline event and disappears when the connection returns.

```jsx
import { OfflineBanner } from '@kryv/teal'

export function OfflineBannerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return <OfflineBanner message="Connection lost — retrying in the background" dismissLabel="Hide message" />
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
      <OfflineBanner />
      <p className="text-black/60">Toggle your network connection to see the banner appear.</p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Custom message

Tailored copy and dismiss label for product-specific offline behavior.

```jsx
import { OfflineBanner } from '@kryv/teal'

export function OfflineBannerDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return <OfflineBanner message="Connection lost — retrying in the background" dismissLabel="Hide message" />
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2 text-sm">
      <OfflineBanner />
      <p className="text-black/60">Toggle your network connection to see the banner appear.</p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Status strip** - Top-of-page role="status" banner with aria-live="polite" that appears on the offline event and clears when the connection returns.
- **Message** - Caller-supplied warning text; wraps at narrow widths.
- **Dismiss** - Labeled close button; the banner stays dismissed until the next offline transition.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Say what offline means for the user's work, such as "Changes may not be saved".
- Let the banner reappear on the next drop even if it was dismissed.

### Don't

- Don't show it when the app is fully local and connectivity is irrelevant.
- Don't auto-hide it on a timer; it clears itself when the connection returns.

## Interface

### OfflineBanner

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | `You are offline. Changes may not be saved until the connection returns.` | Message shown inside the banner. |
| `dismissLabel` | `string` | `Dismiss offline notification` | Accessible label for the dismiss button. |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | - | Called when the banner is dismissed. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the dismiss button. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Dismisses the banner when the dismiss button is focused. |

- Rendered as role="status" with aria-live="polite" so the appearance is announced without stealing focus.
- The dismiss button has an explicit accessible label.

## Related modules

- [Network Status](/modules/network-status)
- [Alert](/modules/alert)

# Save Status

An inline saved/saving/error indicator with an optional relative timestamp.

## Usage

```js
import { SaveStatus } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<SaveStatus
  status="saved"
  savedAt={lastSavedAt}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A document or form autosaves and the user needs quiet, continuous confidence about persistence.
### Avoid when

A save is an explicit user action with a clear result; use a Toast or inline Button feedback instead.
### Behavior

Reflects the status prop: saved shows a check with an optional relative timestamp, saving shows a spinner, error shows a failure message.
### Responsive

Stays inline and compact; pair it with a toolbar or header where space is tight.

## Examples

### All three states

Saved, saving, and error side by side — the full lifecycle of an autosave.

```jsx
import { SaveStatus } from '@kryv/teal'

const threeMinutesAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 3 * 60 * 1000)

export function SaveStatusDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <SaveStatus savedAt={threeMinutesAgo} />
        <SaveStatus savedAt={new Date()} formatSavedAt={(date) => date.toLocaleTimeString()} />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <SaveStatus status="saved" savedAt={new Date()} />
      <SaveStatus status="saving" />
      <SaveStatus status="error" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Relative timestamp

A saved-at time rendered as relative text, with a custom formatter option.

```jsx
import { SaveStatus } from '@kryv/teal'

const threeMinutesAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 3 * 60 * 1000)

export function SaveStatusDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <SaveStatus savedAt={threeMinutesAgo} />
        <SaveStatus savedAt={new Date()} formatSavedAt={(date) => date.toLocaleTimeString()} />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <SaveStatus status="saved" savedAt={new Date()} />
      <SaveStatus status="saving" />
      <SaveStatus status="error" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Status icon** - Check, spinner, or error glyph matched to the status; aria-hidden.
- **Status text** - Saved, Saving, or Save failed wording rendered by the component.
- **Timestamp** - Optional relative saved-at time appended after "Saved", with a custom formatter option.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Place it in the header or toolbar of an autosaving editor where it stays visible.
- Pass the real savedAt time so the relative timestamp stays honest.

### Don't

- Don't use it for an explicit save action; show the result with a Toast instead.
- Don't show the saved state before the persistence request actually resolves.

## Interface

### SaveStatus

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `enum` | `saved` | Current persistence state. |
| `savedAt` | `Date` | - | When the last save completed; rendered as relative text after the "Saved" label. |
| `formatSavedAt` | `(date: Date) => string` | - | Formats `savedAt` into relative text. |

## Accessibility

- Rendered as role="status" so state changes are announced politely.
- The saving spinner is aria-hidden and stops animating under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Related modules

- [Toast](/modules/toast)

# Status Dot

A small colored dot with an optional text label for compact entity status; pass pulse for live presence or ongoing activity.

## Usage

```js
import { StatusDot } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<StatusDot
  variant="success"
  label="Online"
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

You need a compact, glanceable status marker next to an entity name, for example in tables or list rows.
### Avoid when

The status needs more explanation or an action; use Alert instead.
### Behavior

Purely presentational: the dot is hidden from assistive technology and the visible label carries the meaning. With pulse it renders role="status" with the label as aria-label and animates a ping ring, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
### Responsive

Stays inline and shrinks to content; the label truncates with the surrounding layout.

## Examples

### Labeled statuses

Dots paired with text labels for scanable inline status in lists and headers.

```jsx
import { StatusDot } from '@kryv/teal'

export function StatusDotDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <StatusDot variant="success" label="Deployment healthy" />
        <StatusDot variant="warning" label="Approaching quota" />
        <StatusDot variant="danger" label="Build failed" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <StatusDot pulse label="3 editors online" />
          <span className="text-sm">3 editors online</span>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <StatusDot pulse label="Live stream" variant="info" size="lg" />
          <span className="text-sm">Live</span>
        </div>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <StatusDot variant="success" label="Online" />
      <StatusDot variant="neutral" label="Idle" />
      <StatusDot variant="info" label="Syncing" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Semantic variants

The success, warning, and danger variants for health-style readouts.

```jsx
import { StatusDot } from '@kryv/teal'

export function StatusDotDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <StatusDot variant="success" label="Deployment healthy" />
        <StatusDot variant="warning" label="Approaching quota" />
        <StatusDot variant="danger" label="Build failed" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <StatusDot pulse label="3 editors online" />
          <span className="text-sm">3 editors online</span>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <StatusDot pulse label="Live stream" variant="info" size="lg" />
          <span className="text-sm">Live</span>
        </div>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <StatusDot variant="success" label="Online" />
      <StatusDot variant="neutral" label="Idle" />
      <StatusDot variant="info" label="Syncing" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Live pulse

Pulse mode for live presence or streaming activity, announced via an accessible label.

```jsx
import { StatusDot } from '@kryv/teal'

export function StatusDotDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <StatusDot variant="success" label="Deployment healthy" />
        <StatusDot variant="warning" label="Approaching quota" />
        <StatusDot variant="danger" label="Build failed" />
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (exampleIndex === 2) {
    return (
      <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <StatusDot pulse label="3 editors online" />
          <span className="text-sm">3 editors online</span>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <StatusDot pulse label="Live stream" variant="info" size="lg" />
          <span className="text-sm">Live</span>
        </div>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-6">
      <StatusDot variant="success" label="Online" />
      <StatusDot variant="neutral" label="Idle" />
      <StatusDot variant="info" label="Syncing" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Dot** - Small colored marker with variant and size options; aria-hidden. In pulse mode it renders as a ping ring over a solid dot, both aria-hidden.
- **Label** - Optional visible text that carries the status meaning; in pulse mode it becomes the aria-label on the role="status" element (default "Live").

## Do and don't

### Do

- Pair the dot with a text label so color is never the only signal.
- Use the success, warning, and danger variants for health-style readouts.
- Pass pulse with a label that says what is live, such as "3 editors online".

### Don't

- Don't use a bare dot for a status users must act on; use Alert.
- Don't animate a static status dot; reserve pulse for live activity.

## Interface

### StatusDot

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` | - | Optional text rendered next to the dot. In pulse mode it becomes the accessible label (default `'Live'`). |
| `pulse` | `boolean` | `false` | Render as an animated pulsing dot for live presence or ongoing activity. |
| `variant` | `"neutral" \| "info" \| "success" \| "warning" \| "danger" \| null` | - | - |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| null` | - | - |

## Accessibility

- The colored dot is aria-hidden; always pair it with a text label or an aria-label so color is not the only signal.
- Color alone never conveys the status — the label text does.
- With pulse, the dot is rendered as role="status" with an aria-label that describes the live state; the pulsing ring is aria-hidden and uses motion-reduce to respect prefers-reduced-motion.

# Upload Progress

A file upload progress row with file name, determinate bar, formatted size, and a cancel button.

## Usage

```js
import { UploadProgress } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<UploadProgress
  fileName="design-spec.fig"
  progress={62}
  size={4718592}
  onCancel={cancelUpload}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Uploads run in the background and users need per-file progress plus the ability to cancel.
### Avoid when

You only need a single overall progress figure; use Progress or LoadingBar instead.
### Behavior

Clamps progress to 0–100, formats the byte size, and calls onCancel from the trailing button without managing the upload itself.
### Responsive

The file name truncates with ellipsis so the bar and cancel button keep their space at narrow widths.

## Examples

### In-flight uploads

Rows with progress, size, and a cancel action for active uploads.

```jsx
import { UploadProgress } from '@kryv/teal'

export function UploadProgressDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex w-full max-w-md flex-col gap-3">
        <UploadProgress fileName="quarterly-report.pdf" progress={100} size={842_000} />
        <UploadProgress fileName="assets-backup.zip" progress={35} size={1_342_177_280} onCancel={() => {}} />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-md flex-col gap-3">
      <UploadProgress fileName="design-spec.fig" progress={62} size={4_718_592} onCancel={() => {}} />
      <UploadProgress fileName="avatar.png" progress={12} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Completed and large files

A finished upload at 100% and a large file with formatted GB size.

```jsx
import { UploadProgress } from '@kryv/teal'

export function UploadProgressDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="flex w-full max-w-md flex-col gap-3">
        <UploadProgress fileName="quarterly-report.pdf" progress={100} size={842_000} />
        <UploadProgress fileName="assets-backup.zip" progress={35} size={1_342_177_280} onCancel={() => {}} />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex w-full max-w-md flex-col gap-3">
      <UploadProgress fileName="design-spec.fig" progress={62} size={4_718_592} onCancel={() => {}} />
      <UploadProgress fileName="avatar.png" progress={12} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **File icon and name** - Decorative file glyph plus the file name, which truncates with ellipsis.
- **Progress bar** - role="progressbar" labeled "Uploading <file name>" with values clamped to 0–100.
- **Size** - Byte size formatted into KB, MB, or GB.
- **Cancel** - Trailing button that calls onCancel; its accessible name includes the file name.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Keep one row per in-flight upload and wire onCancel to abort the request.
- Pass raw bytes and percentages; the component clamps and formats them.

### Don't

- Don't use it for a single overall progress figure; use Progress or LoadingBar.
- Don't remove the row the instant it hits 100%; give the completion a beat.

## Interface

### UploadProgress

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fileName` (required) | `string` | - | Name of the file being uploaded. |
| `progress` (required) | `number` | - | Upload completion percentage; clamped between 0 and 100. |
| `size` | `number` | - | Total size of the file in bytes, shown formatted next to the percentage. |
| `formatSize` | `(bytes: number) => string` | - | Formats the byte size for display. |
| `onCancel` | `() => void` | - | Renders a cancel button that calls this when pressed. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the cancel button. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Cancels the upload when the cancel button is focused. |

- The bar is a role="progressbar" labeled 'Uploading <file name>' with aria-valuemin/max/now.
- The cancel button's accessible name includes the file name.

## Related modules

- [File Upload](/modules/file-upload)
- [Loading](/modules/loading)

# App Switcher

An entitlement-filtered application switcher with an explicit Home destination and keyboard navigation.

## Usage

```js
import { AppSwitcher, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<AppSwitcher
  trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Switch application</Button>}
  homeHref="#"
  homeLabel="Home"
  apps={[
    { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: '#' },
    { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: '#', current: true },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

People move between entitled ecosystem applications.
### Avoid when

The navigation is inside one application; use a sidebar or tabs instead.
### Behavior

The caller filters applications by entitlement first; the switcher always includes the explicit Home destination.
### Responsive

The dropdown collision-handles to stay on screen; keep labels short on narrow layouts.

## Examples

### Household applications

The caller filters applications by entitlement first; the switcher renders only what it is given plus the explicit Home destination.

```jsx
import { AppSwitcher, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Camera, Gauge, LineChart } from 'lucide-react'

export function AppSwitcherDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <AppSwitcher
      trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Switch application</Button>}
      homeHref="#"
      homeLabel="Home"
      apps={
        exampleIndex
          ? [{ id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: '#', icon: <Gauge /> }]
          : [
              { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: '#', icon: <Gauge /> },
              { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: '#', icon: <Camera /> },
              { id: 'trict', label: 'Trict', href: '#', icon: <LineChart />, current: true },
            ]
      }
    />
  )
}
```

### Single application

A member with one entitled application still gets the explicit Home destination.

```jsx
import { AppSwitcher, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Camera, Gauge, LineChart } from 'lucide-react'

export function AppSwitcherDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <AppSwitcher
      trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Switch application</Button>}
      homeHref="#"
      homeLabel="Home"
      apps={
        exampleIndex
          ? [{ id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: '#', icon: <Gauge /> }]
          : [
              { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: '#', icon: <Gauge /> },
              { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: '#', icon: <Camera /> },
              { id: 'trict', label: 'Trict', href: '#', icon: <LineChart />, current: true },
            ]
      }
    />
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Trigger** - The caller-supplied element, usually a Button, that opens the switcher menu.
- **Home destination** - The explicit Home link rendered first; homeCurrent marks it with aria-current.
- **Separator** - A divider shown only when at least one entitled application follows Home.
- **Application items** - Entitlement-filtered links with optional icons; the current application sets aria-current="page".

## Do and don't

### Do

- Filter apps by entitlement before passing them in; the switcher renders only what it receives.
- Always provide homeHref and homeLabel so people can return to the stable Home destination.
- Mark the application in use with current so it is announced as the current page.

### Don't

- Don't use it for navigation within one application; use Sidebar or Tabs instead.
- Don't hide the current application from the list; show it marked current instead.
- Don't put actions in the menu; every item navigates to a product destination.

## Interface

### AppSwitcher

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `enum` | `end` | Horizontal alignment of the switcher relative to the trigger. |
| `apps` (required) | `AppSwitcherItem[]` | - | Applications to show. The caller filters by entitlement first; the switcher renders only what it is given. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `homeCurrent` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the Home destination as the application the person is currently using. |
| `homeHref` (required) | `string` | - | URL of the explicit Home destination. |
| `homeLabel` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Visible label of the Home destination. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Accessible name for the switcher menu. |
| `onNavigate` | `(id: string) => void` | - | Called with the application id, or 'home', when a destination is selected. |
| `trigger` (required) | `ReactElement<unknown, string \| JSXElementConstructor<any>>` | - | Element that opens the switcher; receives trigger props automatically. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` + `Space` + `Arrow Down` | Opens the switcher menu from the trigger. |
| `Arrow Up` + `Arrow Down` | Moves the highlight between Home and the application items. |
| `Enter` | Follows the highlighted destination link. |
| `Escape` | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger. |

- Implements the dropdown menu pattern through the Radix primitive; the menu is named through the label prop.
- Home is always the first item; the current destination sets aria-current="page".
- Items are real anchor links, so open-in-new-tab and status-bar previews work.

## Related modules

- [Ecosystem Rail](/modules/ecosystem-rail)
- [Launcher Card](/modules/launcher-card)
- [Menu](/modules/menu)

# Account Menu

A household account menu with an identity header, product items, and distinct app and SSO sign-out actions.

## Usage

```js
import { AccountMenu } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<AccountMenu
  user={{ name: 'Avery Chen', email: 'avery@example.com' }}
  items={[{ id: 'sessions', label: 'Active sessions', onSelect: () => undefined }]}
  appSignOut={{ label: 'Sign out of Photos', onSelect: () => undefined }}
  ssoSignOut={{ label: 'Sign out everywhere', onSelect: () => undefined }}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A signed-in household identity needs session and account actions.
### Avoid when

The surface has no identity concept or is public.
### Behavior

App-session and SSO sign-out stay distinct actions with product-supplied labels.
### Responsive

The trigger stays a compact avatar so it fits top bars at any width.

## Examples

### Household account

Sign-out actions are labeled by the product so people can tell an application session from the shared SSO session.

```jsx
import { AccountMenu } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Clock } from 'lucide-react'

export function AccountMenuDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <AccountMenu
      user={{ name: 'Avery Chen', email: 'avery@kryvlabs.example' }}
      items={
        exampleIndex
          ? []
          : [{ id: 'sessions', label: 'Active sessions', icon: <Clock />, onSelect: () => undefined }]
      }
      appSignOut={{ label: 'Sign out of Photos', onSelect: () => undefined }}
      ssoSignOut={{ label: 'Sign out everywhere', onSelect: () => undefined }}
    />
  )
}
```

### Without product items

The items list is optional; the identity header and sign-out actions remain.

```jsx
import { AccountMenu } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Clock } from 'lucide-react'

export function AccountMenuDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  return (
    <AccountMenu
      user={{ name: 'Avery Chen', email: 'avery@kryvlabs.example' }}
      items={
        exampleIndex
          ? []
          : [{ id: 'sessions', label: 'Active sessions', icon: <Clock />, onSelect: () => undefined }]
      }
      appSignOut={{ label: 'Sign out of Photos', onSelect: () => undefined }}
      ssoSignOut={{ label: 'Sign out everywhere', onSelect: () => undefined }}
    />
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Trigger** - Compact avatar button named after the signed-in user.
- **Identity header** - Name and email block that anchors the menu to an account.
- **Product items** - Caller-defined account actions such as active sessions or settings.
- **Sign-out actions** - Distinct app-session and SSO sign-out items with product-supplied labels.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Label both sign-out actions by product so sessions stay distinguishable.
- Keep the identity header even when there are no product items.
- Order neutral account items before the sign-out actions.

### Don't

- Don't merge app and SSO sign-out into one ambiguous action.
- Don't show the menu on public surfaces with no signed-in identity.
- Don't bury primary navigation here; it is for account and session actions.

## Interface

### AccountMenu

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `align` | `enum` | `end` | Horizontal alignment of the menu relative to the trigger. |
| `appSignOut` | `AccountMenuAction` | - | Sign-out that ends only the current application session. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `items` | `MenuItem[]` | `[]` | Additional product-supplied items rendered above the sign-out actions. |
| `label` | `string` | - | Accessible name for the menu. |
| `ssoSignOut` | `AccountMenuAction` | - | Sign-out that ends the shared single-sign-on session. |
| `user` (required) | `AccountMenuUser` | - | Signed-in household identity shown in the trigger and menu header. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` + `Space` + `Arrow Down` | Opens the account menu from the avatar trigger. |
| `Arrow Up` + `Arrow Down` | Moves the highlight through the items and sign-out actions. |
| `Enter` | Activates the highlighted item. |
| `Escape` | Closes the menu and returns focus to the avatar trigger. |

- Implements the dropdown menu pattern through the Radix primitive; the trigger is named after the signed-in user.
- App-session and SSO sign-out are distinct items with product-supplied labels, so the scope of each is announced.
- The identity header is presentational text inside the menu, not an actionable item.

## Related modules

- [App Switcher](/modules/app-switcher)
- [Menu](/modules/menu)
- [Top Bar](/modules/top-bar)

# Tabs

Keyboard-navigable content switching through a compact item interface.

## Usage

```js
import { Tabs } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Tabs
  aria-label="Account sections"
  defaultValue="profile"
  items={[
    { value: 'profile', label: 'Profile', content: <ProfilePanel /> },
    { value: 'billing', label: 'Billing', content: <BillingPanel /> },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Related views share a context and users switch between them.
### Avoid when

Views need independent URLs or a long sequence of steps.
### Behavior

Arrow keys move between tabs and the active panel is announced.
### Responsive

Allow tab labels to scroll rather than wrap into ambiguous rows.

## Examples

### Sections

Tabs follow the ARIA authoring practices keyboard pattern out of the box.

```jsx
import { Tabs } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TabsDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xl">
        <Tabs
          aria-label="Profile sections"
          defaultValue="general"
          items={[
            { value: 'general', label: 'General', content: <p className="text-sm">Name, handle, and avatar for this profile</p> },
            { value: 'security', label: 'Security', content: <p className="text-sm">Sign-in and verification settings</p> },
            { value: 'notifications', label: 'Notifications', content: <p className="text-sm">Delivery preferences for this profile</p> },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xl">
      <Tabs
        aria-label="Project details"
        defaultValue="overview"
        items={[
          { value: 'overview', label: 'Overview', content: <p className="text-sm">Project overview content</p> },
          { value: 'activity', label: 'Activity', content: <p className="text-sm">Recent project activity</p> },
          { value: 'access', label: 'Access', content: <p className="text-sm">Workspace access settings</p> },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Profile sections

Use tabs for peer views that share the same route context.

```jsx
import { Tabs } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TabsDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full max-w-xl">
        <Tabs
          aria-label="Profile sections"
          defaultValue="general"
          items={[
            { value: 'general', label: 'General', content: <p className="text-sm">Name, handle, and avatar for this profile</p> },
            { value: 'security', label: 'Security', content: <p className="text-sm">Sign-in and verification settings</p> },
            { value: 'notifications', label: 'Notifications', content: <p className="text-sm">Delivery preferences for this profile</p> },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xl">
      <Tabs
        aria-label="Project details"
        defaultValue="overview"
        items={[
          { value: 'overview', label: 'Overview', content: <p className="text-sm">Project overview content</p> },
          { value: 'activity', label: 'Activity', content: <p className="text-sm">Recent project activity</p> },
          { value: 'access', label: 'Access', content: <p className="text-sm">Workspace access settings</p> },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Responsive tab list

Long tab labels remain reachable through horizontal scrolling.

```jsx
import { Tabs } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TabsResponsiveDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xl">
      <Tabs
        aria-label="Report sections"
        defaultValue="summary"
        items={[
          { value: 'summary', label: 'Executive summary', content: <p className="text-sm">A concise summary stays visible first.</p> },
          { value: 'evidence', label: 'Evidence and activity', content: <p className="text-sm">Detailed evidence is available without changing route context.</p> },
          { value: 'access', label: 'Access policy', content: <p className="text-sm">Permissions remain a peer view of this report.</p> },
          { value: 'trends', label: 'Quarterly performance trends', content: <p className="text-sm">Long labels stay reachable by scrolling the tab list.</p> },
          { value: 'retention', label: 'Retention and audit history', content: <p className="text-sm">Historical entries sit at the end of the scrollable list.</p> },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Tab list** - The tablist row that owns arrow-key movement between tabs.
- **Tab** - Each trigger; the selected one sets aria-selected and drives the visible panel.
- **Tab panel** - The content region labelled by its tab, shown one at a time.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Keep tab labels to one or two words.
- Set defaultValue so a sensible panel is visible on first render.
- Control selection with value and onValueChange when a route or parent owns it.

### Don't

- Don't use tabs to navigate between routes; use Sub Nav so links stay links.
- Don't nest a tab list inside another tab panel.
- Don't use tabs for a sequential flow; use Steps.

## Interface

### Tabs

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` (required) | `string` | - | Accessible name for the tab list. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional classes merged onto the tabs root. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | - | Initially active tab when uncontrolled. |
| `items` (required) | `TabItem[]` | - | Tabs rendered by the component. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Called with the new value when the active tab changes. |
| `value` | `string` | - | Controlled active tab value. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Arrow Left` + `Arrow Right` | Moves between tabs and activates them. |
| `Home` + `End` | Activates the first or last tab. |
| `Tab` | Moves focus from the active tab into its panel. |

- Implements the ARIA tabs pattern with tablist, tab, and tabpanel roles.
- aria-label on the tab list describes what the tabs switch between.
- Disabled tabs are skipped during arrow-key navigation.

## Related modules

- [Sub Nav](/modules/sub-nav)
- [Toggle Group](/modules/toggle-group)
- [Accordion](/modules/accordion)

# Pagination

A controlled page navigator with compact ranges and unavailable directions.

## Usage

```js
import { Pagination } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(1)

<Pagination page={page} pageCount={12} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A large collection is split into stable pages.
### Avoid when

Users need continuous search, sorting, or infinite history.
### Behavior

The page is controlled by the consumer and unavailable directions are disabled.
### Responsive

Keep controls large enough for touch and preserve the current page label.

## Examples

### Controlled pages

Pagination is fully controlled through page and onPageChange.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Pagination } from '@kryv/teal'

export function PaginationDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(3)
  const [boundaryPage, setBoundaryPage] = useState(1)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Pagination
        label="Audit log pages"
        page={boundaryPage}
        pageCount={8}
        onPageChange={setBoundaryPage}
      />
    )
  }

  return <Pagination page={page} pageCount={8} onPageChange={setPage} />
}
```

### Boundary pages

Disable previous and next controls at the collection boundaries.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Pagination } from '@kryv/teal'

export function PaginationDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(3)
  const [boundaryPage, setBoundaryPage] = useState(1)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Pagination
        label="Audit log pages"
        page={boundaryPage}
        pageCount={8}
        onPageChange={setBoundaryPage}
      />
    )
  }

  return <Pagination page={page} pageCount={8} onPageChange={setPage} />
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Previous and next** - Directional controls that disable at the first and last page.
- **Page buttons** - Numbered pages; the current one sets aria-current="page".
- **Ellipsis** - Collapsed ranges that keep long page counts compact.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Drive it from state with page and onPageChange; it is fully controlled.
- Pair it with a result count so the page numbers have context.
- Reset to page one when filters or sorting change.

### Don't

- Don't use it for a linear wizard; use Steps.
- Don't paginate content that streams better with infinite scroll.
- Don't render it for a single page of results.

## Interface

### Pagination

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional classes merged onto the nav element. |
| `label` | `string` | `Pagination` | Accessible name for the navigation landmark. |
| `onPageChange` (required) | `(page: number) => void` | - | Called with the next page when the user navigates. |
| `page` (required) | `number` | - | Current page, one-based. |
| `pageCount` (required) | `number` | - | Total number of pages. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus through the page controls. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Activates the focused page control. |

- Renders a nav element with an accessible label.
- The current page is marked with aria-current="page".
- Unavailable directions render as disabled buttons rather than being hidden.

## Related modules

- [Table](/modules/table)
- [Steps](/modules/steps)

# Page Header

A responsive page title, supporting text, and action area.

## Usage

```js
import { PageHeader, Button } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<PageHeader
  title="Workspace settings"
  subtitle="Manage security and notifications"
  actions={<Button>Save changes</Button>}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A route needs a consistent title, context, and primary actions.
### Avoid when

The content is a small inline section without route-level actions.
### Behavior

Actions remain aligned with the title and wrap below it when needed.
### Responsive

Let actions wrap naturally below the heading at narrow widths.

## Examples

### Settings header

Actions wrap below the title on narrow screens automatically.

```jsx
import { Button, PageHeader } from '@kryv/teal'

export function PageHeaderDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full">
        <PageHeader
          title="Usage and billing"
          subtitle="Seat counts, invoices, and plan limits for the whole workspace"
          actions={
            <>
              <Button variant="secondary">Download invoice</Button>
              <Button>Upgrade plan</Button>
            </>
          }
        />
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <div className="w-full">
      <PageHeader
        title="Workspace settings"
        subtitle="Manage security and notifications"
        actions={<Button>Save changes</Button>}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Responsive actions

Let actions wrap beneath the title on narrow screens.

```jsx
import { Button, PageHeader } from '@kryv/teal'

export function PageHeaderDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full">
        <PageHeader
          title="Usage and billing"
          subtitle="Seat counts, invoices, and plan limits for the whole workspace"
          actions={
            <>
              <Button variant="secondary">Download invoice</Button>
              <Button>Upgrade plan</Button>
            </>
          }
        />
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <div className="w-full">
      <PageHeader
        title="Workspace settings"
        subtitle="Manage security and notifications"
        actions={<Button>Save changes</Button>}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Title** - Page heading rendered as h1 by default; adjust with titleAs to fit the page outline.
- **Subtitle** - Supporting text rendered under the title.
- **Actions** - Trailing action area that wraps below the title on narrow screens.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Keep one primary action in the actions slot; demote the rest.
- Set titleAs so the heading level fits the page outline.
- Pair with Breadcrumb above when the page sits deep in a hierarchy.

### Don't

- Don't repeat the global Top Bar actions here; keep them page-level.
- Don't stack multiple page headers on one route.

## Interface

### PageHeader

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | - | Actions rendered beside the title; wraps below on narrow screens. |
| `subtitle` | `ReactNode` | - | Supporting text rendered under the title. |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Page title rendered as a heading. |
| `titleAs` | `enum` | `"h1"` | Heading element used for the title; defaults to 'h1'. Adjust to fit the page outline. |

## Accessibility

- The title renders as an h1 by default; set titleAs to fit the page outline and keep one h1 per page.
- Actions are regular buttons and links with standard focus order.

## Related modules

- [Breadcrumb](/modules/breadcrumb)
- [Top Bar](/modules/top-bar)
- [Sub Nav](/modules/sub-nav)

# Nav Rail

A fully rounded floating icon rail for dense product navigation.

## Usage

```js
import { NavRail, NavRailItem } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<NavRail aria-label="Primary">
  <NavRailItem icon={<Home />} label="Home" href="/" active />
  <NavRailItem icon={<Search />} label="Search" href="/search" />
  <NavRailItem icon={<Settings />} label="Settings" href="/settings" />
</NavRail>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A dense product needs a compact, always-visible strip of top-level destinations.
### Avoid when

Destinations need visible labels or grouped sections; use Sidebar.
### Behavior

The active item sets aria-current and every icon is named through aria-label and a tooltip.
### Responsive

Keep the rail floating on desktop and fold destinations into a drawer on narrow screens.

## Examples

### Icon destinations

Circular items tint the active destination; every icon carries an accessible label and a tooltip.

```jsx
import { NavRail, NavRailItem } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Bell, Home, Search, Settings } from 'lucide-react'

export function NavRailDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <NavRail aria-label="Primary">
        <NavRailItem icon={<Home />} label="Home" href="#" active />
        <NavRailItem icon={<Search />} label="Search" href="#" />
        <NavRailItem icon={<Bell />} label="Notifications" href="#" badge />
        <NavRailItem icon={<Settings />} label="Settings" href="#" badge />
      </NavRail>
    )
  }

  return (
    <NavRail aria-label="Primary">
      <NavRailItem icon={<Home />} label="Home" href="#" active />
      <NavRailItem icon={<Search />} label="Search" href="#" />
      <NavRailItem icon={<Bell />} label="Notifications" href="#" />
      <NavRailItem icon={<Settings />} label="Settings" href="#" />
    </NavRail>
  )
}
```

### Badge dots

Pass badge to flag a destination that needs attention without carrying a count.

```jsx
import { NavRail, NavRailItem } from '@kryv/teal'
import { Bell, Home, Search, Settings } from 'lucide-react'

export function NavRailDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <NavRail aria-label="Primary">
        <NavRailItem icon={<Home />} label="Home" href="#" active />
        <NavRailItem icon={<Search />} label="Search" href="#" />
        <NavRailItem icon={<Bell />} label="Notifications" href="#" badge />
        <NavRailItem icon={<Settings />} label="Settings" href="#" badge />
      </NavRail>
    )
  }

  return (
    <NavRail aria-label="Primary">
      <NavRailItem icon={<Home />} label="Home" href="#" active />
      <NavRailItem icon={<Search />} label="Search" href="#" />
      <NavRailItem icon={<Bell />} label="Notifications" href="#" />
      <NavRailItem icon={<Settings />} label="Settings" href="#" />
    </NavRail>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Rail landmark** - The rounded floating nav container named through aria-label, defaulting to "Primary".
- **Items** - Circular icon links or buttons; each requires a label applied as aria-label and mirrored in a tooltip.
- **Badge dot** - An attention dot in the item corner, flagged with badge and hidden from assistive technology.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Give every item a short label; it is the accessible name and the tooltip text.
- Render items as links with href for real destinations so open-in-new-tab works.
- Use badge sparingly to flag a destination that needs attention without carrying a count.

### Don't

- Don't use it when destinations need visible labels or grouped sections; use Sidebar.
- Don't crowd in more than a handful of destinations; the rail is for top-level navigation only.
- Don't rely on the badge dot alone to convey meaning; pair it with a notification surface.

## Interface

### NavRail

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `Primary` | Accessible name for the rail landmark. |

### NavRailItem

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the item as the current page; sets `aria-current="page"`. |
| `badge` | `boolean` | `false` | Renders a small attention dot in the corner of the item. |
| `href` | `string` | - | Destination URL; renders a link instead of a button when provided. |
| `icon` (required) | `ReactNode` | - | Icon rendered inside the circular item. |
| `label` (required) | `string` | - | Accessible name for the item; also shown in a tooltip on hover or focus. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus between the circular items. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Follows the link or activates the button item. |

- Renders a nav landmark named through aria-label, defaulting to "Primary".
- Every item requires a label, applied as aria-label and mirrored in a tooltip on hover or focus.
- The active item sets aria-current="page"; the badge dot is aria-hidden, so pair it with a labeled notification surface.

## Related modules

- [Sidebar](/modules/sidebar)
- [Ecosystem Rail](/modules/ecosystem-rail)
- [Tooltip](/modules/tooltip)

# Ecosystem Rail

A persistent cross-product rail with a stable Home destination, caller-filtered applications, and honest health status.

## Usage

```js
import { EcosystemRail, SidebarItem } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<EcosystemRail
  home={{ href: '#', label: 'Home', icon: <Home /> }}
  destinations={[
    { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: '#', icon: <Gauge />, current: true },
    { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: '#', icon: <Camera />, status: 'degraded' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A product needs persistent navigation across the whole ecosystem, not just its own sections.
### Avoid when

The navigation is inside one application; use Sidebar. For a temporary switcher menu, use App Switcher.
### Behavior

Home always renders first, the caller filters destinations by entitlement, health status appears only when supplied, and onNavigate fires before ordinary anchor navigation.
### Responsive

Rail mode collapses to icons until hover or focus; fold the rail into a drawer on narrow screens.

## Examples

### Rail mode with health status

The default icon rail expands on hover or focus; destinations carry an honest HealthIndicator status only when evidence exists.

```jsx
import { Camera, Gauge, Home, LayoutDashboard, LineChart, Settings } from 'lucide-react'
import { EcosystemRail, SidebarItem } from '@kryv/teal'

export function EcosystemRailDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="relative h-80 w-72 overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-teal-outline-variant/30">
        <EcosystemRail
          className="absolute"
          mode="full"
          home={{
            href: '#',
            label: 'Home',
            icon: <Home className="size-5" />,
            current: true,
          }}
          destinations={[
            { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: '#', icon: <Gauge className="size-5" /> },
            { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: '#', icon: <Camera className="size-5" />, status: 'degraded' },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="relative h-80 w-72 overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-teal-outline-variant/30">
      <EcosystemRail
        className="absolute"
        brand={
          <span className="flex w-16 items-center justify-center">
            <span className="flex size-9 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-teal-primary text-teal-on-primary">
              <LayoutDashboard className="size-5" />
            </span>
          </span>
        }
        home={{ href: '#', label: 'Home', icon: <Home className="size-5" /> }}
        destinations={[
          { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: '#', icon: <Gauge className="size-5" />, current: true, status: 'healthy' },
          { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: '#', icon: <Camera className="size-5" /> },
          { id: 'trict', label: 'Trict', href: '#', icon: <LineChart className="size-5" />, status: 'stale' },
        ]}
        footer={<SidebarItem icon={<Settings className="size-5" />}>Account</SidebarItem>}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Full mode with a degraded destination

mode="full" keeps labels visible; Home is marked current and the degraded Photos status stays readable beside its label.

```jsx
import { Camera, Gauge, Home, LayoutDashboard, LineChart, Settings } from 'lucide-react'
import { EcosystemRail, SidebarItem } from '@kryv/teal'

export function EcosystemRailDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="relative h-80 w-72 overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-teal-outline-variant/30">
        <EcosystemRail
          className="absolute"
          mode="full"
          home={{
            href: '#',
            label: 'Home',
            icon: <Home className="size-5" />,
            current: true,
          }}
          destinations={[
            { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: '#', icon: <Gauge className="size-5" /> },
            { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: '#', icon: <Camera className="size-5" />, status: 'degraded' },
          ]}
        />
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="relative h-80 w-72 overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-teal-outline-variant/30">
      <EcosystemRail
        className="absolute"
        brand={
          <span className="flex w-16 items-center justify-center">
            <span className="flex size-9 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-teal-primary text-teal-on-primary">
              <LayoutDashboard className="size-5" />
            </span>
          </span>
        }
        home={{ href: '#', label: 'Home', icon: <Home className="size-5" /> }}
        destinations={[
          { id: 'yang', label: 'Yang Operations', href: '#', icon: <Gauge className="size-5" />, current: true, status: 'healthy' },
          { id: 'photos', label: 'Photos', href: '#', icon: <Camera className="size-5" /> },
          { id: 'trict', label: 'Trict', href: '#', icon: <LineChart className="size-5" />, status: 'stale' },
        ]}
        footer={<SidebarItem icon={<Settings className="size-5" />}>Account</SidebarItem>}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Brand** - Optional product-family mark rendered above the list, supplied through the brand prop.
- **Home destination** - The stable Home link, always rendered first; pass current when Home is the active product.
- **Destinations** - Caller-filtered application links with icons; an optional HealthIndicator shows an honest status beside each label.
- **Footer** - Optional account or session controls pinned to the bottom of the rail.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Filter destinations by entitlement before passing them in; the rail renders exactly what it is given.
- Mark the product the person is currently using with current so the item sets aria-current.
- Pass status only with real evidence; omit it or use unknown when health is not measured.

### Don't

- Don't use it for navigation inside one application; use Sidebar instead.
- Don't derive or hide entitlements inside the rail; it never filters destinations itself.
- Don't reorder Home into the destination list; it is always rendered first by design.

## Interface

### EcosystemRail

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | `Kryv ecosystem` | Accessible name for the product navigation. |
| `brand` | `ReactNode` | - | Optional product-family brand content. |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `destinations` (required) | `EcosystemRailDestination[]` | - | Caller-filtered destinations. The rail never derives entitlements. |
| `home` (required) | `EcosystemRailHome` | - | Stable Home destination, always rendered first. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | - | Optional account or session controls pinned to the bottom. |
| `mode` | `enum` | `rail` | Rail collapses labels until hover or focus; full keeps labels visible. |
| `onNavigate` | `(id: string) => void` | - | Called before ordinary anchor navigation. |
| `side` | `enum` | `left` | Edge where the rail is attached. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus between destinations. In rail mode, focusing an item expands the rail to reveal labels. |
| `Enter` | Follows the focused destination link. |

- Renders a nav landmark named through the ariaLabel prop, defaulting to "Kryv ecosystem".
- Home is always the first item; the current destination sets aria-current="page".
- Pass ariaLabel on a destination whose visible label is not a plain string so the collapsed rail keeps an accessible name.
- Destination health renders a text badge through HealthIndicator, so the status is announced as text rather than color alone.

## Related modules

- [App Switcher](/modules/app-switcher)
- [Sidebar](/modules/sidebar)
- [Health Indicator](/modules/health-indicator)

# Top Bar

A sticky top bar with brand, search, and action slots.

## Usage

```js
import { TopBar, TopBarBrand, TopBarSearch, TopBarActions } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<TopBar sticky>
  <TopBarBrand>...</TopBarBrand>
  <TopBarSearch>...</TopBarSearch>
  <TopBarActions>...</TopBarActions>
</TopBar>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

An application needs a consistent global header and action slots.
### Avoid when

A page has only local controls that belong in its header.
### Behavior

Sticky mode keeps the bar visible while its slots remain composable.
### Responsive

Collapse secondary actions and move search to a dedicated mobile trigger.

## Examples

### Brand, search, and actions

Slots compose into full and compact headers; sticky keeps the bar visible while scrolling.

```jsx
import { Bell, CircleUserRound, Gauge, Palette, Search, Sun } from 'lucide-react'
import { GitHubIcon } from '../components/GitHubIcon.jsx'
import { IconButton, TopBar, TopBarActions, TopBarBrand, TopBarSearch } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TopBarDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <div className="w-full rounded-xl border border-teal-outline-variant/30">
        <TopBar sticky={false} className="px-4">
          <TopBarBrand>
            <span className="flex size-8 items-center justify-center rounded-xl bg-teal-primary text-teal-on-primary">
              <Gauge className="size-4" />
            </span>
            <span className="font-teal-headline font-extrabold">Acme Console</span>
          </TopBarBrand>
          <TopBarSearch>
            <button
              type="button"
              className="flex h-10 w-full max-w-md items-center gap-2 rounded-xl border border-teal-outline-variant/40 bg-teal-surface px-3 text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant"
            >
              <Search className="size-4" />
              Search projects, people, and settings...
            </button>
          </TopBarSearch>
          <TopBarActions>
            <IconButton label="Show notifications">
              <Bell />
            </IconButton>
            <IconButton label="Account menu">
              <CircleUserRound />
            </IconButton>
          </TopBarActions>
        </TopBar>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="w-full space-y-4">
      <TopBar sticky={false}>
        <TopBarBrand>
          <span className="flex size-8 items-center justify-center rounded-xl bg-teal-primary text-teal-on-primary">
            <Palette className="size-4" />
          </span>
          <span className="font-teal-headline font-extrabold">Teal</span>
        </TopBarBrand>
        <TopBarSearch>
          <button
            type="button"
            className="flex h-10 w-full max-w-sm items-center gap-2 rounded-xl border border-teal-outline-variant/40 bg-teal-surface px-3 text-sm text-teal-on-surface-variant"
          >
            <Search className="size-4" />
            Search the docs...
          </button>
        </TopBarSearch>
        <TopBarActions>
          <IconButton label="GitHub">
            <GitHubIcon />
          </IconButton>
          <IconButton label="Switch theme">
            <Sun />
          </IconButton>
        </TopBarActions>
      </TopBar>

      <TopBar sticky={false} className="rounded-xl">
        <TopBarBrand>
          <span className="flex size-8 items-center justify-center rounded-xl bg-teal-primary text-teal-on-primary">
            <Palette className="size-4" />
          </span>
          <span className="font-teal-headline font-extrabold">Teal</span>
        </TopBarBrand>
        <TopBarActions>
          <IconButton label="View on GitHub">
            <GitHubIcon />
          </IconButton>
          <IconButton label="Toggle dark mode">
            <Sun />
          </IconButton>
        </TopBarActions>
      </TopBar>
    </div>
  )
}
```

```jsx
            <GitHubIcon />
          </IconButton>
          <IconButton label="Toggle dark mode">
            <Sun />
          </IconButton>
        </TopBarActions>
      </TopBar>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Compact shell

Use the same slots for a focused route header with fewer global actions.

```jsx
import { Bell, Palette, Search } from 'lucide-react'
import { IconButton, TopBar, TopBarActions, TopBarBrand, TopBarSearch } from '@kryv/teal'

export function TopBarShellDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full rounded-xl border border-teal-outline-variant/30">
      <TopBar sticky={false} className="px-4">
        <TopBarBrand>
          <span className="flex size-8 items-center justify-center rounded-xl bg-teal-primary text-teal-on-primary"><Palette className="size-4" /></span>
          <span className="font-teal-headline font-bold">Project Orion</span>
        </TopBarBrand>
        <TopBarSearch>
          <button type="button" className="flex h-9 w-full max-w-xs items-center gap-2 rounded-lg border border-teal-outline-variant/40 px-3 text-xs text-teal-on-surface-variant"><Search className="size-4" />Search workspace</button>
        </TopBarSearch>
        <TopBarActions><IconButton label="Notifications" size="sm"><Bell /></IconButton></TopBarActions>
      </TopBar>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Bar** - The sticky container that keeps its slots visible while scrolling.
- **Brand** - TopBarBrand slot for product identity on the leading edge.
- **Search** - TopBarSearch slot for global search in the middle.
- **Actions** - TopBarActions slot for trailing controls such as the account menu.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Use sticky for apps where global actions must stay reachable while scrolling.
- Collapse secondary actions into a menu on narrow screens.

### Don't

- Don't put page-level actions here; they belong in Page Header.
- Don't stack multiple top bars; compose the slots into one.

## Interface

### TopBar

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sticky` | `boolean` | `true` | When true, the bar sticks to the top of the scrolling container. |
| `as` | `ElementType` | `header` | - |

### TopBarBrand

_This module forwards native element properties._

### TopBarSearch

_This module forwards native element properties._

### TopBarActions

_This module forwards native element properties._

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus through the brand, search trigger, and action buttons in order. |

- Renders a <header> element by default; use the as prop to change the element if needed.
- Keep action buttons labeled with aria-label when they contain only icons.
- Sticky keeps the bar in view during scrolling; use sticky={false} for an inline bar.

- [Page Header](/modules/page-header)
- [App Switcher](/modules/app-switcher)
- [Account Menu](/modules/account-menu)

# Breadcrumb

A hierarchical trail with router-ready items and automatic middle-item collapse.

## Usage

```js
import { Breadcrumb } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Breadcrumb
  items={[
    { label: 'Workspace', href: '/' },
    { label: 'Projects', href: '/projects' },
    { label: 'Orion' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

Users need to see and move within a deep page hierarchy.
### Avoid when

The structure is flat or the trail would duplicate primary navigation.
### Behavior

The last item is the current page; middle items collapse into a menu past collapseAfter.
### Responsive

Let items wrap and prefer collapsing over shrinking labels.

## Examples

### Hierarchy

Items render in order; the last item is the current page.

```jsx
import { Breadcrumb } from '@kryv/teal'

export function BreadcrumbDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Breadcrumb
        collapseAfter={3}
        items={[
          { label: 'Workspace', href: '#' },
          { label: 'Projects', href: '#' },
          { label: 'Orion', href: '#' },
          { label: 'Reports', href: '#' },
          { label: 'Quarterly review' },
        ]}
      />
    )
  }
  return (
    <Breadcrumb
      items={[
        { label: 'Workspace', href: '#' },
        { label: 'Projects', href: '#' },
        { label: 'Orion' },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

### Collapsed middle items

Trails longer than collapseAfter move middle items into a labeled menu.

```jsx
import { Breadcrumb } from '@kryv/teal'

export function BreadcrumbDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Breadcrumb
        collapseAfter={3}
        items={[
          { label: 'Workspace', href: '#' },
          { label: 'Projects', href: '#' },
          { label: 'Orion', href: '#' },
          { label: 'Reports', href: '#' },
          { label: 'Quarterly review' },
        ]}
      />
    )
  }
  return (
    <Breadcrumb
      items={[
        { label: 'Workspace', href: '#' },
        { label: 'Projects', href: '#' },
        { label: 'Orion' },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Trail** - Nav landmark rendering the items in order as links.
- **Separators** - Chevron icons between items, hidden from assistive technology.
- **Current page** - The last item, rendered as text with aria-current="page".
- **Collapse menu** - Middle items fold into an overflow menu past collapseAfter.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Keep the last item as plain text; it is the current page, not a link.
- Prefer collapsing middle items over truncating labels on narrow screens.

### Don't

- Don't use breadcrumbs on flat structures or as a back button.
- Don't duplicate the primary navigation in the trail.

## Interface

### Breadcrumb

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | - | - |
| `collapseAfter` | `number` | `5` | Maximum items shown before middle items collapse into a menu. |
| `items` (required) | `BreadcrumbItem[]` | - | Items in hierarchy order ({ label, href?, as?, onSelect? }); the last item is the current page. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Breadcrumb"` | Accessible name for the navigation landmark. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus through the trail links and the collapsed-items menu trigger. |

- Renders a nav landmark with an ordered list; the landmark label defaults to "Breadcrumb".
- The current page is a span with aria-current="page", not a link.
- Middle items beyond collapseAfter move into a labeled menu.
- Pass a router link component through an item's as prop, mirroring SidebarItem.

## Related modules

- [Page Header](/modules/page-header)
- [Sub Nav](/modules/sub-nav)
- [Anchor Nav](/modules/anchor-nav)

# Steps

A numbered flow indicator with done, current, and upcoming states.

## Usage

```js
import { Steps } from '@kryv/teal'
```

```jsx
<Steps
  current={1}
  steps={[
    { label: 'Workspace' },
    { label: 'Members' },
    { label: 'Review' },
  ]}
/>
```

## Design guidance

### Use when

A flow has a clear sequence and the user benefits from seeing progress.
### Avoid when

Steps are independent views; use Tabs or navigation.
### Behavior

The current step sets aria-current and completed steps can be made clickable.
### Responsive

Steps wrap with their labels on narrow screens; keep labels short.

## Examples

### Flow progress

Completed steps can be clickable; the current step sets aria-current.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Steps } from '@kryv/teal'

export function StepsDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [current, setCurrent] = useState(1)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Steps
        className="w-full max-w-2xl"
        current={current}
        onStepClick={setCurrent}
        steps={[
          { label: 'Account', description: 'Basic details' },
          { label: 'Workspace', description: 'Name and region' },
          { label: 'Members', description: 'Invite your team' },
          { label: 'Review', description: 'Confirm and finish' },
        ]}
      />
    )
  }

  return (
    <Steps
      className="w-full max-w-xl"
      current={2}
      steps={[{ label: 'Draft' }, { label: 'Review' }, { label: 'Approved' }, { label: 'Published' }]}
    />
  )
}
```

### Clickable completed steps

Allow returning to completed steps with onStepClick.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Steps } from '@kryv/teal'

export function StepsDemo({ exampleIndex = 0 }) {
  const [current, setCurrent] = useState(1)

  if (exampleIndex === 1) {
    return (
      <Steps
        className="w-full max-w-2xl"
        current={current}
        onStepClick={setCurrent}
        steps={[
          { label: 'Account', description: 'Basic details' },
          { label: 'Workspace', description: 'Name and region' },
          { label: 'Members', description: 'Invite your team' },
          { label: 'Review', description: 'Confirm and finish' },
        ]}
      />
    )
  }

  return (
    <Steps
      className="w-full max-w-xl"
      current={2}
      steps={[{ label: 'Draft' }, { label: 'Review' }, { label: 'Approved' }, { label: 'Published' }]}
    />
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

- **Markers** - Numbered circles that switch to a check once a step is done.
- **Labels** - Step names; the current step sets aria-current="step".
- **Connectors** - Lines between markers that fill as steps complete.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Provide onStepClick so people can return to completed steps.
- Keep step labels to short nouns.

### Don't

- Don't let people jump ahead; only completed steps become clickable.
- Don't use it as page navigation; it tracks one flow's progress.

## Interface

### Steps

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` (required) | `StepItem[]` | - | Steps to render, in order. |
| `current` (required) | `number` | - | Zero-based index of the current step. Earlier steps render as completed. |
| `onStepClick` | `(index: number) => void` | - | When provided, completed steps render as buttons and call this with their index. |

## Accessibility

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus between the clickable completed steps. |
| `Enter` + `Space` | Jumps back to the focused completed step. |

- Rendered as an ordered list, so each step's position and the total count are announced.
- The current step sets aria-current="step".
- Only completed steps become buttons when onStepClick is provided; upcoming steps stay inert.

## Related modules

- [Pagination](/modules/pagination)
- [Breadcrumb](/modules/breadcrumb)
- [Timeline](/modules/timeline)
